strategies.name: Box-vs-Treasury convenience-yield trade

legs.strike_rule: Funding leg: short the maturity-matched T-bill (via repo) with face K2 - K1; a short SOFR/bill future only hedges rate risk, it does not fund the box

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Box pays K2 - K1, the shorted bill repays K2 - K1: zero at T. The P&L is collected at inception: (K2 - K1)(e^{-r_bill T} - e^{-r_box T}) ~ (r_box - r_bill) T (K2 - K1). With a SOFR-future hedge instead of a bill short, the P&L is box carry minus your own cash opportunity cost, with rates hedged.
strategies.max_profit: (K2 - K1)(e^{-r_bill T} - e^{-r_box T}), locked if both legs are held to T.
strategies.max_loss: Negative if r_box < r_bill at entry; mark-to-market losses if the spread widens before T (it widened sharply in 2008 and March 2020).
strategies.breakevens: r_box = r_bill.

greeks_at_inception.vega: 0; rho ~0 net, exposed to the box-bill basis

strategies.when_to_use: Institutions that can short bills cheaply, when the box-bill spread is above its typical ~35 bp; for retail the practical version is simply holding long boxes instead of bills.
strategies.risks: Maturity basis; two venues of margin; the spread is a convenience yield that widens in stress when balance sheet is scarce; four-leg spread costs consume much of a ~35 bp edge below 6 months.
strategies.margin_note: Portfolio margin on the box (~0) plus repo/CME margin on the funding or hedge leg; cross-venue collateral.
strategies.crypto_notes: Analogue: Deribit inverse box rate (= futures basis) minus bills is a crypto dollar premium, not a convenience yield; the funding leg would be a bill short or USDC borrowing.
strategies.metals_notes: n/a (no European metals boxes).
variants: Box vs SOFR futures strip (rate-hedged carry)
Only maturities > 6 months to amortise spreads
Short box / long bill when r_box < r_bill
strategies.claim: Daily changes in the SPX box-minus-bill spread (60-120 DTE, mid prices) are positively correlated with daily changes in VIX, with correlation above 0.2.

trial.statistic: Pearson correlation of d(r_box - r_bill) with d(VIX), studentized block bootstrap CI.
trial.procedure: Build a daily SPX box-rate series from captured chains; join DGS3MO and VIX; block bootstrap (5-day blocks) of the correlation; report the mean spread separately.
trial.data: Daily SPX chain capture (none before 2026-10-14), FRED DGS3MO, CBOE VIX history.
trial.pass: Correlation > 0.2 with the 95% CI excluding 0.
trial.controls: Fixed strike-pair rule; exclude < 30 DTE; mid series for the statistic, executable for P&L; check robustness to dropping FOMC days.

strategies.blocked_on: daily SPX chain capture, ~120 trading days, to form a box-rate series (alternative: ingest published van Binsbergen-Diamond-Grotteria box-rate data)
strategies.harness_suggestion: box.py daily series -> mandel/experiments/box_bill_spread.py joining FRED + VIX; existing block bootstrap.

strategies.name: Butterfly convexity arbitrage (negative-priced butterfly)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Tent: 0 for S_T <= K1, S_T - K1 on [K1, K2], K3 - S_T on [K2, K3], 0 above K3; never negative. Static no-arbitrage requires price B = C(K1) - 2 C(K2) + C(K3) >= 0 (discounted risk-neutral density >= 0); an executable credit (B_exec < 0) is a riskless profit. Put butterflies obey the same condition.
strategies.max_profit: h - B (at S_T = K2); if B < 0 the minimum profit is -B.
strategies.max_loss: B (debit) when positive; zero when bought for a credit.
strategies.breakevens: K1 + B and K3 - B (for B > 0).

greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative near K2 for an ATM-centred long fly (positive if spot is outside the wings)

strategies.when_to_use: Scan every chain for executable negative butterflies (ask on wings, bid on the body): they appear in far wings, stale quotes and around strike-spacing changes; also the basis of density extraction (Breeden-Litzenberger) used by the event-contract entry.
strategies.risks: Delayed quotes create false positives; American early assignment of the short body (ITM calls before ex-div) breaks the static argument; spacing must be exactly equal (or use the general convexity condition with weights).
strategies.margin_note: Long butterfly is a paid debit (defined risk); a credit butterfly still has defined, non-negative payoff.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit: apply the convexity test to USD prices (C_btc x F); an inverse butterfly's BTC payoff is tent/S_T, still non-negative, so negative BTC prices are arbitrage too.
strategies.metals_notes: OG/SO and GLD/SLV chains: same test; American OG legs carry early-exercise caveats.
variants: Density non-negativity scan across all strikes
strategies.claim: On the CBOE delayed SPX and SPY chains, fewer than 0.5% of equally spaced call or put butterflies (adjacent listed strikes within +/- 20% of spot, all expiries) can be bought for a net credit at executable prices (ask on wings, bid on the body).

trial.statistic: Share of butterflies with B_exec < 0.
trial.procedure: Day one: enumerate butterflies from adjacent equally spaced strikes; compute B_exec and B_mid; count; bootstrap across expiries; repeat daily.
trial.data: CBOE delayed SPX and SPY chains (available).
trial.pass: Share < 0.5% with the 95% upper bound < 0.5% on day one and on >= 80% of captured days.
trial.controls: Mid-price share should be small but non-zero; drop legs with zero bid; separate wing strikes (> 10% OTM) from the core.

strategies.harness_suggestion: mandel/options/static_arb.py: butterfly_scan(chain) with executable and mid prices; payoff engine template [call+ K1, call-2 K2, call+ K3].

strategies.name: Calendar (time-value) arbitrage
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At T1: C(K, T2 at S_T1) - max(S_T1 - K, 0), maximal near S_T1 = K and non-negative for American options (the far option is worth at least intrinsic). Static no-arbitrage for American options (or European with no dividends and r >= 0): C(K, T2) >= C(K, T1); for European index options the correct condition is total implied variance non-decreasing in T at fixed forward-moneyness. An executable credit calendar in American options is riskless.
strategies.max_profit: Value of the T2 option at S_T1 = K minus the debit.
strategies.max_loss: Debit (zero or negative if bought for a credit in American options).
strategies.breakevens: Two S_T1 values around K where C(K, T2) - (S_T1 - K)^+ = debit (model-dependent).
strategies.when_to_use: Scan for far-dated options priced below near-dated ones at the same strike (stale far quotes, dividend-driven distortions in European roots); verify term-structure consistency before fitting volatility surfaces.
strategies.risks: European options with dividends can legitimately violate the naive price inequality (use the variance condition); early assignment on the short near leg; delayed quotes.
strategies.margin_note: Long calendar is a paid debit; Reg-T treats it as a spread if the long expires after the short.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit options are European on different futures per expiry: compare at fixed moneyness K/F_T using total variance from mark_iv, not raw BTC prices.
strategies.metals_notes: OG options on different GC months have different underlyings: use the variance condition at K/F_T.
variants: Calendar arbitrage on Deribit via mark_iv
strategies.claim: On the CBOE delayed SPY chain (American), fewer than 0.1% of same-strike call or put pairs at adjacent expiries can be bought as a calendar for a net credit at executable prices (far ask < near bid).

trial.statistic: Share of same-strike adjacent-expiry pairs with far_ask < near_bid.
trial.procedure: Day one: enumerate pairs; count executable credits; for SPX, compute total-variance violations at fixed forward-moneyness as a companion statistic; repeat daily.
trial.data: CBOE delayed SPY and SPX chains (available).
trial.pass: Share < 0.1% on day one and on >= 80% of captured days.
trial.controls: Exclude zero-bid near legs; separate deep ITM calls straddling ex-div (early-exercise value); Deribit total-variance scan as a crypto replication.

strategies.harness_suggestion: static_arb.py calendar_scan(chain) plus total_variance_check(surface).

strategies.name: Cash-and-carry with options (spot vs synthetic short / dated future)

legs.strike_rule: spot (BTC on venue, IBIT, GLD, or stock)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Flat at K: you sold the forward at F_impl = K + (C - P) e^{rT} and own spot, earning the basis F_impl - S0 e^{...}. Future version: replace the two options with a short dated future at F (for Deribit inverse futures, short USD notional F per BTC held, which locks F USD = F/S_T BTC).
strategies.max_profit: Locked basis: F_impl - S0 minus financing, storage and fees, if held to T.
strategies.max_loss: Negative basis at entry; mark-to-market and margin calls on the short leg if basis widens; custody/venue risk.
strategies.breakevens: F_impl = S0 e^{r_fund T} (basis equals your funding rate).
strategies.when_to_use: Crypto: annualised dated basis above the bill rate plus fees and a venue-risk premium (~5.3-5.6%/yr on Deribit BTC quarterlies on 2026-10-14). Metals: GC contango above financing plus storage (rare for retail). Equities: this is a conversion.
strategies.risks: Spot and short leg on different venues (cannot cross-margin); exchange failure; basis inversion; for inverse futures the hedge must be sized in USD notional F per BTC, not 1/F.
strategies.margin_note: Deribit: spot BTC on the venue collateralises the short future (hedged, low margin). IBIT + CME BTC futures: Reg-T and SPAN, no cross-margin.
strategies.crypto_notes: Long spot BTC on Deribit + short dated inverse future of USD notional F per BTC: final BTC = 1 + F (1/S_T - 1/F) = F/S_T BTC = F USD. No funding on dated futures; the perpetual version pays/receives funding (next entry). 08:00 UTC settlement.
strategies.metals_notes: GC cash-and-carry needs COMEX-registered metal; retail route is GLD long vs OG synthetic short, whose carry is the USD rate minus the GLD fee minus the gold lease rate; Section 1256 on OG/GC legs only.
variants: Reverse cash-and-carry when basis is negative
Spot + option synthetic short instead of future
strategies.claim: Across the daily history of expired and live Deribit BTC quarterly futures, the median annualised basis of the second-nearest quarterly over the index exceeds the same-day FRED 3-month bill by at least 100 bp.

trial.statistic: Median over days of [ln(F_q2 / S) x 365/DTE - r_bill]; block-bootstrap CI.
trial.procedure: Pull daily closes for every quarterly via get_tradingview_chart_data (works for expired instruments, e.g. BTC-27DEC24, verified); spot proxy = BTC daily close (or BTC-PERPETUAL close at the same tick); compute annualised basis of the second quarterly; join DGS3MO; studentized block bootstrap (block 20 days); walk-forward by year.
trial.data: Deribit public API (chart data for expired dated futures), BTC daily closes, FRED DGS3MO.
trial.pass: Median > 100 bp with the 95% CI excluding 100 bp and the sign holding in a majority of calendar years.
trial.controls: Timestamp alignment of futures and spot closes; exclude the final 7 days before each expiry; ETH replication; report 2022 separately (basis compression).

strategies.harness_suggestion: mandel/options/deribit_basis.py (curve snapshot + historical chart pull) feeding this, the box and the perp entries; template [underlying+, put+, call-].

strategies.name: Conversion
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Flat: the position is worth K at every S_T (stock called away at K above K, put to the writer at K below K), plus any dividends received before T.
strategies.max_profit: Locked, in PV terms: K e^{-rT} + PV(D) - (S0 + P - C) = (C - P) - (S0 - PV(D) - K e^{-rT}). Positive only when the call is rich / put cheap relative to parity at your funding rate.
strategies.max_loss: The same expression when negative (the usual case after spreads); plus pin-risk and early-assignment frictions listed under risks.
strategies.breakevens: None in S_T. The trade lends S0 + P - C at the implied rate r_impl = ln(K / (S0 + P - C - PV(D))) / T; it beats cash only if r_impl > your funding rate.

greeks_at_inception.theta: Small positive: r K e^{-rT} - q S e^{-qT} (accretion of the locked amount)
greeks_at_inception.vega: 0; rho negative (-K T e^{-rT}: a fixed payoff K at T loses PV when rates rise)

strategies.when_to_use: When C - P exceeds S - PV(D) - K e^{-rT} by more than all spreads (rare in liquid names); to flatten a long stock position through an event while keeping the shares (e.g. to extend a tax holding period, subject to straddle rules); market makers use it to unload long-call/short-put inventory. Not a way to collect stock-borrow fees: in hard-to-borrow names the put is rich and the call cheap, so a conversion earns LESS than the risk-free rate unless the shares are also lent out (the holder's trade that captures the fee is the reversal-from-inventory entry).
strategies.risks: Pin risk at K (uncertain call assignment leaves stock unhedged); early assignment of the short call the day before ex-dividend (lose the dividend); dividend cuts or specials; rate changes before T; in HTB names the conversion pays away the borrow fee.
strategies.margin_note: Broker-specific: under Reg-T the stock is margined (50% initial) with the short call covered and the long put paid in full; brokers that recognise the conversion reduce this toward the net debit; portfolio margin ~0 beyond the debit. Funding of the stock dominates the economics.
strategies.crypto_notes: With spot BTC as the stock leg and Deribit inverse options, the locked amount is fixed in USD (K) but paid in BTC at delivery (K / S_T BTC); with a dated future as the 'stock' leg it collapses to a parity check (F - K locked, no funding); with the perpetual as the stock leg it becomes a funding trade (see perp entry).
strategies.metals_notes: GC version: long GC future + long OG put + short OG call (same month); SPAN margin; American OG options can be assigned early when deep ITM (interest on the intrinsic value). GLD/SLV version identical to the equity case with no dividends.
variants: Conversion to extend holding period through an event (watch straddle rules)
strategies.claim: For SPY expiries before the next ex-dividend date (2026-12-18) with 30-64 DTE and strikes within +/- 5% of spot, the executable conversion lending rate (stock at ask, put at ask, call at bid, D = 0) is below the FRED 3-month bill rate in at least 95% of (K, T) pairs.

trial.statistic: Share of (K, T) pairs with r_conv_exec = ln(K / (S_ask + P_ask - C_bid)) / T below r_bill (both continuously compounded).
trial.null: Share < 95% (executable conversions beat bills in a material fraction of pairs).
trial.procedure: Day one: SPY chain plus underlying quote; restrict to expiries strictly before 2026-12-18 so no dividend enters; compute r_conv_exec per pair; compare to DGS3MO converted to continuous compounding; repeat daily until the ex-date window closes, then roll to the next quarter.
trial.data: CBOE delayed SPY chain with underlying bid/ask; FRED DGS3MO.
trial.pass: >= 95% of pairs below r_bill on day one and on >= 80% of captured days.
trial.controls: Mid-price version should sit near the SPX box rate (bill + ~0-60 bp); drop zero-bid legs; drop pairs where the short call is deep ITM (early-exercise contamination).

strategies.harness_suggestion: Reuse parity.py executable-rate function; payoff template [underlying+, put+, call-] must draw a flat line at K in the payoff-engine test.

strategies.name: Covered call / cash-secured put equivalence (synthetic identity trade)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Covered call P&L = min(S_T, K) - S0 + C. Equivalent form: cash-secured short put at the same K, T with cash K: P&L = P - max(K - S_T, 0) = min(S_T, K) - K + P. Difference (covered call minus short put) = (K - S0) + (C - P), a constant equal by parity to the carry difference; holding the covered call AND buying the put back is a conversion (flat at K).
strategies.max_profit: Covered call: (K - S0) + C. Short put: P.
strategies.max_loss: Covered call: S0 - C (at S_T = 0). Short put: K - P.
strategies.breakevens: Covered call: S_T = S0 - C. Short put: S_T = K - P (equal when parity holds with zero carry).

greeks_at_inception.delta: positive (1 - call delta; ~+0.5 ATM, higher for OTM calls), equal for both forms by parity

strategies.when_to_use: Choose the cheaper execution of one payoff: short puts need one trade, less capital under portfolio margin and no dividend/assignment handling; covered calls collect dividends and can be 'qualified covered calls' for tax; index exposure as put-write via SPX/XSP (1256).
strategies.risks: Full downside in both forms; early-assignment patterns differ (calls before ex-div, deep ITM puts for interest); margin treatment differs by broker.
strategies.margin_note: Covered call: stock margin, call covered; cash-secured put: full K in cash or Reg-T naked-put margin; portfolio margin ~15% stress for either.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit covered call = BTC on venue + short inverse call; short put needs BTC collateral and pays in BTC; the equivalence holds in USD with interest_rate 0, but BTC-denominated P&L differs because of inverse convexity.
strategies.metals_notes: GC: long future + short OG call equals short OG put plus a forward at K (all 1256); GLD covered call vs GLD short put as in equities; assigned GLD shares are collectibles.
variants: Cboe PutWrite (PUT) vs BuyWrite (BXM) index comparison
XSP put-write as 1256 substitute for SPY covered calls
strategies.claim: Over their common daily history in Cboe's published files, the annualised return of the Cboe S&P 500 PutWrite Index (PUT) exceeds that of the BuyWrite Index (BXM) by between 0 and 1.5 percentage points.

trial.statistic: Annualised return difference PUT - BXM from monthly returns; studentized block-bootstrap CI.
trial.procedure: Download PUT and BXM daily histories (free Cboe CSVs); monthly returns; block bootstrap of the difference; walk-forward by decade; report monthly correlation as a diagnostic.
trial.data: Cboe PUT and BXM index histories (free download, not yet ingested; PUT dashboard lists daily data since January 2007, with longer back-calculated history); FRED bills to explain the collateral-yield component.
trial.pass: 95% CI of the difference inside (0, 1.5) pp/yr.
trial.controls: BXMD (OTM calls) for strike dependence; check that 2008 and 2020 drawdowns coincide; T-bill collateral yield subtracted as an explanation test.

strategies.name: Crypto put-call parity vs dated future (Deribit inverse options)

legs.strike_rule: K near ATM (USD strike, premium in BTC), 1 BTC notional
legs.expiry_rule: T (Deribit 08:00 UTC expiry with a listed dated future)

legs.strike_rule: matching dated inverse future, USD notional = F (i.e. 1 BTC at entry price)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: In BTC: call (S_T - K)^+/S_T, put -(K - S_T)^+/S_T, short future of F USD notional F/S_T - 1; sum = (F - K)/S_T BTC = F - K USD at delivery. Deribit marks equal Black-76(F)/F with interest_rate 0, so fair C_btc - P_btc = 1 - K/F and the option-implied forward is F_impl = K / (1 - (C_btc - P_btc)). Multiplying (C - P) by the index is wrong by the basis.
strategies.max_profit: Locked (in BTC at entry terms): (C_btc - P_btc) received/paid vs 1 - K/F; trade the rich side: if C_btc - P_btc > 1 - K/F sell the synthetic and buy the future, otherwise the reverse.
strategies.max_loss: Same expression with the wrong sign after fees; plus liquidation risk under BTC-denominated margin in a crash.
strategies.breakevens: C_btc - P_btc = 1 - K/F.

greeks_at_inception.vega: 0; residual BTC/USD exposure on the locked amount (fixed USD paid in variable BTC)

strategies.when_to_use: Continuous scan of Deribit BTC/ETH books; violations beyond taker fees appear in illiquid strikes/expiries and near settlement; base for every crypto synthetic.
strategies.risks: Collateral convexity (inverse); 24/7 liquidation; delivery price is a time-averaged index, not the last trade; expiries without a listed future use a synthetic underlying built from option prices, so parity is tautological there; exchange counterparty risk; USDC-linear options follow ordinary (non-inverse) parity.
strategies.margin_note: Deribit portfolio margin recognises the flat combination; standard margin charges the short put in BTC.
strategies.crypto_notes: Live check 2026-10-14 ~17:00 UTC: BTC-15OCT26-73000-C mark 0.1095 BTC (bid 0.1075 / ask 0.1115; 0.12575 is the previous settlement_price), index 81,953, underlying_price 81,973.6, interest_rate 0. BTC-24SEP27-80000 C/P marks 0.1864/0.1153 give F_impl = 80000/(1 - 0.0711) = 86,123 vs future 86,134 (~1 bp). Futures curve: BTC-25DEC26 82,854 (~5.6%/yr), BTC-26MAR27 83,926 (~5.3%/yr), BTC-24SEP27 86,126 (~5.3%/yr) over index 81,953.

variants: Deribit synthetic vs CME BTC futures (cross-venue)

strategies.name: Deribit inverse box spread (USD lending/borrowing in BTC collateral)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: (K2 - K1)/S_T BTC = exactly K2 - K1 USD at the delivery price. Net debit is paid in BTC today, worth debit_usd = debit_btc x index; USD rate r_box = ln((K2 - K1)/debit_usd)/T. Under Deribit marks the box is worth (K2 - K1)/F BTC, so r_box at marks equals the futures basis ln(F/index)/T; executable prices and fees create the deviation.
strategies.max_profit: Long box: (K2 - K1) - debit_usd in USD, certain at expiry; received as (K2 - K1)/S_T BTC.
strategies.max_loss: None in USD at expiry (European); in BTC terms the receivable shrinks as BTC rises; liquidation risk on short legs before expiry under standard margin.
strategies.breakevens: None.

greeks_at_inception.delta: 0 in USD; in a BTC-denominated account the fixed-USD claim behaves like short BTC / long USD of notional (K2 - K1)

strategies.when_to_use: Lend USD into the crypto basis while holding BTC (long box); borrow USD against BTC (short box) when r_box is below CEX margin-borrow rates; stablecoin-free USD rate exposure.
strategies.risks: Exchange insolvency; liquidation of short legs in a crash (portfolio margin mitigates); wide far-strike quotes; fees capped as a fraction of premium can still be large relative to interest for short maturities.
strategies.margin_note: Portfolio margin nets the box to near-zero risk; standard margin charges each short option in BTC.
strategies.crypto_notes: Premiums and settlement in BTC (ETH for ETH options); 08:00 UTC expiry; mark-implied r_box = futures basis (~5.3%/yr to BTC-26MAR27 and BTC-24SEP27 on 2026-10-14). Compare with CME BTC options (USD cash, 1256).
strategies.metals_notes: n/a.
variants: Short inverse box (borrow USD against BTC)

trial.statistic: Median over snapshots of r_box_exec - r_bill (bp).
trial.procedure: Hourly polls for 14 days; build boxes from executable bid/ask; subtract fees; join DGS3MO; bootstrap (block = 1 day).
trial.data: Deribit public API, FRED DGS3MO.
trial.pass: Median > 100 bp with the 95% CI excluding 100 bp.
trial.controls: Mid vs executable; strike-pair invariance; exclude the settlement hour; ETH replication; report r_box_exec - basis separately.

strategies.name: Dividend arbitrage (long stock + ITM put over ex-div)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(S_T, K) + D - S0 - P.
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded above K; the floor outcome is K + D - S0 - P.
strategies.max_loss: P - (K - S0) - D = put time value minus the dividend (a loss whenever time value > D, the normal case).
strategies.breakevens: Floor breaks even when D = P - (K - S0); upside breakeven S_T = S0 + P - D.

greeks_at_inception.theta: negative (put time value), offset by the dividend capture

strategies.when_to_use: Ex-dividend eve in names whose deep ITM puts trade at or near intrinsic (time value < dividend), typically illiquid names; mostly a test of market efficiency.
strategies.risks: Put prices already embed the dividend; dividend cancellation; legging; the protective put can disqualify the dividend from qualified status (IRC 246(c) holding-period rules for diminished risk of loss).
strategies.margin_note: Protective put: stock at 50% Reg-T initial, put paid in full; portfolio margin ~ the max loss.
strategies.crypto_notes: No dividends; the loose analogue is airdrop/fork capture, which Deribit handles by contract adjustment, not cash dividends.
strategies.metals_notes: GLD/SLV/GC/SI pay no dividends; not applicable.
variants: Deep ITM covered call over ex-div (assignment usually removes the dividend)
SPY dividend capture with ITM puts around the quarterly ex-date
strategies.claim: For SPY and liquid US dividend payers on ex-dividend eve, the executable time value (P_ask - (K - S_bid)) of puts with delta < -0.9 and 7-30 DTE exceeds the declared dividend in more than 95% of observations.

trial.statistic: Share of ex-div-eve observations with P_ask - (K - S_bid) > D.
trial.null: Share <= 95% (an exploitable pocket exists among liquid names).
trial.procedure: Capture chains on ex-div eves; compute executable time value; compare with declared D; stratify by option volume.
trial.data: CBOE delayed chains captured on ex-div eves; ex-dividend calendar (not ingested); SPY 2026-12-18 ex-date as first ETF observation.
trial.pass: Share > 95% with the bootstrap 95% lower bound > 95% in liquid names.

strategies.name: Early exercise of deep ITM American puts for interest
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Decision rule: exercise now (receive K, deliver stock) iff K (1 - e^{-rT}) > C(K, T) + PV(D), i.e. interest on K exceeds the same-strike call value plus dividends you would forgo. Trading version: if a deep ITM American put is offered below intrinsic, buy the put and the stock and exercise for a riskless K - S_ask - P_ask.
strategies.max_profit: Sweep: K - S_ask - P_ask (instant). Rule: interest saved minus forfeited C + PV(D).
strategies.max_loss: Exercising when C + PV(D) > K (1 - e^{-rT}) forfeits the difference; sweep: execution slippage on the stock leg.

greeks_at_inception.theta: ~0 inside the exercise region (value pinned at intrinsic K - S)

strategies.when_to_use: High-rate regimes with deep ITM American puts; sub-intrinsic quotes; forecasting assignment of short deep ITM puts in synthetic longs and reversals.
strategies.risks: Need the deliverable shares; delayed quotes can show false sub-intrinsic prices; exercising a hedge removes protection.
strategies.margin_note: Exercise without shares creates a short stock position (Reg-T short-sale margin).
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit options are European: no early exercise; sub-intrinsic quotes in BTC are liquidity artefacts, captured by trading. IBIT options are American and follow the equity rule with D = 0.
strategies.metals_notes: OG/SO are American options on futures: exercising a deep ITM put creates a short future and credits K - F immediately as variation margin, which earns interest, so early exercise of deep ITM futures options (calls and puts) can be optimal; GLD/SLV follow the equity rule with D = 0.
variants: Assignment forecast for short deep ITM puts
Futures-option early exercise for interest on intrinsic

trial.null: Difference <= 30 pp (quotes do not reflect the early-exercise rule).

strategies.name: Early exercise of deep ITM calls before ex-dividend (and dividend spread)

legs.expiry_rule: first expiry after ex-div; exercise decision at the close of ex-div eve

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Decision rule: exercise on ex-div eve iff D > P(K, tau) + K (1 - e^{-r tau}), with tau the time remaining after the ex-date and P the same-strike put (from parity: holding is worth S - D - K e^{-r tau} + P). After exercise you hold stock and collect D. Dividend-spread variant: long and short deep ITM calls in huge size; exercise all longs and profit from the short calls left unassigned.
strategies.max_profit: D - [P + K (1 - e^{-r tau})] per share versus holding; dividend spread: D x unassigned fraction minus costs.
strategies.max_loss: Wrong exercise forfeits P + K (1 - e^{-r tau}) - D; dividend spread: fees with zero capture if all shorts are assigned.
strategies.breakevens: D = P(K, tau) + K (1 - e^{-r tau}).

greeks_at_inception.theta: small negative (~ -r K e^{-r tau}) before exercise

strategies.risks: Exercising forfeits the embedded put; broker exercise cutoffs; exchange fee changes ended the retail-scale dividend spread; in a conversion an assigned short call loses the expected dividend.
strategies.margin_note: Exercise needs cash or margin for K per share overnight; the dividend spread is margined as a vertical.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit options are European and BTC pays no dividend; IBIT pays no dividend; rule void.

strategies.name: Event-contract vs vertical-spread replication (Kalshi/Polymarket digitals vs SPXW verticals)

legs.strike_rule: K - w, where K = event threshold (e.g. 'S&P 500 closes above 6,800') and w = narrowest listed width (5)
legs.expiry_rule: SPXW 0 DTE matching the event date (PM, 4:00 pm ET close)

legs.strike_rule: Sell 100 x w = 500 YES contracts on 'close above K' (each pays $1); YES is a cash-or-nothing digital, recorded as 'underlying' because the schema has no digital type

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Vertical [K - w, K] pays 100 x min(max(S_T - K + w, 0), w): $0 below K - w, rising to $500 at K. Short 500 YES pays -$500 if S_T > K. Net: 0 for S_T <= K - w, 100 (S_T - K + w) >= 0 inside the band, 0 for S_T > K. The combination never pays negative, so it is a static super-replication: arbitrage if 500 x YES_bid - vertical_ask - fees > 0. Mirror (YES cheap): buy 500 YES, sell vertical [K, K + w], payoff >= 0. No-arbitrage band: (C(K) - C(K + w))/w <= YES <= (C(K - w) - C(K))/w (0 DTE, discounting negligible).
strategies.max_profit: 500 x YES - V + 100 w at S_T just below K (V = vertical cost); at least 500 x YES - V everywhere.
strategies.max_loss: V - 500 x YES (paid at entry) when outside the band edge, plus fees; settlement-source mismatch can create true losses.
strategies.breakevens: Price condition YES = V / (100 w); no S_T breakeven because the payoff is non-negative.

greeks_at_inception.delta: small; residual exposure concentrated in [K - w, K]
greeks_at_inception.gamma: approximately offsetting away from the band
greeks_at_inception.vega: ~0 net; the YES fair value moves with SPX IV

strategies.when_to_use: Whenever an event venue lists a threshold contract on an asset with a liquid 0 DTE chain (SPX/NDX, BTC via Deribit dailies, gold via GLD weeklies) and the YES price leaves the vertical-implied band by more than fees; also to quote binaries fairly.
strategies.risks: Settlement-source and timing mismatch (Kalshi uses its rulebook's official close; Polymarket may use a different oracle/time); the free CBOE feed is 15-minute delayed so this is a signal/paper test without a real-time feed; venue counterparty and withdrawal risk; event-venue position limits; fees (Kalshi's fee scales with P(1 - P); use the current schedule).
strategies.margin_note: Vertical is a paid debit (or defined-risk credit); YES/NO contracts are fully collateralised; no cross-margin between venues.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC threshold contracts vs Deribit daily options: Deribit inverse call spreads give the digital in BTC terms (convert with F), settled at the 08:00 UTC delivery price; event venues settle at their own time/oracle, so align or carry the gap as basis.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold thresholds vs GLD weekly verticals: GLD close vs the event's gold reference price differ, so the basis is larger.

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Short straddle at the pin: (C + P) - |S_T - K_pin|. The defensive use is the opposite action: close or roll any short option within ~1% of spot before the close to avoid uncertain assignment.

strategies.max_loss: Unbounded above (S_T - K_pin - (C + P)); K_pin - (C + P) below. After the close: pin risk (unknown assignment, unhedged weekend stock position).
strategies.breakevens: K_pin +/- (C + P).

strategies.name: Hard-to-borrow synthetic (implied borrow extraction; reversal from inventory)

legs.strike_rule: sell shares you already own at S0 (or short only with a locate cheaper than the implied borrow)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Standalone legs are a reversal: flat -K at T against cash S0 - C + P received today. For a holder who sold owned shares, the overall exposure is unchanged (synthetic long replaces the stock) and the lock is (S0 - C + P) e^{rT} - K = S0 e^{rT} - F ~ b S0 T, the options-implied borrow fee b (plus dividends priced into F, which the holder no longer receives but which are already in F). A conversion does the opposite and PAYS b.
strategies.max_profit: (S0 - C + P) e^{rT} - K - FV(D forgone) ~ b x S0 x T, locked if the short put is not assigned early.
strategies.max_loss: Early assignment of the short put (American, deep ITM) returns the stock early and ends the accrual; if the stock leg was a real short sale, recall/buy-in and fee resets apply.
strategies.breakevens: None in S_T; profitable while the implied borrow b exceeds spreads (and any fee your broker would pay you for lending the shares).
strategies.when_to_use: You own an HTB stock (meme names, recent IPOs, small biotech) and the chain implies borrow > 5%/yr while your broker's share-lending program pays you little: selling the shares and buying the synthetic captures the fee. Short sellers should use the synthetic short only when its implicit borrow is below their locate fee.
strategies.risks: HTB names have wide option spreads; selling shares realises capital gains and can trigger wash-sale rules if done at a loss; corporate actions; extreme squeezes make deep ITM short-put assignment and margin calls likely.
strategies.margin_note: Short put and long call margin (Reg-T naked-put requirement); if a real short sale is used, 150% short margin plus locate.
strategies.crypto_notes: No stock-borrow market on Deribit; the analogue is perpetual funding (longs pay shorts when crowded long) and CEX margin borrow rates for altcoins.
strategies.metals_notes: GLD/SLV occasionally become HTB in physical squeezes (SLV 2021); the chain's implied borrow spikes then. GC/SI futures have no borrow.

trial.procedure: Daily SPX chain plus ES quarterly option quotes; implied forwards from ATM pairs; record; bootstrap.
trial.data: CBOE delayed SPX chain (available); CME ES option quotes (not in the free data set).
trial.pass: Share above 3 bp below 5% over 60 days.
trial.controls: Quarterly-only matching; executable vs mid; XSP/MES replication.

strategies.blocked_on: CME ES/MES option quote source plus ~60 days of daily capture
strategies.harness_suggestion: parity.py cross_venue() with Black-76 for futures options once an ES chain source exists.

strategies.name: Long box spread (SPX box lending)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Exactly K2 - K1 at every S_T (bull call spread K1/K2 + bear put spread K2/K1).
strategies.max_profit: (K2 - K1) - net_debit, certain for European options held to T; implied lending rate r_box = ln((K2 - K1)/net_debit)/T.
strategies.max_loss: None at expiry for European options; mark-to-market loss if rates rise and you unwind early; with American options early assignment of a short leg can leave open directional risk (2019 Robinhood case: >$57k lost on $5k).
strategies.breakevens: None; it is a zero-coupon bond paying K2 - K1 at T.

greeks_at_inception.vega: 0; rho negative (-(K2 - K1) T e^{-r_box T})

strategies.when_to_use: Lend cash at the SPX box rate, which van Binsbergen-Diamond-Grotteria and Diamond-Van Tassel find above Treasuries by a convenience yield (~35 bp for USD on average, larger in stress and at higher rates); interest is taxed as Section 1256 60/40 gain; park margin-account collateral.
strategies.risks: Four-leg spread cost; only European cash-settled roots are safe (SPX, SPXW, XSP, NDX, RUT); American boxes (SPY, equity, OG/SO) are exposed to early assignment; OCC counterparty; mark-to-market before T.
strategies.margin_note: Fully paid net debit; portfolio margin recognises the flat payoff. Use wide strikes and complex-order-book execution; legged quotes from the delayed feed overstate cost.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit inverse box pays (K2 - K1)/S_T BTC = K2 - K1 USD at the delivery price; European, 08:00 UTC. Under Deribit marks its value is (K2 - K1)/F BTC, so its USD rate (debit_btc x index) equals the futures basis: ~5.3%/yr to BTC-24SEP27 on 2026-10-14 (86,126 vs index 81,953). See deribit-inverse-box entry.
strategies.metals_notes: OG/SO and GLD/SLV boxes are American (early-assignment risk); not a clean lending vehicle in metals.
variants: Box calendar / forward-rate lock (long near box, short far box)
Box ladder across expiries (box term structure)
Box vs bills spread trade (see box-treasury-convenience-yield)
strategies.claim: On the capture day, the median mid-price SPX box lending rate across SPX/SPXW expiries with 60-120 DTE (strike pairs within +/- 15% of spot) exceeds the FRED 3-month bill (continuously compounded) by between 15 and 80 bp.

trial.statistic: Median over boxes of r_box_mid - r_bill; companion executable rate r_box_exec (pay the ask on long legs, receive the bid on short legs).
trial.null: Median r_box_mid - r_bill <= 15 bp or >= 80 bp.
trial.procedure: Day one: build all boxes at 60-120 DTE (matched to the 3-month bill) from strike pairs with both legs bid > 0; r_box = ln((K2-K1)/debit)/T; median and bootstrap CI over strike pairs; repeat daily; extend to 6-12 months once DGS6MO/DGS1 are pulled from the same free FRED API.
trial.data: CBOE delayed SPX chain (29,918 contracts today), FRED DGS3MO.
trial.pass: Day-one median spread inside [15, 80] bp with the 95% bootstrap CI inside [0, 120] bp; persistence over 20 captured days.
trial.controls: Strike-invariance of r_box (if r_box varies by more than spreads across pairs, quote noise dominates); SPX AM vs SPXW PM roots; XSP replication; convert DGS3MO from bond-equivalent to continuous.

strategies.harness_suggestion: mandel/options/box.py: box_rate(chain, expiry, K1, K2, side) and daily box_curve; payoff-engine test asserts a flat K2 - K1.

strategies.name: Merger arbitrage with options (collared cash deal)

legs.strike_rule: target stock at S0 < offer price O (cash deal)
K_c = O (or the nearest strike at or below O)
K_p near the pre-announcement price (deal-break floor)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: min(max(S_T, K_p), K_c) - S0 + C - P: deal closes -> S_T ~ O, collect O - S0 + C - P; deal breaks -> loss limited at K_p.
strategies.max_profit: K_c - S0 + C - P.
strategies.max_loss: S0 - K_p - C + P.
strategies.breakevens: S_T = S0 - C + P.

greeks_at_inception.vega: negative near O, positive deal-break protection in the put

strategies.when_to_use: Announced cash deals with listed options where the spread (O - S0) is wide relative to the time to close and the put floor is cheap; variants for stock deals short the acquirer.
strategies.risks: Deal break (antitrust, financing); timing delays beyond the option expiry; competing bids above O (capped by the short call); early assignment of the short call near completion; options on targets are often illiquid.
strategies.margin_note: Collar: stock margin with covered call and paid put; portfolio margin reflects the floor.
strategies.crypto_notes: n/a (no corporate takeovers); loose analogue: token migration/merger events.
strategies.metals_notes: n/a (mining-company deals are equity deals).
variants: Stock-for-stock deal: long target, short acquirer x ratio, options on either
Naked short puts on the target below the offer
Long target + short calls only (no break protection)
strategies.claim: Collared cash-merger arbitrage on US targets with listed options earns an annualised return above the 3-month bill after option spreads, averaged across all deals in the sample.

trial.statistic: Mean annualised deal-level return minus the bill rate; bootstrap across deals.
trial.procedure: For each announced cash deal: enter the collar at the first close after announcement, hold to completion or break; compute returns; bootstrap; deflated Sharpe across collar-strike choices.
trial.data: Deal database (announcement, offer, outcome dates; not in the listed feeds) and option chains at announcement (history begins 2026-10-14).
trial.pass: Mean excess return > 0 with the 95% CI excluding 0.
trial.controls: Uncollared merger-arb return as benchmark; exclude deals with competing bids; size buckets.
