strategies.harness_suggestion: mandel/experiments/merger_collar.py once a deal feed exists; payoff template [underlying+, call- K=O, put+ K_p].

strategies.name: Perpetual funding vs dated-future/option-synthetic carry

legs.strike_rule: BTC-PERPETUAL, USD notional matched to the synthetic (collect funding when positive)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Delta-flat: long dated forward at F_impl (via options) vs short perp at P0 ~ S0. P&L ~ cumulative funding received - (F_impl - S0) + perp-vs-index tracking at exit; inverse-contract sizing leaves a small BTC-convexity residual.
strategies.max_profit: Cumulative funding over T minus the basis paid at entry (funding is uncapped in principle).
strategies.max_loss: Basis paid plus any negative funding paid over T; liquidation risk on the perp in squeezes.
strategies.breakevens: Cumulative funding over T = F_impl - S0 (basis paid at entry).

greeks_at_inception.theta: carry = funding rate minus annualised basis (sign varies)

strategies.when_to_use: When annualised perp funding exceeds the dated basis (crowded longs); the reverse (long perp, short dated) when the basis exceeds expected funding.
strategies.risks: Funding is variable and mean-reverting; perp mark vs index deviations; 24/7 liquidation; inverse collateral convexity.
strategies.margin_note: Deribit portfolio margin offsets the perp against the option synthetic; standard margin charges both.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit BTC-PERPETUAL funding is accrued continuously and published hourly (interest_1h) with an 8h reference (interest_8h) via public get_funding_rate_history; positive funding means longs pay shorts. Pre-check 2026-10-14: the trailing 365-day sum of interest_1h is ~2.28%, well below the ~5.3%/yr dated basis, so the short-perp/long-dated direction has recently lost carry.
strategies.metals_notes: n/a.
variants: Short perp / long dated future (no options)
Long perp / short dated (reverse) when basis > expected funding
Short perp / long spot (pure funding vs bills)
strategies.claim: Over non-overlapping 90-day windows since 2020, cumulative BTC-PERPETUAL funding received by a short perp exceeds the annualised basis of the front quarterly future paid at window start (pro-rated to 90 days) in at least 50% of windows.

trial.statistic: Share of windows with funding_90d - basis_90d > 0; mean difference with block-bootstrap CI.
trial.null: Share < 50% (the dated basis prices funding fully or over-prices it).
trial.procedure: Funding: sum interest_1h per window from get_funding_rate_history; basis: front-quarterly close / spot at window start from get_tradingview_chart_data (expired instruments available); compute differences; bootstrap; walk-forward by year.
trial.data: Deribit public API funding history and expired-futures chart data (both verified reachable), BTC daily closes.
trial.pass: Share >= 50% with the mean difference's 95% CI excluding 0 from below.
trial.controls: ETH replication; drop top 1% funding prints; account for taker fees on four legs; options-synthetic version tested separately on captured chains.

strategies.harness_suggestion: mandel/ingest deribit funding + expired-futures chart pulls -> mandel/experiments/perp_funding_carry.py with block bootstrap.

strategies.name: Put-call parity scan / synthetic forward
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Per unit S_T - K; P&L = S_T - K - (C - P). European parity: C - P = S - PV(D) - K e^{-rT} (continuous yield: S e^{-qT} - K e^{-rT}), so the implied forward is F_impl = K + (C - P) e^{rT}. American options (SPY, single names, GLD, IBIT) satisfy only the bounds S - PV(D) - K <= C - P <= S - K e^{-rT}. Every other entry in this family is a rearrangement of this identity.
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded: S_T - K - (C - P) as S_T rises.
strategies.max_loss: K + (C - P) at S_T = 0 (same as a forward bought at K + (C - P)).
strategies.breakevens: S_T = K + (C - P).

greeks_at_inception.gamma: 0 (call and put gamma cancel at the same K, T)
greeks_at_inception.theta: Small negative: q S e^{-qT} - r K e^{-rT} per year (accretion of the discounted strike), ~0 for short T
greeks_at_inception.vega: 0 (same-strike call and put vega cancel); rho +K T e^{-rT}

strategies.when_to_use: Baseline monitor: for each (K, T) compute F_impl and check that it is the same across strikes within an expiry (strike consistency) and consistent with the financing rate (box rate) and dividends. Violations wider than the combined half-spreads are conversion/reversal candidates; otherwise the scan outputs the market-implied forward, financing rate and dividend that every other template in this family consumes.
strategies.risks: American early exercise makes parity only a band for equity/ETF options; dividend forecast error; the free CBOE feed is 15-minute delayed, so apparent violations are not executable and stale quotes can fake them; legging risk; on SPX, SPX (AM-settled) and SPXW (PM-settled) roots on the same date are different contracts.
strategies.margin_note: Reg-T: naked short put requirement (greater of 20% of underlying minus OTM amount, or 10% of strike, plus premium) plus the long call paid in full; portfolio margin treats the pair as synthetic stock. SPX/XSP options are Section 1256 nonequity options; SPY/GLD/IBIT options are not.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit inverse options quote in BTC and their marks equal the Black-76 USD price divided by underlying_price F (the matching dated future, or a synthetic future 'SYN.' for expiries without a listed future) with interest_rate = 0. Verified 2026-10-14 on BTC-24SEP27-80000-C/P: marks 0.1864/0.1153 = Black76(F=86,134)/F, not /index. Parity in BTC terms is therefore C_btc - P_btc = 1 - K/F, i.e. F_impl = K / (1 - (C_btc - P_btc)); multiplying by the index instead of F is wrong by the basis (~5% at 1 year). No dividends; 24/7; funding enters only through the perpetual, not the option legs.
strategies.metals_notes: OG/SO options are American options on GC/SI futures: European parity would be C - P = e^{-rT}(F - K); for American futures options it holds only as a band. GLD/SLV follow the equity version with D = 0 (their forward embeds the 0.40%/0.50% expense ratio and any gold lease rate via the gold market). OG/SO are Section 1256; GLD/SLV options are not.
variants: Fiduciary call = protective put (long call + K e^{-rT} cash vs long stock + long put)
American parity band check (S - PV(D) - K <= C - P <= S - K e^{-rT})
Implied dividend extraction PV(D_impl) = S - K e^{-rT} - (C - P) (European)
Implied-volatility parity check (call IV = put IV at the same K, T under correct forward)
Strike-consistency of F_impl within one expiry (model-free, dividend-free)
strategies.claim: On the CBOE delayed SPX chain (European, cash-settled), fewer than 2% of (K, T) pairs within ATM +/- 5 strikes have an implied forward F_impl = K + (C_mid - P_mid) e^{rT} that differs from the median F_impl of the same root and expiry by more than half the combined call + put bid-ask spread (times e^{rT}).

trial.statistic: Share of (K, T) pairs with |F_impl(K,T) - median_K F_impl(T)| > 0.5 e^{rT} (spread_call + spread_put).
trial.null: The share is >= 2% (parity is not strike-consistent within spreads on the SPX book).
trial.procedure: Day one: pull the SPX chain, split by root (SPX vs SPXW), take ATM +/- 5 strikes per expiry, drop zero-bid legs, compute F_impl from mids using the FRED 3-month bill (the rate cancels to first order in the cross-strike comparison), count exceedances; repeat daily and block-bootstrap the daily share as capture accumulates.
trial.data: CBOE delayed SPX chain (available today); FRED DGS3MO. No dividend input is needed because the comparison is across strikes within one expiry.
trial.pass: Day-one share < 2% with a one-sided 95% bootstrap bound < 2%; still < 2% on >= 16 of the first 20 captured days.
trial.controls: Placebo: shift put quotes by one strike and confirm the statistic flags them; repeat on XSP (should match SPX); repeat on SPY with the American band instead of equality; exclude quotes whose last update is older than the chain timestamp.

strategies.harness_suggestion: mandel/options/parity.py: implied_forward(chain, r) -> per-(K,T) table with strike-dispersion column; inverse_parity(deribit_book) using F_impl = K/(1 - (C_btc - P_btc)); 2-leg template [call+, put-] in the payoff engine must draw a straight line.

strategies.name: Reversal (reverse conversion)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Flat: -K at every S_T (you buy the stock at K, via the call above K or put assignment below K, and return the borrowed shares), minus dividends paid on the short before T.
strategies.max_profit: Locked: (S0 - C + P) e^{r_reb T} - K - FV(D) - borrow fee, where r_reb is the rebate actually earned on short proceeds.
strategies.max_loss: The same expression when negative; plus buy-in/recall risk on the short stock and borrow-fee spikes before T.
strategies.breakevens: None in S_T. The trade borrows at r_impl = ln(K / (S0 - C + P - PV(D))) / T via the options and lends the short proceeds at the rebate rate.

greeks_at_inception.theta: Small negative: q S e^{-qT} - r K e^{-rT} (mirror of the conversion)
greeks_at_inception.vega: 0; rho positive (+K T e^{-rT}, a fixed liability K at T)

strategies.when_to_use: When the put is cheap relative to the call (C - P below parity) and you receive close to full interest on short proceeds with a cheap locate; market makers use reversals to flatten short-call/long-put inventory. In HTB names the implied borrow in the chain is the price of this trade.
strategies.risks: Locate/buy-in risk; borrow fee resets; you owe dividends on the short stock (increases hurt); pin risk on the short put; early assignment of a deep ITM short put (American) ends the trade early.
strategies.margin_note: Short stock 150% Reg-T requirement with the long call as cover; short proceeds earn little or nothing at most retail brokers, which removes the edge for retail; portfolio margin near zero.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit: short the dated future instead of borrowing coin (no borrow fee, no recall); the lock becomes a pure inverse-parity check F_impl = K/(1 - (C_btc - P_btc)) vs F. Shorting spot on a CEX margin account pays hourly borrow interest, the analogue of the stock-borrow fee.
strategies.metals_notes: GC: short GC future + long OG call + short OG put; no borrow fee, SPAN margin. GLD/SLV borrow is usually general collateral but tightens in physical squeezes (SLV 2021), which shows up as a high implied borrow in the chain.
variants: Reversal from inventory: sell owned shares and buy the synthetic (see hard-to-borrow entry)
strategies.claim: On a single capture day, the 90th percentile of options-implied borrow (r_bill - r_impl from 30-90 DTE ATM parity at mid prices, dividend-adjusted) across the 200 most liquid optionable US single names exceeds 200 bp/yr.

trial.statistic: 90th percentile across names of implied borrow b_i = r_bill - r_impl,i.
trial.null: 90th percentile <= 200 bp (implied borrow is not dispersed).
trial.procedure: For each name: ATM +/- 2 strikes at the first two expiries with 30-90 DTE; r_impl from parity with PV(D) of declared dividends inside T; b_i = r_bill - r_impl; take the cross-sectional 90th percentile; bootstrap across names; repeat daily.
trial.data: CBOE delayed chains (available), FRED DGS3MO, ex-dividend dates and amounts for 200 names (NOT in the listed feeds).
trial.pass: Day-one 90th percentile > 200 bp with bootstrap 95% lower bound > 200 bp.
trial.controls: SPY/QQQ/IWM computed the same way should be < 50 bp; exclude names with a zero-bid ATM leg; placebo with mismatched expiries.

strategies.blocked_on: Single-name ex-dividend calendar (free sources exist but are not ingested); without it dividend yield is indistinguishable from implied borrow. The cross-section itself needs only today's chain.
strategies.harness_suggestion: parity.py implied_borrow column; payoff template [underlying-, call+, put-] asserting a flat -K line.

strategies.name: Short box spread (SPX box borrowing)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Exactly -(K2 - K1) at every S_T; you received net_credit at inception.
strategies.max_profit: net_credit - (K2 - K1), which is negative whenever rates are positive: the trade is a loan, not a profit-seeking position. Implied borrowing rate r_box = ln((K2 - K1)/net_credit)/T.
strategies.max_loss: (K2 - K1) - net_credit (the interest), certain for European options; American options can be assigned early and create open risk.
strategies.breakevens: None.
strategies.when_to_use: Borrow near Treasury-plus-convenience-yield rates against a portfolio-margin account instead of paying the broker's margin rate; the implied interest is a Section 1256 loss.
strategies.risks: Reg-T brokers may hold the full spread width as requirement; liquidation if other positions lose; never with American options; unwind cost if rates fall.
strategies.margin_note: Portfolio margin recognises the defined liability; Reg-T may require the full width. SPX/XSP/NDX/RUT only.
strategies.crypto_notes: A Deribit short inverse box borrows USD value (received as BTC premium) and repays a fixed USD amount in BTC; its rate equals the futures basis (~5.3%/yr on 2026-10-14), so it is a dearer loan than SPX boxes.
strategies.metals_notes: Not advisable with American OG/SO or GLD/SLV options (early assignment).
variants: XSP short box for small loans
Short far box + long near box (forward borrowing lock)
strategies.claim: On the capture day, the median executable SPX short-box borrowing rate (sell bids, buy offers on all four legs) across expiries with 180-730 DTE is below the FRED 3-month bill + 50 bp, i.e. at least 100 bp below a benchmark retail margin rate of bill + 150 bp.

trial.statistic: Median over expiries of r_box_borrow_exec - r_bill.
trial.procedure: Day one: for each SPX expiry with 180-730 DTE build wide boxes from legs with bids > 0; compute executable and mid borrowing rates; compare to DGS3MO (margin rates float off short rates, so the 3-month bill is the right benchmark); repeat daily.
trial.data: CBOE delayed SPX chain, FRED DGS3MO.
trial.pass: Median < 50 bp on day one and on >= 80% of captured days.
trial.controls: Strike-invariance; SPX vs XSP agreement; mid vs executable gap reported.

strategies.harness_suggestion: box.py with side='short' using executable prices; borrow-curve output.

strategies.name: Synthetic long stock (combo)

legs.strike_rule: K ATM (or K_call >= K_put for split-strike)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Same strike: S_T - K - (C - P). Split strike (K_p < K_c): max(S_T - K_c, 0) - max(K_p - S_T, 0) - net premium: flat between K_p and K_c, long above K_c, long via the short put below K_p.
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded.
strategies.max_loss: Same strike: K + (C - P) at S_T = 0. Split strike: K_p + net premium.
strategies.breakevens: Same strike: S_T = K + (C - P). Split strike: K_c + net premium if net premium > 0, K_p + net premium (i.e. K_p - net credit) if net premium < 0.

greeks_at_inception.delta: +1 (same strike) / about +0.4 to +0.6 for a 25-delta risk reversal
greeks_at_inception.gamma: 0 (same strike) / sign depends on which wing is nearer spot (split strike)
greeks_at_inception.theta: Same strike: small negative q S e^{-qT} - r K e^{-rT}; split strike: sign depends on wing values
greeks_at_inception.vega: 0 (same strike) / long call vega minus short put vega, skew-dependent (split strike)

strategies.when_to_use: Stock replacement when the options-implied financing rate (r_impl from parity) is below your margin-loan rate; long exposure in accounts that cannot hold the underlying; split-strike for a cheaper, gapped long.
strategies.risks: Full downside; early assignment of a deep ITM short put (American); dividends are priced out of the forward, not received; implied financing can exceed margin rates in HTB names; margin calls on the short put.
strategies.margin_note: Reg-T: naked short put requirement plus long call paid in full; portfolio margin ~15% stress; SPX/XSP versions are cash-settled Section 1256 contracts.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit synthetic long via inverse options pays (S_T - K)/S_T BTC: in USD it is linear, in BTC it is concave (a long inverse future); collateral is BTC, so a crash shrinks collateral while the position loses. Fair value C_btc - P_btc = 1 - K/F.
strategies.metals_notes: OG synthetic long = long GC future at K with option margin instead of SPAN (1256). GLD options are equity options (not 1256); the tax character of GLD option gains relative to the 28% collectibles rate on GLD shares is not settled guidance, so treat tax as a question for an adviser, not an edge.
variants: Deep ITM call stock replacement (delta 0.85-0.95 single leg)
IBIT synthetic vs Deribit future (cross-venue BTC financing)
strategies.claim: For SPY expiries with 180-365 DTE, the executable financing rate of an ATM synthetic long (call at ask, put at bid, dividends from SPY's trailing four distributions) is below the 3-month bill + 50 bp in at least 80% of expiries, i.e. at least 100 bp cheaper than a benchmark retail margin rate of bill + 150 bp.

trial.statistic: r_impl_exec - r_bill per expiry, r_impl_exec solving C_ask - P_bid = S - PV(D) - K e^{-r T}.
trial.null: r_impl_exec - r_bill >= 50 bp in more than 20% of expiries.
trial.procedure: Day one on SPY (QQQ/IWM/GLD/IBIT as replications): ATM strike per expiry with 180-365 DTE; PV(D) from trailing distributions on the known quarterly ex-dates; compute r_impl_exec and r_impl_mid; compare to DGS3MO; repeat daily.
trial.data: CBOE delayed SPY chain, FRED DGS3MO, SPY trailing four quarterly distributions (4 public numbers entered by hand; not in the listed feeds). GLD/IBIT replications need no dividends.
trial.pass: >= 80% of expiries with r_impl_exec - r_bill < 50 bp on day one and on >= 80% of captured days.
trial.controls: Sensitivity to +/-10% dividend forecast; mid-based rate; exclude expiries with a zero-bid leg; GLD/IBIT dividend-free replication.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Template [call+, put-]; parity.py reports r_impl_askbid and r_impl_mid per expiry.

strategies.name: Synthetic options (synthetic call / synthetic put from stock + option)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Synthetic long call (protective/married put): max(S_T, K) - S0 - P = max(S_T - K, 0) + K - S0 - P, i.e. a long call plus a bond paying K. Variants: synthetic long put = short stock + long call (P&L = S0 - C - min(S_T, K)); synthetic short call = short stock + short put; synthetic short put = long stock + short call (covered call); synthetic straddle = long stock + 2 puts; collar (long stock + long put K1 + short call K2) = bull call spread K1/K2 + bond K1.
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded (synthetic long call).
strategies.max_loss: S0 + P - K (at S_T <= K).
strategies.breakevens: S_T = S0 + P.
strategies.when_to_use: Replicate the cheaper side of a payoff given spreads, financing, borrow and dividends; convert an existing stock position into option-like exposure without selling; hedge with whichever leg is liquid.
strategies.risks: Same as the replicated option plus stock-leg funding; early exercise and dividend timing break exact equivalence for American options; short-stock variants need a locate.
strategies.margin_note: Protective put: stock margin with the put paid; synthetic put via short stock: 150% short margin with the call as cover.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit: BTC on venue + inverse put = synthetic call in USD terms; inverse convexity changes BTC-denominated P&L.
strategies.metals_notes: GC future + OG put = synthetic OG call (1256); GLD + GLD put as the equity route.
variants: Synthetic long put (short stock + long call)
Synthetic short call (short stock + short put)
Synthetic straddle (stock + 2 puts / short stock + 2 calls)
Collar = bull call spread + bond equivalence
strategies.claim: For SPY expiries before 2026-12-18 with 30-64 DTE and strikes within +/- 5% of spot, buying SPY at the ask plus the put at the ask costs less than buying the call at the ask plus holding K e^{-r_bill T} in bills in at least 60% of strikes, because option prices embed a financing rate above the bill rate.

trial.statistic: Share of strikes with (S_ask + P_ask) < (C_ask + K e^{-r_bill T}).
trial.procedure: Day one: SPY chain and underlying quote; no dividend inside T; compute both costs per strike; repeat daily.
trial.data: CBOE delayed SPY chain, FRED DGS3MO.
trial.pass: Share >= 60% on day one and on >= 80% of captured days.
trial.controls: Replace r_bill with the SPX box rate (the share should fall to ~50%); mid-price version; GLD/IBIT dividend-free replications.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Templates [underlying+, put+] vs [call+] plus a bond leg; payoff engine must show identical kinked shapes offset by K - S0 - P + C.

strategies.name: Synthetic short stock (combo)

legs.strike_rule: K ATM (or K_put <= K_call for split strike)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Same strike: K - S_T + (C - P) (net credit C - P, negative if a debit).
strategies.max_profit: K + (C - P) at S_T = 0.
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded as S_T rises.
strategies.breakevens: S_T = K + (C - P).

greeks_at_inception.theta: Small positive: r K e^{-rT} - q S e^{-qT}; the implicit borrow (r_bill - r_impl) is paid through the price

strategies.when_to_use: Short exposure without a locate or buy-in risk, with dividends priced in rather than paid explicitly; hedging a long in an HTB name; shorting the index through SPX/XSP with 1256 treatment.
strategies.risks: Unbounded loss; early assignment of the short call before ex-dividend (American); in HTB names the put is rich so the full borrow is paid up front; margin on the short call rises in a rally; pin risk at K.
strategies.margin_note: Reg-T: naked short call requirement plus long put paid in full; portfolio margin ~15% stress.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit inverse synthetic short pays K/S_T - 1 BTC: convex in the short's favour in BTC terms (like a short inverse future); no borrow, no funding, unlike shorting the perpetual.
strategies.metals_notes: OG synthetic short = short GC future with option margin (1256); GLD/SLV synthetic shorts avoid ETF borrow, which spikes in physical squeezes (the chain then prices the borrow anyway).
variants: Deep ITM put single-leg short replacement
SPX/XSP synthetic short as 1256 hedge of a SPY portfolio
strategies.claim: For SPY expiries before 2026-12-18 with 30-64 DTE (no dividend inside T), the executable implicit borrow cost of an ATM synthetic short, r_bill - r_impl with r_impl solving C_bid - P_ask = S - K e^{-r T}, is below 50 bp/yr in at least 80% of (K, T) pairs within +/- 2% of spot.

trial.statistic: Share of near-ATM pairs with r_bill - r_impl_exec < 50 bp.
trial.null: Share < 80% (synthetic shorts in SPY cost more than 50 bp/yr over general collateral).
trial.procedure: Day one: SPY chain, expiries strictly before the ex-date, strikes within +/- 2%; compute r_impl_exec from put ask / call bid; compare to DGS3MO; repeat daily; replicate on GLD and IBIT with no dividend (their expense ratios reduce the forward via the underlying market and are reported separately).
trial.data: CBOE delayed SPY/GLD/IBIT chains, FRED DGS3MO.
trial.pass: Share >= 80% on day one and on >= 80% of captured days.
trial.controls: Mid-price version; stale-quote filter; exclude zero-bid legs; compare with the SPX box rate to separate the bill-vs-option-financing basis from borrow.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Template [put+, call-]; parity.py implicit_borrow column using executable sides (put ask, call bid).

strategies.name: Vertical-spread bound and strike-monotonicity arbitrage
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: min(max(S_T - K1, 0), K2 - K1): between 0 and K2 - K1. No-arbitrage bounds: 0 <= C(K1) - C(K2) <= (K2 - K1) e^{-rT} (European; <= K2 - K1 for American). Violations: a call spread offered for a credit (monotonicity, buy it) or bid above the discounted width (sell it). Puts mirror: 0 <= P(K2) - P(K1) <= (K2 - K1) e^{-rT}. Intrinsic bounds: C >= max(S - PV(D) - K e^{-rT}, 0), C <= S.
strategies.max_profit: Bought: (K2 - K1) - debit (all of it plus the credit if bought for a credit). Sold above width: credit - (K2 - K1) e^{-rT} minimum.
strategies.max_loss: Bought: debit. Sold: (K2 - K1) - credit.
strategies.breakevens: Bought: S_T = K1 + debit.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: positive if spot nearer K1, negative if nearer K2
greeks_at_inception.theta: negative if spot nearer K1, positive if nearer K2
greeks_at_inception.vega: positive if spot nearer K1, negative if nearer K2

strategies.when_to_use: Automated scan for bound violations (crossed strikes, spreads priced above width, options below intrinsic) in delayed or illiquid chains; validation of quotes before any model consumes them.
strategies.risks: Delayed/stale quotes; American early exercise of a short ITM leg; width bounds for American options are undiscounted.
strategies.margin_note: Defined-risk spread: Reg-T requirement is the debit (bought) or the width minus credit (sold).
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit: test on USD prices (C_btc x F); the width bound is K2 - K1 in USD, i.e. (K2 - K1)/F in BTC at marks.
strategies.metals_notes: Same tests on GLD/SLV and OG/SO (Black-76 discounted width for futures options).
variants: Intrinsic lower-bound sweep (buy below intrinsic and exercise / hedge)
Upper bound C <= S, P <= K e^{-rT} (European)
Bound checks on Deribit and event-venue ladders
strategies.claim: Across the CBOE delayed SPY, SPX, QQQ, GLD and IBIT chains, fewer than 0.1% of adjacent-strike call or put verticals violate monotonicity or the width bound at executable prices on the capture day.

trial.statistic: Share of adjacent-strike verticals with executable violation (debit < 0 or bid > width bound).
trial.procedure: Day one: enumerate adjacent pairs per expiry; compute executable debits/credits; count violations; repeat daily.
trial.data: CBOE delayed chains (available), FRED DGS3MO for discounting.
trial.pass: Share < 0.1% on day one and on >= 80% of captured days.
trial.controls: Mid-price violation rate as a quote-quality diagnostic; exclude zero-bid legs; IBIT/GLD reported separately (wider spreads).

strategies.harness_suggestion: static_arb.py vertical_scan(chain); also used as a quote-sanity gate in the daily options-fetch job.

strategies.name: Calendarised (time) butterfly
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Wings are bought in the far expiry and the body sold in the near; K1 < K2 < K3, equidistant. At the front expiry T1: P&L(S) = V_far(S; K1) + V_far(S; K3) - 2*max(S - K2, 0) - D. For equidistant strikes the intrinsic values cancel on a big up-move ((S-K1) + (S-K3) - 2(S-K2) = 0), so what remains is the far wings' extrinsic: a butterfly whose edges are lifted by the wings' time value.
strategies.max_profit: Near S = K2 at T1: (K2 - K1) + extrinsic_far(K2; K1) + extrinsic_far(K2; K3) - D. Compare the plain same-expiry fly's (K2 - K1) - D (OIC: high strike - middle strike - net premium).
strategies.max_loss: About D minus the residual far-wing extrinsic when S is far outside the wings at T1, bounded by D. If the far wings are held after T1 they become a long strangle, which cannot lose more than its value.
strategies.breakevens: Two roots of V_far(S; K1) + V_far(S; K3) - 2*max(S-K2, 0) = D, near K1 + D - extrinsic_far and K3 - D + extrinsic_far. These are the plain fly's K1 + D and K3 - D (OIC) pushed outward by the wings' remaining time value.

greeks_at_inception.delta: about 0 (+0.03 in the Black-Scholes example at 16% IV)
greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative near K2 (two short near calls; -0.064)
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive between the wings (+8.1 per year per 100 of notional)
greeks_at_inception.vega: positive (+6.1): two far-wing vegas exceed two near-body vegas. Unlike the plain butterfly, which loses slightly when IV rises (OIC).

strategies.when_to_use: A pin-the-strike view for the front cycle with protection against an IV rise (the plain fly loses when IV rises). Low absolute IV; flat or inverted term structure (front body rich). It works as a calendar with a cheaper, wider body.
strategies.risks: A move through a wing before T1 loses toward D. The two short body calls carry assignment and pin risk at T1. Six contracts of costs. After T1 the far wings must be re-sold against or closed.
strategies.margin_note: Debit structure; margined as two diagonal spreads (long far / short near on each side); defined risk; IRA-eligible at most brokers.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit strike grids are coarser at long expiries, so equidistant wings may not exist on the far expiry at the body's spacing. European cash settlement removes body-assignment risk. Portfolio Margin is needed for netting. Weekend theta on the body helps the seller.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: wings and body may reference different futures months; SPAN spread credit; 1256. GLD/SLV: fine strike grids ($1 on GLD) make equidistant time butterflies easy; SLV's call skew tilts the pricing. CME pages returned 403 this session.
variants: Broken-wing calendarised fly (skip a strike on one wing to finance)
Iron calendarised fly: short near ATM straddle, long far OTM strangle
Reverse calendarised fly: body in the far, wings in the near (short vega)
Weekly body (7 DTE) vs monthly wings
Same-strike horizontal time butterfly across three expiries (separate entry)
strategies.claim: In the top-decile months of VIX increase since 2007-12, a calendarised ATM SPY butterfly (+/-3% wings at 60 DTE, 2x ATM body at 30 DTE) loses less per unit of debit by the front expiry than the 30-DTE butterfly on the same strikes, model-priced.

trial.statistic: Mean paired difference in P&L/debit (time fly minus plain fly) within top-decile delta-VIX holding periods
trial.null: Zero difference in the spike decile (paired bootstrap)
trial.procedure: Monthly entries since 2007-12. Black-Scholes pricing from VIX/VIX3M. Revalue both structures at T1 and sort by delta-VIX over the hold. Paired bootstrap; walk-forward halves.
trial.data: SPY closes, VIX, VIX3M, FRED 3-month bill
trial.pass: Spike-decile difference > 0 with the 95% CI excluding 0
trial.controls: VIX is a 30-day variance-swap index that sits above 30-day ATM IV, so this trial is model-priced, not market-priced (flat smile). Costs on 6 vs 4 contracts. Pin risk modelled at mid minus half the spread. The overall mean P&L is reported but is not the claim.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Two-expiry simulator with K-slot strikes. Add the plain butterfly as the control leg set and report results by delta-VIX decile.

strategies.name: Double calendar spread
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At the front expiry T1, with K1 (puts) < S0 < K2 (calls): P&L(S) = V_far_put(S; K1) + V_far_call(S; K2) - max(K1-S, 0) - max(S-K2, 0) - D. Two humps, peaking at K1 and K2, with a saddle between them. Far outside both strikes the P&L falls toward -D.
strategies.max_profit: At S = K1: V_far_put(K1; K1) + V_far_call(K1; K2) - D. At S = K2: V_far_put(K2; K1) + V_far_call(K2; K2) - D. The larger of the two depends on IV at T1.
strategies.max_loss: D (net debit) when S finishes far outside both strikes at T1, for American puts and for calls. On European underlyings (SPX/XSP, Deribit) a deep-ITM put side can lose slightly more than D, by about K1(1 - e^(-r*tau)) - S(1 - e^(-q*tau)), as for the put calendar.
strategies.breakevens: The roots of V_far_put(S) + V_far_call(S) - max(K1-S, 0) - max(S-K2, 0) = D. Normally there are two, one below K1 and one above K2. If the saddle between the strikes dips below zero (wide strikes, low IV), there are two more inside.

greeks_at_inception.delta: about 0 (the call calendar above spot leans long, the put calendar below spot leans short; Black-Scholes at 16% IV: +0.04)
greeks_at_inception.gamma: slightly negative at S0 (-0.005 in the example) because both calendars are OTM; most negative near each strike
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive at S0 and between the strikes; negative far outside
greeks_at_inception.vega: positive (two long far legs; +11.3 in the example)

strategies.when_to_use: A range-bound view over the front cycle, with low IV expected to rise or hold. It gives a wider profit zone than a single calendar, at the cost of a lower peak and twice the fills. Prefer it when the term structure is flat or inverted, so the front is sold rich.
strategies.risks: A trending move through either strike loses toward D. A drop in IV hurts. Four legs of bid-ask. Early assignment on short near legs (ITM puts deep in the money, ITM calls before ex-dividend). Pin risk at T1 on either short strike.
strategies.margin_note: Debit paid in full. It is two defined-risk calendar spreads and IRA-eligible; no margin beyond the debit while the longs outlive the shorts.
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit all four legs pay taker fees (capped at a fraction of premium). European cash settlement at 08:00 UTC removes assignment risk. BTC's flat-to-positive call skew makes the call half pricier than on SPY. Weekend theta accrues seven days a week. Margin offsets between shorts and longs depend on Portfolio Margin.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: with near and far legs on different futures months, the structure also carries the futures calendar spread; SPAN margins it as two calendar spreads; 1256. GLD/SLV are the equity-option route with weeklies; SLV's call skew tilts the pricing. CME pages returned 403 this session.
variants: Straddle-strike double calendar (both calendars ATM) = straddle calendar (separate entry)
Puts at the lower strike and calls at the upper (the default here, keeping both shorts OTM)
Unbalanced: wider on the side the trader expects to hold
Triple calendar (adds an ATM calendar to fill the saddle)
strategies.claim: Entered on the same days and held to the front expiry, a +/-5% 30/60-DTE double calendar on SPY has a lower standard deviation of P&L as a percentage of debit than the ATM single calendar of the same expiries, model-priced (VIX/VIX3M).

trial.statistic: Ratio of standard deviations of P&L/debit (double / single), paired by entry date
trial.null: Ratio = 1 (variance-ratio test via paired bootstrap of non-overlapping monthly entries)
trial.procedure: Daily entries since 2007-12-04 with Black-Scholes pricing from VIX/VIX3M (OTM legs at the same flat IV; a SKEW-based tilt as a sensitivity), revalued at T1. Non-overlapping monthly subsample for CIs; walk-forward halves.
trial.data: SPY closes, VIX, VIX3M, SKEW, FRED 3-month bill
trial.pass: Std ratio < 0.9 with the 95% CI excluding 1 in both halves
trial.controls: VIX is a 30-day variance-swap index that sits above 30-day ATM IV, so this trial is model-priced, not market-priced. A flat smile understates the put wing. Commissions for 8 fills vs 4. Pin risk modelled by closing at mid minus half the spread at T1. The OTM debit is smaller, so also report std of P&L per unit of max loss.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Use the same two-expiry simulator as the single calendar with a strike list. Add the SKEW-index tilt as an optional smile adjustment (put IV = VIX + k*(SKEW - 100)).

strategies.name: Double diagonal spread

legs.strike_rule: K1: put delta -0.10 at 60 DTE (~0.93*S0 at 16% IV)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Wings-outside form: K1 < K2 < S0 < K3 < K4, an iron condor whose wings sit in the later expiry. At the front expiry T1: P&L(S) = V_far_put(S; K1) + V_far_call(S; K4) - max(K2-S, 0) - max(S-K3, 0) - D (or + C if entered for a credit). Between K2 and K3 the shape is U-shaped, not a plateau: the far strangle is worth least midway between the wings, so P&L peaks near K2 and K3. Beyond the short strikes it slopes down to a floor.
strategies.max_profit: Near S = K2 or S = K3 at T1: both shorts expire worthless or at the money, and the far wings hold their maximum time value. Max = max over S in [K2, K3] of V_far_put(S; K1) + V_far_call(S; K4) - D. It depends on IV at T1.
strategies.max_loss: About max(K2 - K1, K4 - K3) + D - the residual far-wing value, when S is far beyond a wing at T1 (with a credit entry: width - C). An alternative inside-straddle form (long far ATM straddle, short near OTM strangle) has max loss D, if S sits at the straddle strike at the straddle's expiry.
strategies.breakevens: Two: one below K2 and one above K3, where the far wing's remaining value minus the short's intrinsic equals D. Exact levels depend on IV at T1.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative between the short strikes (Black-Scholes at 16% IV: -0.052)
greeks_at_inception.vega: about 0 for this 0.16/0.10-delta wings-outside form (Black-Scholes: +0.28, vs +11 for the +/-5% double calendar): the far wings' vega roughly offsets the near shorts'. The inside-straddle form is strongly long vega.

strategies.when_to_use: An iron-condor alternative when the near strangle is rich relative to the far wings (flat or inverted term structure). Use it for a neutral view with S between K2 and K3 through T1. Use the inside-straddle form, not this one, to add long vega.
strategies.risks: Small dollar profit relative to the number of legs. A trending move past a short strike approaches max loss. Early assignment on the shorts around ex-dividend. After T1 the two far wings are a long strangle that bleeds unless re-sold against.
strategies.margin_note: The wings-outside form is margined as two diagonal spreads (max loss = width + debit) and is IRA-eligible at most brokers. The long expiry must be at or after the short expiry on each side.
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit the wings and body expire at 08:00 UTC on different dates. European cash settlement means the body settles to cash and leaves the far strangle. Portfolio Margin is needed for spread-level margin. BTC skew is roughly symmetric to call-skewed, so the call side is not the cheap side as it is on SPY.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: four options, possibly across two futures months; SPAN inter-month credit; 1256. GLD/SLV are the retail route; SLV's call skew makes the call wing costly. CME pages returned 403 this session.
variants: Inside-straddle double diagonal (long far ATM straddle, short near OTM strangle): long vega
Credit double diagonal: far wings far enough OTM that the structure nets a credit
Calendarised iron condor: iron-condor strikes with the wings one cycle later
Campaign double diagonal: re-sell the near strangle monthly against the far wings
Weekly double diagonal: 7-DTE strangle vs 35-DTE wings
strategies.claim: On SPY, a double diagonal (near 0.16-delta strangle at 30 DTE, far 0.10-delta wings at 60 DTE) has a higher mean P&L per unit of max loss than the 30-DTE iron condor on the same strikes when entered with VIX below its trailing 1-year median, model-priced.

trial.statistic: Mean P&L / max loss for the double diagonal minus that of the iron condor, on low-VIX entry days
trial.null: Zero difference; paired monthly P&L permuted between the two structures
trial.procedure: Monthly entries since 2007-12 on days with VIX below its trailing 252-day median. Black-Scholes pricing from VIX/VIX3M, with a SKEW tilt as a sensitivity. Revalue at T1; paired bootstrap; walk-forward halves.
trial.data: SPY closes, VIX, VIX3M, SKEW, FRED 3-month bill
trial.pass: Difference > 0 with the 95% CI excluding 0 in both halves, holding with and without the SKEW tilt
trial.controls: VIX is a 30-day variance-swap index that sits above 30-day ATM IV, so this trial is model-priced, not market-priced. Costs on eight fills vs four. Max-loss normalisation uses the realised far-wing value at T1.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Two-expiry simulator with four delta-ruled legs. Run an iron-condor control leg set in the same pass and report the paired difference.

strategies.name: Event (earnings / macro) calendar

legs.expiry_rule: near: first expiry after the event (<= 7 DTE)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At the front expiry just after the event: P&L(S) = V_far(S, T2-T1; sigma_T1_post) - max(S - K, 0) - D. The same tent as a long calendar, but the edge is in the entry. The event-week option carries an implied event move that inflates the front IV far above the back (a local inversion of the term structure). After the event the front IV collapses, while the back's IV falls much less (tastylive on IV crush around earnings).
strategies.max_profit: V_far(K, T2-T1; sigma_post) - D at S = K after the event, where sigma_post is typically the back IV minus the event's share of variance.
strategies.max_loss: D, when the realised event move carries S far from K. D is small when the front is sold rich.
strategies.breakevens: Two roots of V_far(S, T2-T1; sigma_post) - max(S - K, 0) = D. The distance from K is roughly the implied event move minus the IV-crush hit to the back leg.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative and large (the event move is the risk)
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive and large (the front's event premium decays within days)
greeks_at_inception.vega: net positive to a parallel shift (the back leg's vega dominates), while short the event variance concentrated in the front expiry

strategies.when_to_use: When the implied event move (front ATM straddle / spot) exceeds the name's historical realised event move by a margin and the front/back IV ratio is well above 1. Works on earnings (TSLA, NVDA, AAPL and other large caps), on FOMC/CPI weeks in SPY/TLT, and on macro or flow dates in IBIT.
strategies.risks: A realised move beyond the implied move loses the debit, which is the only cushion. The post-event IV crush also hits the back leg partially. Pin risk on the event-week expiry. Early assignment if the stock gaps through K before expiry. Thin liquidity in the event-week expiry on smaller names.
strategies.margin_note: Debit calendar: defined risk, IRA-eligible. The short leg must expire no later than the long.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit dailies (any day, including weekends, at 08:00 UTC) and weeklies let the front leg sit just after a scheduled macro print or decision. BTC has no earnings; its events are CPI/FOMC, ETF-flow announcements and protocol dates. The event premium shows up as a kink in the chain's mark_iv by expiry (DVOL is 30-day only and will not show it). European cash settlement means no assignment risk; inverse premium is in coin.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: FOMC/NFP/CPI weeks inflate the front weekly options on the active futures month, and weekly GC options give precise post-event expiries. The far leg references the same futures month if both expiries fall within it; otherwise the futures spread enters. 1256. GLD/SLV weeklies for the same trade. CME pages returned 403 this session.
variants: Event double calendar (OTM strikes on both sides)
Event diagonal (directional lean into the print)
Reverse event calendar (buy the event, sell the back) when the front is cheap vs history
FOMC/CPI calendar on SPY/TLT (about 20 events a year)
IBIT calendar around ETF-flow and macro dates
strategies.claim: Across earnings events in the 10 most option-active US single stocks (including TSLA, NVDA, AAPL), the ATM calendar sold in the event-week expiry and bought in the next monthly has positive mean P&L as a percentage of debit when the front straddle's implied move is at least 1.25 times the trailing 8-quarter median realised earnings move.

trial.statistic: Mean P&L/debit across qualifying events (implied/realised ratio >= 1.25)
trial.null: Zero mean (bootstrap across events); for the placebo, ratios are permuted across events
trial.procedure: For each event, capture front and back ATM IVs and the straddle on the close before the event. Realised move = |log(close_after/close_before)|. Revalue the back leg at the front expiry from the captured post-event IV. Bootstrap across events; tercile monotonicity as a diagnostic.
trial.data: Daily CBOE chain captures (from 2026-10-14) for the 10 names plus SPY/TLT; earnings and FOMC/CPI calendars (free IR pages, SEC 8-K, Federal Reserve schedule; not yet ingested); daily closes
trial.pass: Mean > 0 with the 95% CI excluding 0 over at least 40 qualifying events
trial.controls: Exclude events with concurrent M&A or guidance shocks. Compare with the plain short front straddle to test whether the back leg earns its cost. Costs from captured spreads. Trailing realised moves need 8 quarters of closes (available).

strategies.blocked_on: Daily chain capture spanning at least 40 qualifying events. With 10 names (about 40 earnings a year), and only the high-ratio subset qualifying, that takes roughly 18-24 months of captures (TSLA/NVDA/AAPL alone would take about 3+ years). Paid chain history (ORATS/ThetaData) would unblock it now. An earnings-calendar ingest is also needed.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Tag chain captures with event dates; store per-capture front/back ATM IV and the straddle-implied move in the surface file, so the test runs itself once n is reached.

strategies.name: Horizontal time butterfly (same strike, three expiries)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At the near expiry T1: P&L(S) = max(S - K, 0) - 2*V_mid(S, T2-T1) + V_far(S, T3-T1) - D, where D = C30 - 2*C60 + C90. ATM premium scales with sqrt(T), which is concave, so D is about 0 and usually a small credit (Black-Scholes at 16% IV: a 0.18 credit per 100). At S = K the near call expires worthless while the mid shorts hold the most time value, so P&L is lowest there. Far from K all three legs converge to intrinsic or zero and P&L tends to -D (the credit kept). The economic exposure is the curvature of the IV term structure: the trade gains if 60-day IV falls relative to the 30- and 90-day IVs.
strategies.max_profit: About -D (the entry credit) on a large move either way by T1, plus any flattening of curvature (mid IV falling relative to the wings) before exit.
strategies.max_loss: At S = K at T1: 2*V_mid(K, T2-T1) - V_far(K, T3-T1) + D. For flat IV this is about (2*sqrt(30) - sqrt(60))/sqrt(30) = 0.59 times a 30-day ATM call. It is larger if the mid expiry's IV rises relative to the far.
strategies.breakevens: Two roots at T1 of max(S-K, 0) - 2*V_mid(S) + V_far(S) = D, one each side of K. They depend on IVs at T1 (model required).

greeks_at_inception.theta: negative (-1.8 per year per 100 of notional)
greeks_at_inception.vega: slightly negative to parallel shifts (-1.1, since sqrt(30) + sqrt(90) < 2*sqrt(60)); mainly short mid-expiry vega, long wing vega (a curvature trade)

strategies.when_to_use: When the middle of the term structure is humped (an event priced into the mid expiry, or a bulge from hedging demand) and the hump is expected to flatten; also as a cheap long-gamma structure funded by selling the mid expiry. Johnson finds the second principal component (slope) carries nearly all the term structure's information on variance premia, which is a prior that pure curvature trades earn little.
strategies.risks: A quiet market to T1 near K is the worst case. The mid IV can rise further (an event moves closer to the mid expiry). Six contracts of costs. After T1 the remaining -2 mid / +1 far is a short ratio calendar with naked upside risk unless it is closed.
strategies.margin_note: The two long wings cover the two mid shorts only partly by expiry order: the far long covers one short; the near long expires first and leaves one mid short covered only by the far. Brokers typically margin it as one calendar (mid short vs far long) plus one reverse calendar (near long vs mid short), with the second short treated as naked after T1. Close at T1.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit lists many expiries (dailies, weeklies, monthlies, quarterlies), and BTC's term structure often humps around scheduled events or a quarterly expiry, so curvature trades are natural there. Build curvature from mark_iv at three expiries in each capture (from today forward). Inverse premium is in coin; standard margin treats the mid shorts individually.

strategies.name: Jelly roll (synthetic time spread / financing trade)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: A long jelly roll is a long far synthetic (long call / short put at K, T2) plus a short near synthetic (short call / long put at K, T1); it is the same as a long call calendar plus a short put calendar. At T1 the near synthetic settles to -(S - K), and the far synthetic is worth S - K*exp(-r*tau) - PV(dividends in (T1, T2)) (European, no early exercise). Value at T1 = K(1 - exp(-r*tau)) - PV(div), independent of S. Fair value at entry: D* = K(exp(-r*T1) - exp(-r*T2)) - PV0(dividends between T1 and T2).
strategies.max_profit: D* - D in present-value terms (fair carry minus price paid), locked at entry absent early exercise or dividend surprises; no dependence on spot.
strategies.max_loss: D - D*, plus early-assignment and dividend-change risk on the American short legs (a deep-ITM short put may be assigned early for interest; a short ITM call before ex-dividend), plus pin risk at T1 if S is near K.
strategies.breakevens: None in spot. The trade breaks even when the realised carry (rates and dividends over (T1, T2)) equals the price paid.

greeks_at_inception.theta: about 0 apart from the carry accrual
greeks_at_inception.vega: about 0. The live sensitivities are rho (positive for the long roll: d/dr = K(T2*e^(-r*T2) - T1*e^(-r*T1)) > 0) and dividends (negative).

strategies.when_to_use: To lend or borrow at the option-implied rate, to move a synthetic position between expiries (roll a long synthetic forward), or to take a view on dividends or rates (Wikipedia: used to position on dividends or interest rates, or to profit from mispriced calendar spreads). Also a no-arbitrage check on a chain.
strategies.risks: Early assignment on the short legs converts the structure into stock plus options, with margin consequences. Dividend changes between T1 and T2 move fair value one-for-one. Pin risk at T1. Four-leg execution slippage usually exceeds the theoretical edge. Under Reg T the short legs may be margined as naked options.
strategies.margin_note: Portfolio margin (and SPX/XSP in particular) recognises the near-zero risk; Reg T accounts may require naked-short margin on the short legs, which kills the economics. SPX/XSP jelly rolls are 1256 contracts and European (no early exercise).
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit the jelly roll trades the futures basis/funding between two expiries rather than r - q: fair value is K times the difference in the two expiries' discount factors implied by the futures, with no dividends. European settlement removes early exercise, so deviations are purer; inverse premium denominates the carry in coin. Deribit lists option_combo instruments, and public/get_delivery_prices gives the settlement series for checking realised carry (Deribit options data guide).
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: a jelly roll across futures months is a synthetic futures calendar spread whose fair value is the futures spread (gold carry = rate - lease rate), so deviations measure option-vs-futures mispricing; 1256. GLD/SLV: no dividends, so fair value is K(exp(-r*T1) - exp(-r*T2)); American exercise adds a small early-exercise premium on deep-ITM puts. CME pages returned 403 this session.

strategies.name: LEAPS collar (long-dated put, serial short calls)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At each short-call expiry T1: P&L(S) = (S - S0) + V_put(S, T2-T1; sigma_T1) - max(S - Kc, 0) + sum of call credits - P_put. At the put's expiry, with all shorts expired OTM, this is the standard collar payoff: floor at Kp, cap at the last Kc (OIC collar).
strategies.max_profit: Per cycle: Kc - S0 + C_t + V_put(Kc) - P_put. Over the put's life: (Kc - S0) + sum of credits - P_put, if the stock finishes at or above the final Kc (OIC: call strike - stock purchase price + net credit, or - net debit).
strategies.max_loss: S0 - Kp + P_put - sum of credits, if S <= Kp at the put's expiry (OIC: stock purchase price - put strike + net premium paid).
strategies.breakevens: S0 + P_put - sum of call credits (OIC: breaks even when the stock is above its initial level by the net debit); falls each month as credits accumulate.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative at inception (the 30-DTE short call's gamma is about 4 times the 12-month put's; Black-Scholes: -0.058 per 100 of notional). It turns positive only if S falls toward Kp after the call has been rolled away.
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive (fast decay of the monthly call vs slow decay of the 12-month put)
greeks_at_inception.vega: positive (the long-dated put's vega far exceeds the near call's; +21.8 in the example). A same-expiry collar with these deltas has near-zero vega.

strategies.when_to_use: Protect a concentrated or low-basis position with a long-dated floor that is cheap per day, financed by serial monthly calls. It exploits the term structure of theta: the 365-DTE put loses time value far more slowly than the 30-DTE calls sold against it.
strategies.risks: A strong rally caps gains at each Kc while the put's value evaporates. After a sell-off the put is ITM but rolling it resets the floor at a higher cost. An IV collapse hurts the long put. Early assignment on the short call before ex-dividend. The monthly credits may not cover the put's annual cost in low-IV regimes.
strategies.margin_note: Long stock plus long put plus covered call: no margin beyond the stock; IRA-eligible; the short call is covered by the shares. The synthetic version (LEAPS call instead of stock) is a debit structure, also IRA-eligible.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit: the collar is built with options against BTC held as collateral. An inverse put pays out in BTC, whose USD value falls in exactly the scenario it hedges, so buy more notional or use USDC linear puts. The longest puts are about 11-month quarterlies (furthest expiry today 2027-09-24). Monthly and weekly calls expire on Fridays at 08:00 UTC. No dividends, and European settlement removes assignment risk. IBIT holders can run the exact US equity version.
strategies.metals_notes: GC: collar the futures with a deferred-month put and front-month calls (American exercise; SPAN nets the hedged position); 1256. GLD/SLV: equity-style collar on the shares, no dividends. GLD/SLV gains held over a year are taxed as collectibles, and a protective put can interact with the straddle rules (a tax question outside this scope). CME pages returned 403 this session.

trial.pass: Sharpe difference > 0 with the 95% CI excluding 0 in both halves

A flat smile underprices the OTM put: rerun with a SKEW-index tilt. Dividends are credited to the stock leg in both strategies.

strategies.name: Long calendar (horizontal) spread
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Evaluated at the front expiry T1, while the far leg is still alive: P&L(S) = V_far(S, T2-T1; sigma_T1) - max(S-K, 0) - D, where V_far is the Black-Scholes value of the far call with T2-T1 remaining at the IV prevailing then, and D is the net debit. The shape is a tent: the slope is +delta_far below K and delta_far - 1 above K, so the peak is exactly at S = K, and it falls toward -D far from K. The put version is the same with max(K-S, 0) (OIC long put calendar).
strategies.max_profit: V_far(K, T2-T1; sigma_T1) - D at S = K on the front expiry. It depends on the IV at T1 and is not known in advance (OIC: maximum gain at the strike of the expiring option; Options Playbook: risk cannot be calculated precisely at initiation). If the near leg expires worthless and the far call is kept, upside is unlimited (OIC).
strategies.max_loss: D (net debit), when both legs reach parity: S far below K (both near zero) or far above K (both near intrinsic) (OIC). Caveat for European-style puts (SPX/XSP, Deribit): a deep-ITM far put is worth K*e^(-r*tau) - S*e^(-q*tau), which is less than K - S, so a put calendar can lose about K(1 - e^(-r*tau)) - S(1 - e^(-q*tau)) beyond D (Black-Scholes: about 0.33 per 100 of strike at r = 4%, tau = 30 days, S = 50).
strategies.breakevens: Two roots at T1, both depending on IV then (no closed form; OIC and tastylive: the breakeven cannot be computed in advance). Lower S_L < K where V_far(S_L, T2-T1) = D (the far call's whole value equals the debit). Upper S_U > K where V_far(S_U) - (S_U - K) = D (the far call's time value equals the debit).

greeks_at_inception.delta: about 0, slightly positive for a spot-ATM call calendar because the far call's N(d1) exceeds the near call's (Black-Scholes at S = K = 100, 16% IV, 30/60 DTE, r = 4%: +0.016)
greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative (near-leg gamma exceeds far-leg gamma; -0.026 in the same example)
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive while S is near K; turns negative once S moves far from K, and once the near leg has expired the remaining long call decays (OIC)
greeks_at_inception.vega: positive (far vega is larger, roughly in proportion to sqrt(T): +4.6 per 1.00 of vol in the example; OIC: a rise in IV is 'extremely positive')

strategies.when_to_use: A neutral forecast around K for the front cycle, with low absolute IV that is expected to rise (tastylive: lowest-IV environments; take profits at about 25% of the debit, ideal range 10-25%), or when front IV is rich relative to the back (flat or inverted term structure). OIC's outlook: steady to slightly declining during the near option, then a move higher, or a sharp rise in IV. Johnson (JFQA 2017) finds that the slope of the VIX term structure prices variance risk rather than forecasting the VIX. A steep contango therefore argues against buying the back month, and so against this trade. The abstract states only that the slope predicts returns; the sign is taken from the paper's body.
strategies.risks: A large move either way loses the debit. A fall in IV hurts (long vega). Early assignment on the short near call before an ex-dividend date leaves a one-day short-stock position (OIC). There is pin risk at the front expiry. After T1 the position is a naked long option with its own theta bleed unless the near leg is re-sold (campaign) or the position is closed. Near and far legs usually trade at different IVs (OIC), so the term-structure spread at entry is part of the trade.
strategies.margin_note: The debit is paid in full. Options Playbook: 'After the trade is paid for, no additional margin is required if the position is closed at expiration of the front-month option.' It is defined-risk while the long outlives the short and is IRA-eligible at most brokers.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit options are European and cash-settled against a 30-minute TWAP delivery price (public/get_delivery_prices). Every expiry is at 08:00 UTC. Dailies cover non-Friday days too: the live public/get_instruments call today lists Thu 15 Oct, Sat 17 Oct and Sun 18 Oct 2026. Weeklies and monthlies expire on Fridays. The settlement_period values are day, week and month (quarterlies are tagged month), and the furthest expiry listed today is 2027-09-24. Inverse BTC/ETH options denominate both debit and P&L in coin, so the premium carries coin exposure. USDC-settled linear options are also listed (BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, AVAX, TRX, HYPE) for a USD-denominated calendar. There are no dividends, so no ex-dividend assignment problem. 24/7 trading means weekend theta is real. Unverified this session: standard margin is believed to margin each short option on its own, with calendar offsets mainly under Portfolio Margin. DVOL is 30-day only, so the term-structure slope must be built from chain mark_iv (get_book_summary_by_currency kind=option).
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: American-style options on futures. When the near and far options sit on different futures months, the calendar also carries the futures spread (gold contango is roughly the rate minus the lease rate). Serial options on the same futures month avoid this. Short legs are SPAN-margined with spread recognition. These are Section 1256 contracts (26 USC 1256(b)(1)(A) for futures and (C) for nonequity options), taxed 60/40 with year-end mark-to-market. GLD/SLV are the equity-option route: weeklies, physical delivery of ETF shares, no dividends (so no ex-dividend assignment risk), and not 1256. CME spec pages returned 403 again this session, so expiry and exercise details come from training knowledge.

trial.statistic: Difference in mean P&L/debit to the front expiry between entries with VIX/VIX3M >= 1.0 and entries with VIX/VIX3M <= 0.9
trial.null: No regime difference: the VIX/VIX3M regime label is circularly block-shifted against the P&L series
trial.procedure: Run from 2007-12-04, the first VIX3M date (verified in FRED VXVCLS). On each trading day, price 30- and 60-DTE ATM calls with Black-Scholes (front IV = VIX; back IV from the total-variance interpolation w(60) = w(30) + (w(93) - w(30))*(60-30)/(93-30), where w = IV^2*T). Hold 21 trading days, then revalue the far leg at the IV interpolated that day and the SPY close. Use a studentized block bootstrap (block 21) on the daily series, a plain bootstrap on non-overlapping monthly entries, deflation for the thresholds tested, and walk-forward halves.
trial.data: SPY daily closes, CBOE VIX and VIX3M daily history, FRED 3-month bill rate (all free and in the data list)
trial.pass: Regime difference > 0 with p < 0.05 after deflating for thresholds (0.9/0.95/1.0), with the same sign in both walk-forward halves. A sensitivity rerun at today's measured SPY 30/60-DTE ATM IV spread from the chain capture.
trial.controls: VIX is a 30-day variance-swap index that sits above 30-day ATM IV because it includes the skew, so using VIX as ATM IV overstates premium levels. This trial is model-priced, not market-priced, and runs on a flat smile. The verdict stays 'model-only' until at least 120 daily chain captures confirm the real front-vs-back ATM IV spread. Costs and pin risk at T1 are modelled by closing both legs at mid minus half the spread. Backwardation entries cluster in 2008, 2011, 2020 and 2022, so report the result with each of those episodes left out.

strategies.name: Long diagonal spread (bullish call / bearish put)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At the front expiry T1, with K1 < K2: P&L(S) = V_far(S, T2-T1; sigma_T1) - max(S-K2, 0) - D. The curve rises with S up to K2 (peak at K2). Above K2 it does not flatten but declines slowly as the far call's extrinsic shrinks, toward (K2 - K1) + K1(1 - e^(-r*tau)) - D for very large S. It falls toward -D as S collapses.
strategies.max_profit: (K2 - K1) + extrinsic_far(K2, T2-T1) - D at S = K2 on the front expiry. This can exceed the strike width minus the debit because the long keeps its time value (tastylive).
strategies.max_loss: D (net debit), if S <= K1 and the far call later expires worthless (tastylive: the max loss is the debit, realised if the long expires OTM). Upside asymptote at T1 is (K2 - K1) - D plus carry. It is non-negative only if D <= K2 - K1. tastylive's rule is D <= 75% of the width.
strategies.breakevens: Lower: S* where V_far(S*, T2-T1) = D, roughly K1 + D - the remaining extrinsic. Upper: none when D <= K2 - K1; otherwise S** above K2 where V_far(S**) - (S** - K2) = D. Both need a pricing model (Options Playbook: no exact formula).

greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative: the near 0.30-delta gamma is about sqrt(T2/T1) = 1.7 times the far 0.70-delta gamma (Black-Scholes at 16% IV: -0.032 net)
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive (near short decays faster; +2.7 per year per 100 of notional in the example)
greeks_at_inception.vega: positive (far vega is about 1.7 times near vega; +7.3 in the example)

strategies.when_to_use: Moderately bullish (calls) or bearish (puts), with elevated near-term IV (event week) or a flat or inverted term structure. It suits a trader who wants a vertical with positive theta and long vega, and a two-step forecast: first neutral up to K2, then higher. tastylive setup rules: the short premium should be at least the long's extrinsic, and the debit at most 75% of the strike width. At the stated 0.70/0.30 deltas, Black-Scholes prices fail both rules at normal SPY IVs (at 16% IV: short premium 0.85 vs long extrinsic 2.53, debit/width 0.79), so in practice move the long deeper (0.80+) or the short closer (0.35-0.40).
strategies.risks: An IV collapse hurts the far leg. A sharp early rally through K2 caps gains while the far leg's extrinsic shrinks. Early assignment on the short when ITM before ex-dividend. Rolling the short up and out for a debit can push the total debit past the width. tastylive never trades diagonals on volatility products, because each expiry is its own underlying and the max loss is undefined.
strategies.margin_note: Debit spread: pay D in full. Brokers require the long expiry to be at or after the short's, and the long strike no higher than the short strike for calls (no lower for puts), for defined-risk treatment; otherwise the short is margined naked.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit strikes come in fixed USD steps, and all expiries are at 08:00 UTC: dailies on any day, weeklies and monthlies on Fridays. With inverse premium, the coin cost of the ITM long rises as BTC falls, so the premium itself has convexity in coin terms. USDC linear options avoid this. There are no dividends and settlement is European, so there is no assignment risk. With 24/7 trading the near short decays through weekends. Portfolio Margin is needed for spread-level margin. BTC's call skew is often flat to positive, so call diagonals are relatively dearer than on SPY.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: the far long and near short may reference different futures months. Exercise is American, so the short can be exercised into a futures position. SPAN gives spread credit; 1256 60/40 applies. GLD/SLV are equity options with weeklies, well suited to 7-DTE short vs 60-DTE long diagonals. SLV's upside call skew makes put diagonals cheaper than call diagonals. CME pages returned 403 this session.
