strategies.name: Poor man's covered call (PMCC / LEAPS diagonal)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At each short expiry T1, with K1 < K2: P&L(S) = V_leaps(S, T2-T1; sigma_T1) - max(S-K2, 0) + sum of credits collected - P_leaps. The shape of a covered call whose 'stock' is the LEAPS: it rises with S to K2, then declines slowly above K2 as the LEAPS extrinsic shrinks, and falls toward -(P_leaps - credits) as S drops below K1.
strategies.max_profit: Per cycle, at S = K2 on the short expiry: (K2 - K1) + extrinsic_leaps(K2, T2-T1) - D, where D = P_leaps - C_short (tastylive: hard to estimate before the long's expiry because the long keeps extrinsic value).
strategies.max_loss: P_leaps minus all credits collected, if S <= K1 at the LEAPS expiry; per single cycle D = P_leaps - C_short. A 0.80-delta 1-year LEAPS costs about 15-25% of the stock price (Black-Scholes at r = 4%: 14.8% at 18% IV, 22.6% at 30% IV). Options Playbook: look at least 20% ITM for 0.80 delta on volatile names.
strategies.breakevens: On a short expiry: S* where V_leaps(S*, T2-T1) = D, roughly K1 + D - the remaining LEAPS extrinsic. At LEAPS expiry: K1 + P_leaps - total credits. tastylive entry guards: short premium at least the LEAPS extrinsic, and total debit at most 75% of the strike width.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative (the 30-45 DTE short's gamma far exceeds the LEAPS's; Black-Scholes: -0.055 per 100 of notional)
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive in most setups (the short decays faster than the LEAPS), although the LEAPS still loses its extrinsic over a year if the stock is flat
greeks_at_inception.vega: positive (LEAPS vega far exceeds the short's; +17 in the example). This makes it a long-vega covered call, the opposite of the stock-based covered call (Options Playbook: an IV drop can deflate the LEAPS even if the stock has not moved).

strategies.when_to_use: A capital-efficient covered call on a bullish-to-neutral view; best when long-dated IV is low (cheap LEAPS) and front IV is relatively rich. It is a term-structure trade in theta per day: sell fast-decaying front extrinsic against slow-decaying LEAPS extrinsic.
strategies.risks: An IV collapse deflates the LEAPS even if the stock is flat. The short caps the upside, so the PMCC lags the stock in a strong rally. Assignment on the short leaves short stock, and exercising the LEAPS to cover forfeits its extrinsic. The LEAPS receives no dividends. Options Playbook: roll the short before it is about 2-4% ITM; rolling up costs a debit, and rolling out may earn a credit. Rolling for debits can push the total debit past the width. tastylive never runs PMCCs on volatility products.
strategies.margin_note: Debit paid in full. Treated as a diagonal spread (defined risk) and IRA-eligible when the long expiry is later than the short's and K1 <= K2; no stock-level margin needed.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit's furthest expiry today is 2027-09-24 (about 11 months), so the 'LEAPS' is the furthest quarterly. With inverse premium, the deep-ITM long's coin cost rises as BTC falls; USDC linear options avoid this. There are no dividends, and European settlement removes early assignment. Portfolio Margin is needed for spread-level margin. Weekend theta on the front short helps the seller. IBIT options (US-listed, American, no dividend) give the equity-style route with SPY-like mechanics.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: long-dated options on deferred futures months (thin beyond about 6-9 months), American exercise, SPAN spread margin, 1256. The long and short may reference different futures, so the structure carries the gold forward curve. GLD/SLV: LEAPS out to about 2 years and no dividends, so the PMCC transfers cleanly; they are equity options, not 1256. CME pages returned 403 this session.
variants: Poor man's covered put (bearish): long ITM LEAPS put, short OTM near puts
PMCC with weekly shorts (7 DTE) for faster extrinsic capture
PMCC + long put = LEAPS collar (separate entry)
ZEBRA-covered call: replace the single LEAPS with a 2:1 ZEBRA for about 100 delta
strategies.claim: On SPY, a PMCC (0.80-delta 12-month LEAPS replaced at 90 DTE, plus a monthly 0.30-delta short call) does not have a higher annualised Sharpe ratio, measured on capital deployed, than the stock-based covered call with the same short-call rule, model-priced (LEAPS IV = VIX3M, short IV = VIX).

trial.statistic: Difference in annualised Sharpe (PMCC minus covered call), monthly returns on capital deployed
trial.null: Sharpe(PMCC) > Sharpe(CC): the claim is falsified if the paired-bootstrap 95% CI of the difference lies entirely above 0
trial.procedure: Monthly rebalance since 2007-12, Black-Scholes pricing and daily mark-to-model, roll rules as in the claim. Paired block bootstrap of the Sharpe difference (run.py _sharpe_diff_p); walk-forward halves. Sensitivity at today's SPY 12-month ATM IV vs VIX3M from the chain capture.
trial.data: SPY closes and dividends, VIX, VIX3M, FRED 3-month bill
trial.pass: The claim survives if the CI of the Sharpe difference includes 0 or lies below it in both halves; return on capital and drawdown are also reported
trial.controls: VIX is a 30-day variance-swap index that sits above 30-day ATM IV, and VIX3M (93-day) is a coarse proxy for 365-day IV (sensitivity +/-3 vol points), so this trial is model-priced, not market-priced. The covered call receives dividends and the PMCC does not. Costs on monthly rolls.

strategies.harness_suggestion: A roll-schedule simulator shared with the diagonals. Add a 'capital deployed' denominator option (debit vs stock price) to overlay_verdict, so return on capital and absolute return are both reported.

strategies.name: Ratio (vega-weighted) calendar spread
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At the front expiry T1, with n near shorts per far long (n = vega_far/vega_near, about sqrt(T2/T1) = 1.73 for ATM 30/90; 2:1 in practice): P&L(S) = V_far(S, T2-T1) - n*max(S-K, 0) - D. Because both ATM premium and ATM vega scale with sqrt(T), the vega-neutral ATM ratio costs almost nothing: D is about 0 (Black-Scholes at 16% IV: a debit of 0.21 per 100). The tent peaks at K and falls with slope -(n-1) on the upside.
strategies.max_profit: V_far(K, T2-T1; sigma_T1) - D at S = K on the front expiry.
strategies.max_loss: Downside: D (about 0), when S is far below K. Upside: unlimited. At T1 the n near calls settle at n(S-K) while the far call is worth about (S-K) + extrinsic, so the loss is (n-1)(S-K) - extrinsic_far(S) + D, growing without bound in S. A gap before T1 is worse.
strategies.breakevens: Lower: V_far(S, T2-T1) = D (none if entered for a credit). Upper: V_far(S, T2-T1) - n(S-K) = D, i.e. n(S-K) - V_far(S) = -D.

greeks_at_inception.delta: negative for the call version (Black-Scholes: -0.37 per far contract at n = 1.73); positive for the put version
greeks_at_inception.gamma: strongly negative (n times the near gamma, about 3 times the far gamma)
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive and large (+14.3 per year per 100 of notional in the example, vs +3.3 for the 1:1 calendar)
greeks_at_inception.vega: about 0 by construction to parallel shifts (-0.18 in the example). This holds only at inception: by T1 the near legs have no vega, so the position held to T1 carries the far leg's full remaining vega.

strategies.when_to_use: Harvest front-month theta while flat to instantaneous parallel IV shifts, i.e. express 'front realised < front implied' without a bet on the IV level; attractive when the term structure is flat or inverted. To stay vega-neutral it must be re-sized or closed well before T1. The opposite back-ratio (long more far than near) is a long-gamma, long-vega structure.
strategies.risks: Uncovered shorts: a gap through K before T1 loses many multiples of any credit. Vega neutrality holds only for parallel shifts: VIX moves more than VIX3M (front steepening in a spike), which leaves the structure short front vol exactly when gamma also loses. Pin and assignment risk on n short options. The excess shorts are margined as naked.
strategies.margin_note: The n-1 excess short options are margined as naked (Reg T about 20% of the underlying each; portfolio margin far less on SPX). Not permitted in most IRAs. The 1:1 portion is a calendar spread.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit BTC options trade in 0.1-contract steps (min_trade_amount = 0.1 on all 894 BTC options listed today), so the 1.73:1 ratio can be set as 1.7:1. Standard margin charges the shorts individually, so the structure is collateral-heavy outside Portfolio Margin. With 24/7 gaps, the uncovered front shorts are riskier than on SPY.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: SPAN margins the uncovered shorts against the futures scan range; near and far legs may reference different futures months; 1256. GLD/SLV: equity-option naked margin on the excess shorts. CME pages returned 403 this session.
variants: 2:1 call ratio calendar (practical rounding of the vega ratio)
Back-ratio calendar: long about sqrt(T2/T1) far / short 1 near for theta-neutral, long-gamma, long-vega (2:1 at 30/90 is slightly theta-negative)
Diagonal ratio: OTM shorts in the near, ATM long in the far
strategies.claim: Re-sized to vega-neutral at each weekly entry and held 5 trading days, the SPY 30/90-DTE ATM ratio call calendar has weekly P&L whose absolute Spearman correlation with the weekly change in VIX is below 0.3, model-priced (VIX/VIX3M term interpolation).

trial.statistic: Spearman correlation of 5-day P&L with delta-VIX over the same 5 days
trial.procedure: Weekly entries since 2007-12. Black-Scholes pricing with front IV = VIX and back IV from the VIX/VIX3M total-variance interpolation; n set from model vegas at entry. Revalue after 5 trading days with the new interpolated IVs and SPY close. Block bootstrap (block 4 weeks); walk-forward halves. The 1:1 calendar is the comparison.
trial.data: SPY closes, VIX, VIX3M, FRED 3-month bill
trial.pass: Upper bound of the 95% CI of |rho| < 0.3 in both halves
trial.controls: VIX is a 30-day variance-swap index that sits above 30-day ATM IV, so this trial is model-priced, not market-priced. Gamma losses co-move with VIX spikes, so also report the correlation of the delta-hedged P&L. Separate top-decile VIX-spike weeks. Costs on 2.7 fills.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Fractional qty already works in Leg. Add a sizing hook that sets qty from model vegas at entry, and a short-horizon revaluation step in the two-expiry simulator.

strategies.name: Rolling a short option (out / up / down / in)

legs.strike_rule: K (the existing short put; 'tested' = delta beyond -0.30)
same K (roll out) or lower K2 (roll out-and-down)
legs.expiry_rule: far: next monthly, ~49 DTE (sell to open)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: The roll itself is a calendar/diagonal trade whose cash flow is Prem(K2, T2) - Prem(K, T1) (a credit when positive). The rolled position's payoff at T2 is that of the new short. For a put: cumulative net credits - max(K2 - S, 0). For a call: cumulative net credits - max(S - K2, 0). tastylive's terminology: roll out = later expiry, same strike; roll up/down = strike higher/lower; roll in = strike moved closer to the stock price (not shorter time).
strategies.max_profit: Sum of all net credits collected across rolls, if the final short expires OTM.
strategies.max_loss: Put: K2 - cumulative net credits. Call: unbounded when naked, capped by the shares in a covered call. Rolling moves risk in time; it does not remove it.
strategies.breakevens: Put: K2 - cumulative net credits. Call: K2 + cumulative net credits. Each credit roll moves the breakeven further from spot; each debit roll moves it closer.

greeks_at_inception.delta: roll out at the same strike: |delta| stays about the same, or grows for an OTM short (longer-dated OTM options have larger delta). Only rolling out-and-away (down for puts, up for calls) reduces |delta|.
greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative, and smaller after moving out in time
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive, but smaller per day than the 21-DTE short it replaces (more extrinsic, slower decay)
greeks_at_inception.vega: negative, and larger in magnitude after moving to the longer expiry

strategies.when_to_use: Defend a tested short (roll out, or out-and-away, for a credit) to re-centre the breakeven and buy time. Roll an untested strangle side in toward spot to collect premium. Roll a covered call up and out when the stock rallies through the strike (Options Playbook: consider rolling before it is about 2-4% ITM; rolling up usually costs a debit, rolling further out may earn a credit). Roll winners at 21 DTE to the next cycle (tastylive's 21-DTE management).
strategies.risks: Rolling for a debit adds risk without new premium. Repeated rolls of a losing short can accumulate a large loss and tie up margin for months. Rolling a defined-risk spread can push the debit past the width. Early assignment can pre-empt the roll. Each roll is two fills of slippage.
strategies.margin_note: Naked shorts remain margined as naked and covered calls remain covered. Rolling out in time usually raises Reg T margin; portfolio margin is more forgiving.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit: every expiry is at 08:00 UTC, with dailies on any weekday or weekend day, so rolls can target a specific day. European settlement means no early assignment pre-empts a roll. Inverse premium credits are in coin. 24/7 trading lets a tested short be rolled on a weekend gap (thinner liquidity). The two legs are margined separately under standard margin.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: rolling out in time may mean rolling to an option on a different futures month (the futures spread moves the effective strike). American exercise can assign a deep-ITM short early. SPAN; 1256. GLD/SLV: equity-style rolls with weeklies. CME pages returned 403 this session.
variants: Roll up / roll down (strike only, same expiry)
Roll in: strike moved toward spot (tastylive)
Roll a vertical spread as a unit
Roll a long LEAPS at ~90 DTE
strategies.claim: For a 0.16-delta 45-DTE SPY short put that is tested (delta beyond -0.30) at 21 DTE, rolling it out at the same strike to the next monthly does not produce a higher mean P&L per day than closing it and opening a fresh 0.16-delta 45-DTE put, model-priced (VIX as IV).

trial.statistic: Mean P&L per day held, roll path minus close-and-reset path, paired by entry
trial.null: Roll path P&L/day > reset path. The claim is falsified if the paired-bootstrap 95% CI of the difference lies entirely above 0.
trial.procedure: Daily entries since 1993-01-29 (SPY inception; VIX exists from 1990, but SPY prices do not). Black-Scholes pricing from VIX. At 21 DTE apply the 'tested' trigger; simulate both paths to the next cycle's 21-DTE exit. Paired block bootstrap; walk-forward halves.
trial.data: SPY closes, VIX, FRED 3-month bill
trial.pass: The claim survives if the CI of (roll - reset) includes 0 or lies below it in both halves; the variance ratio is reported
trial.controls: VIX is a 30-day variance-swap index that sits above 30-day ATM IV and has no skew, so this trial is model-priced, not market-priced; rerun with a SKEW tilt. Both paths pay the same number of fills. Margin-time cost charged at the bill rate.

strategies.harness_suggestion: A roll-schedule simulator with conditional actions on delta/DTE triggers; express roll vs reset as two action lists over the same price path.

strategies.name: Short (reverse) calendar spread
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At the front expiry T1: P&L(S) = C + max(S-K, 0) - V_far(S, T2-T1; sigma_T1), where C is the net credit. An inverted tent: the trough is at S = K, and P&L approaches +C when S is far from K.
strategies.max_profit: About C (net credit), reached when both options reach parity: S far below K (both near zero) or far above K (both near intrinsic) (OIC). Deep in the money the far call keeps carry of about K(1 - e^(-r*tau)), so the realised gain is slightly below C.
strategies.max_loss: V_far(K, T2-T1; sigma_T1) - C at S = K on the front expiry: the cost to buy back the far option less the credit (OIC). This depends on IV at T1. If the near leg expires and the far short is left open, the call version is a naked call with unlimited loss and the put version a naked put losing up to K - C (OIC).
strategies.breakevens: Two roots at T1 of V_far(S*, T2-T1) - max(S*-K, 0) = C, one each side of K: that is, where the far option's time value equals the credit. Rising IV moves them further from K.

greeks_at_inception.delta: about 0 (slightly negative for a spot-ATM call version: -0.016 in the 16%-IV Black-Scholes example)
greeks_at_inception.theta: negative near K (OIC: the passage of time has a 'very negative' impact); turns slightly positive once S is far from K
greeks_at_inception.vega: negative (short the higher-vega far leg; OIC: a rise in IV is 'extremely negative')

strategies.when_to_use: OIC's outlook: a sharp move either way during the near option's life, or a sharp drop in IV. Also when the term structure is expected to flatten or invert (front IV rising relative to back). A steep contango, where the far variance carries a large premium (Johnson: the slope reflects variance risk premia), makes the far short the richer sale.
strategies.risks: If the stock sits at K, losses approach the far option's full time value. After the near leg expires, the far short is naked (unlimited for calls). The far short call can be assigned early near an ex-dividend date. Broker margin on the far short jumps when the near long expires. A volatility spike before T1 can cause 'substantial losses' (OIC).
strategies.margin_note: Credit structure, but the long leg expires first, so many brokers margin the far short as naked from the start, or at least from T1, and most do not allow it in IRAs. Risk is the naked far option after T1.
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit the far short needs its own collateral (standard margin is believed not to offset it against the nearer long; not verified this session), so the coin-denominated credit is small relative to collateral. The big-move thesis fits BTC's fat tails. Expiries are at 08:00 UTC (dailies include weekend days), with European cash settlement at TWAP, so the near long settles to cash at 08:00 UTC and leaves the far short naked automatically unless it is closed. Build the BTC term structure from chain mark IVs (DVOL is 30-day only).
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI options on futures: if the far short references a later futures month, after T1 you are short an American option on a different contract under SPAN margin. The metals term structure usually slopes mildly upward, so selling the back captures both the vol premium and the futures carry. GC/SI are 1256 contracts; GLD/SLV equity options are not. CME pages returned 403 this session.
variants: Reverse put calendar (OIC short put calendar: max loss strike minus credit once naked)
Reverse diagonal: long near OTM / short far ATM (credit, directional)
Pre-event reverse calendar: buy the event-week option, sell the next month when the back is rich
Short calendar as the cheap long-gamma leg around known dates (FOMC/CPI)
strategies.claim: A 30/60-DTE ATM SPY short call calendar, entered only on days when VIX3M/VIX >= 1.15 (steep contango) and closed at the front expiry, has positive mean P&L, model-priced (front IV = VIX, back IV = VIX/VIX3M total-variance interpolation).

trial.statistic: Mean P&L per conditional entry as a fraction of the far leg's premium
trial.null: Zero conditional mean (studentized block bootstrap); for the placebo, the regime label is block-shifted
trial.procedure: Daily entries since 2007-12-04 on days meeting the gate. Price with Black-Scholes from VIX/VIX3M. Revalue the far short at T1 (21 trading days) with the IV interpolated that day. Studentized block bootstrap (block 21), walk-forward halves, and deflation for the 1.10/1.15/1.20 thresholds.
trial.data: SPY closes, CBOE VIX, VIX3M, FRED 3-month bill
trial.pass: Conditional mean > 0 with the 95% CI excluding 0 in both halves after deflation, surviving removal of the five largest VIX-spike months
trial.controls: VIX is a 30-day variance-swap index that sits above 30-day ATM IV, so this trial is model-priced, not market-priced, and runs on a flat smile. A VIX-level tercile control checks that the result is not just a low-VIX effect. Unconditional entry is reported alongside. Cost is half the bid-ask on four fills, from today's SPY chain spreads.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Reuse calendar_model_backtest with the legs reversed and an entry mask from the VIX3M/VIX ratio. Report the conditional and unconditional means beside the existing term_structure_reversion output (experiments/volatility.py).

strategies.name: Straddle calendar (time spread of straddles / forward-vol trade)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At the front expiry T1: P&L(S) = V_far_straddle(S, T2-T1; sigma_T1) - |S - K| - D. A tent peaked at K whose height is the far straddle's time value. The economic exposure is forward volatility between T1 and T2: FV^2 = (T2*sigma_T2^2 - T1*sigma_T1^2)/(T2 - T1).
strategies.max_profit: V_far_straddle(K, T2-T1; sigma_T1) - D at S = K on the front expiry; it grows with the IV prevailing then.
strategies.max_loss: About D: on a large move the near straddle's intrinsic cancels the far straddle's intrinsic, leaving only the lost time value, plus or minus a small carry term on the ITM leg.
strategies.breakevens: K +/- x, where the far straddle's remaining time value at K +/- x equals D: V_far_straddle(K +/- x, T2-T1) - x = D.

greeks_at_inception.delta: about 0 (Black-Scholes at 16% IV, r = 4%: +0.06 from the drift in the far call's delta)
greeks_at_inception.vega: positive to parallel IV shifts: far vega is about sqrt(93/30) = 1.76 times near vega (+16.9 in the example). It is long forward volatility, and vega-neutral only if sized by the vega ratio (see ratio calendar).

strategies.when_to_use: Long version: when forward implied volatility between 30 and 93 days is low relative to the volatility expected over that window, or a vol shock is expected after T1. Reverse version (short far / long near, delta-hedged): to harvest a forward variance risk premium when forward implied exceeds subsequently realised variance.
strategies.risks: A realised move before T1 larger than the near straddle's premium. An IV collapse hurts the long version. Pin risk at K. Early assignment on short near legs (deep-ITM puts; calls before ex-dividend). The reverse version is short far vega and loses in a vol spike that outlasts the near long.
strategies.margin_note: Long version: debit paid, defined risk, IRA-eligible. Reverse version: the far short straddle is margined as naked once the near expires. SPX under portfolio margin is far cheaper than SPY under Reg T.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit lists dailies, weeklies, monthlies and quarterlies (08:00 UTC), so a 30/90-day straddle calendar maps onto a monthly vs a quarterly. With inverse premium, a USD view gets distorted by BTC's own move; hedge with a perpetual or use USDC linear options. DVOL gives only the 30-day point, so compute forward vol from the chain's ATM mark_iv at two expiries. Realised vol comes from public/get_historical_volatility.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: the two straddles may reference different futures months, so the forward-vol trade also carries the futures spread and the two months' different realised vols; SPAN spread credit; 1256. GLD/SLV are the cleanest pure forward-vol route on gold. GVZ (the CBOE gold ETF vol index) gives a 30-day point with no 3-month analogue. CME pages returned 403 this session.
variants: Reverse straddle calendar (short far / long near): a gamma-vs-vega swap that harvests the forward variance premium
Strangle calendar (OTM strikes; becomes the double calendar)
Delta-hedged version to isolate the forward-variance P&L
strategies.claim: The 30-to-93-day forward variance implied by VIX and VIX3M, FV = (93*VIX3M^2 - 30*VIX^2)/63, exceeds the realised SPY variance over trading days 21..63 after entry on average: a positive forward variance risk premium of more than 1 vol point.

trial.statistic: Mean of (sqrt(FV) - sqrt(RV_fwd)) in annualised vol points, where RV_fwd is the realised SPY variance over trading days 21..63; also the share of positive observations
trial.null: Zero mean forward premium (the expectations hypothesis holds for the 30-93 day segment)
trial.procedure: Daily since the first aligned VIX/VIX3M/SPY date. Compute FV from VIX and VIX3M in variance units and RV_fwd from SPY log returns. Studentized block bootstrap (block 63) on the overlapping daily series, a sign test on non-overlapping 63-day windows, walk-forward halves.
trial.data: CBOE VIX and VIX3M daily history, SPY daily closes (data-only: no option pricing)
trial.pass: Mean > 1 vol point with the one-sided p < 0.025 in both halves and a sign test p < 0.05 on non-overlapping windows
trial.controls: VIX and VIX3M are variance-swap rates, so FV is a forward variance-swap rate, not a forward ATM-straddle vol (it includes the skew premium). Compare with the spot VRP (VIX^2 - RV_30) to show the forward premium adds information. Report 2008 and 2020 separately. Position-level straddle-calendar P&L needs model pricing; the claim itself is data-only.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Already harnessed as T-148, forward_variance_premium in experiments/options_market.py (not volatility.py). The archived verdict is supported: +6.21 vol points, positive on 87% of 4,229 days since 2009-09-18, halves +6.42/+5.99, sign test 59/68. Next: a model-priced delta-hedged reverse straddle-calendar P&L through the two-expiry simulator, to check that the premium survives four-leg costs.

strategies.name: Theta ladder (staggered-expiry short premium)

legs.expiry_rule: 24 DTE (rung 4; next to exit at 21 DTE)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Sum of the rungs' payoffs: P&L = sum_i 0.25*[c_i - max(K_i - S_Ti, 0)], where each rung i has its own strike (set at entry) and expiry. One new quarter-size rung is sold each week at 45 DTE, and each rung is closed at 21 DTE or at 50% of its credit, so the book always holds four rungs spanning 24-45 DTE.
strategies.max_profit: 0.25 * the sum of the four credits (or half of that under the 50% rule).
strategies.max_loss: 0.25 * sum_i (K_i - c_i), if every put goes to zero value of the underlying: about one full-size short put's risk. The ladder changes the path, not the total notional.
strategies.breakevens: Per rung: K_i - c_i. The aggregate breakeven is the average of the four rungs' strikes minus credits, which were set in four different weeks.

greeks_at_inception.delta: positive (short puts, about +0.16-0.30 per full-size equivalent)
greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative, spread across four DTEs, so any one expiry's gamma peak is a quarter of a single-expiry book
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive and smoother through time (a rung is always in the fast-decay zone)

strategies.when_to_use: Smooth the path dependence and roll-date risk of monthly premium selling and keep capital continuously deployed, with a rung always near the 21-DTE exit. Also applies to laddered covered calls, laddered calendars and laddered LEAPS rolls.
strategies.risks: The same total tail risk as a single entry: a crash hits all rungs at once (rung correlation is about 1 in a sell-off), so the diversification is in timing only. Four times the fills and management. After a rally, strikes set on different weeks can cluster below spot and be tested together.
strategies.margin_note: Each rung is margined as a naked (or cash-secured) put; total margin equals one full-size position. Portfolio margin recognises the common underlying.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit weeklies expire every Friday at 08:00 UTC, so a four-rung weekly ladder maps onto consecutive Fridays. 0.1-contract minimum steps allow quarter-size rungs on 0.4+ BTC books. Credits are in coin; theta accrues seven days a week; strikes are sized from DVOL.
strategies.metals_notes: GC: weekly options make a weekly ladder possible on the active futures month; SPAN; 1256. GLD/SLV: weeklies available for the equity-option ladder. CME pages returned 403 this session, so weekly-listing details come from training knowledge.
variants: Laddered covered calls (sell a quarter of the calls each week)
Laddered LEAPS replacement across quarterly expiries
strategies.claim: A 4-rung weekly ladder of quarter-size 0.16-delta SPY short puts, each managed at 50% or 21 DTE, has a maximum drawdown at least 15% smaller than a single full-size 45-DTE monthly entry managed the same way, model-priced (VIX as IV).

trial.statistic: Ratio of max drawdowns (ladder / single entry); mean monthly P&L per unit of margin and the standard deviation are reported alongside
trial.null: Drawdown ratio >= 0.85 (compared across block-bootstrap resampled paths)
trial.procedure: Daily simulation since 1993-01-29 (SPY inception) with VIX-as-IV pricing. The single-entry book enters monthly at 45 DTE; the ladder enters weekly at a quarter size; identical exit rules. Studentized block bootstrap; walk-forward halves.
trial.data: SPY closes, VIX, FRED 3-month bill

strategies.name: Time-decay harvesting (45 DTE short premium, managed at 50% or 21 DTE)

legs.expiry_rule: 45 DTE; exit at 50% of credit or at 21 DTE
45 DTE; exit at 50% of credit or at 21 DTE

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Held to expiry: P&L(S) = C - max(Kp - S, 0) - max(S - Kc, 0). The defining feature is the exit rule, which cuts the path before the last three weeks. Under Black-Scholes, the gamma part of theta is -0.5*sigma^2*S^2*Gamma at every DTE, so theta per unit of gamma does not peak at 45 DTE (that statement was removed). What changes toward expiry is that dollar gamma (and so daily P&L variance) grows roughly as 1/sqrt(T) for near-the-money strikes. The 21-DTE exit avoids that stretch.
strategies.max_profit: C (full credit) if held to expiry with Kp < S < Kc; 0.5*C under the 50% rule; the realised credit at 21 DTE under the time rule.
strategies.max_loss: Downside: Kp - C. Upside: unbounded (naked call). Defined-risk variants (iron condor) cap it at the width minus C.
strategies.breakevens: Kp - C and Kc + C at expiry; before expiry the exit rules make the realised breakeven path-dependent.
strategies.when_to_use: Systematic premium selling when IV rank is elevated and the term structure is in contango (see the regime-filter entry). tastylive (Kai Zeng, 2024): in a portfolio of SPY 45-DTE 1SD strangles, exiting at 21 DTE gave the highest return and the lowest volatility; managing at 50% beat holding to expiration on return but did not control volatility as well. tastylive manages winners at 50% generally, and at 10-50% for calendars, diagonals and iron flies.
strategies.risks: Tail risk: a gap beyond a strike can lose many times the credit before any exit rule triggers. tastylive's studies are its own simulations (no stated sample period, no CIs). Early assignment. The 50% target shrinks absolute profit while leaving absolute risk. Margin is a capital drag.
strategies.margin_note: Naked strangle: Reg T about 20% of notional per side less the OTM amount; portfolio margin far less on SPX. Not IRA-eligible unless cash-secured or defined-risk (iron condor).
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit: monthlies expire on the last Friday at 08:00 UTC, so '45 DTE' is approximated by the second monthly out. Theta accrues seven days a week, and DVOL/sqrt(365) sizes the 1SD daily move. Credits are in coin. DVOL history (public/get_volatility_index_data) and realised vol (public/get_historical_volatility) allow a model-priced BTC version now (about 1,000 days).
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: 1SD strangles on the active futures month with SPAN margin (far below Reg T), American exercise, 1256; weekly GC options allow 7-14 DTE variants. GLD/SLV: cash-secured or Reg T equity margin. CME pages returned 403 this session.

strategies.name: VIX futures / VIX options calendar (term-structure roll trade)

legs.expiry_rule: near: M1, settles on the Wednesday 30 days before the third Friday of the following calendar month (CBOE VX spec)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At M1 settlement (special opening quotation of VIX, from A.M.-settled SPX options; $1,000 per point): P&L = (F1_0 - SOQ) + (F2_T - F2_0), i.e. the change in the M2 - M1 spread times $1,000. In contango both futures roll down toward spot VIX over time, the front faster, so the position earns the roll. In a vol spike M1 rises more than M2 (higher beta to VIX) and the position loses. VIX options variant: each VIX option expiry is priced off its own VX future, not spot VIX.
strategies.max_profit: Bounded in practice by the initial M2 - M1 spread plus any further steepening; theoretically unbounded if M2 rallies while M1 settles low.
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded in principle: a spike that lifts M1 far more than M2 (the front's beta to VIX is well above the second month's). Historical worst days are many multiples of the mean daily roll gain.
strategies.breakevens: The M2 - M1 spread at exit equals the spread at entry (P&L = 0 when the slope is unchanged).

greeks_at_inception.delta: negative to spot VIX (short the higher-beta front)
greeks_at_inception.gamma: no option gamma (linear futures). The effective convexity to VIX spikes is negative because M1's beta to spot VIX rises in spikes.
greeks_at_inception.vega: short front-month variance, long second-month variance (net short in a parallel-plus-front-steepening spike)

strategies.when_to_use: Contango with M2/M1 >= 1.05 and VIX below its 1-year median; exit or reverse when VIX/VIX3M >= 1 (regime filter). The reverse (long M1 / short M2) is a cheap crash hedge in steep contango only if its carry cost is tolerable. Johnson's SLOPE predicts VIX-futures excess returns, which is the premium being harvested.
strategies.risks: Vol spikes (Feb 2018, Mar 2020) produce losses far beyond the accumulated roll. Margin calls on the short front. The spread's sensitivity changes near expiry. Wednesday-morning SOQ settlement risk. Size: VX is $1,000 per point, but the CBOE spec also lists Mini VIX futures (VXM, one tenth of a VX), so retail can scale down; VIX options and ETPs are other routes.
strategies.margin_note: CFE/clearing margin on a VX calendar is a fraction of outright margin (spread credit), but spikes have produced intraday margin calls. VIX futures are regulated futures contracts and VIX options are nonequity options, so both are Section 1256 (26 USC 1256(b)(1)(A),(C)). ETP routes (short VXX/UVXY vs long VIXM) carry financing and borrow costs instead.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit has no listed futures or options on DVOL (it is an index only), so there is no direct analogue. The closest proxies are a BTC futures calendar (the basis roll between two dated futures, which trades funding rather than variance) or a straddle calendar on BTC options (see straddle-calendar).
strategies.metals_notes: No listed gold volatility futures; GVZ is an index only. The analogue is a GC options straddle calendar across futures months, or a GLD straddle calendar; both carry the metals IV term structure rather than a listed vol future. CME pages returned 403 this session.

strategies.name: VIX term-structure regime filter (VIX3M/VIX gate for premium selling)

legs.expiry_rule: 45 DTE; entered only when VIX/VIX3M < 1 (contango); flat or long-vol when >= 1

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: The gated position is a standard short strangle: P&L(S) = C - max(Kp - S, 0) - max(S - Kc, 0). The strategy is the gate. VIX/VIX3M < 1 is contango (normal: 1-month implied below 3-month); >= 1 is backwardation (stress). Johnson (JFQA 2017): the shape of the VIX term structure conveys the price of variance risk rather than expected VIX changes, and SLOPE predicts excess returns of variance swaps, VIX futures and S&P 500 straddles. That is the rationale for using the slope as a gate. VIX3M (formerly VXV) is the 3-month analogue of VIX, with daily history since 2007-12-04 (CBOE VIX3M_History.csv; FRED VXVCLS).
strategies.max_profit: C per gated entry.
strategies.max_loss: Downside: Kp - C. Upside: unbounded. The gate changes how often stress-period entries happen, not the tail of any single entry.
strategies.breakevens: Kp - C and Kc + C.

greeks_at_inception.vega: negative; the gate's purpose is to avoid holding this when the term structure says variance is being repriced

strategies.when_to_use: As the entry/exit switch for every short-theta strategy in this family (calendars, theta harvesting, ladders, VX calendars): sell premium in contango; stand aside, or flip to long calendars or long VIX call spreads, in backwardation. Mandel's registry already tests whether backwardation predicts a VIX decline (term_structure_reversion); this entry tests whether the regime conditions the premium itself.
strategies.risks: The ratio is a slow signal: it flips after the first leg of a sell-off. Contango persists through gradual bear markets. Thresholds invite overfitting (deflate). 2008 and 2020 dominate the backwardation sample. The gate does not shorten the tail of a single entry.
strategies.margin_note: Inherits the gated position's margin; the backwardation alternatives are debit trades.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit publishes only DVOL (30-day), with history via public/get_volatility_index_data. There is no 3-month DVOL, so the BTC slope must be built from chain mark_iv at a monthly vs a quarterly expiry, available from today's captures forward. A DVOL-vs-realised VRP conditional on that slope is the crypto analogue and becomes testable as captures accumulate.
strategies.metals_notes: CBOE's GVZ (gold ETF vol index, 30-day) has no 3-month analogue, so the gold term structure must come from GLD chain captures. GC/SI SPAN margin and 1256 treatment apply to the gated position. CME pages returned 403 this session.

strategies.name: Weekend theta capture (Friday-to-Monday short premium)

legs.expiry_rule: next Monday (opened at Friday's close; SPY/SPX daily expiries); closed or settled Monday

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At Monday's close/settlement: P&L(S) = C - |S_Mon - K|, where C is the straddle credit received at Friday's close. The thesis: on Friday, options are priced as if three calendar days of variance lie ahead, but the stock realises only about one trading day's worth of variance over the weekend. Jones and Shemesh (Journal of Finance, 2018) find option returns are significantly lower over nontrading periods, mostly weekends, and attribute it to mispricing from incorrect treatment of variance during market closure.
strategies.max_profit: C, if S_Mon = K.
strategies.max_loss: Upside unbounded: S_Mon - K - C. Downside: K - C, if the stock goes to 0. Weekend gaps are the risk.
strategies.breakevens: K - C and K + C.

greeks_at_inception.theta: positive: three calendar days of decay collected

strategies.when_to_use: When Friday option prices still charge for calendar-day variance over the weekend and weekend realised variance is well below three weekdays' worth (French and Roll, JFE 1986: return variance is much lower over non-trading periods than over trading periods). Defined-risk versions (iron fly) cap the gap risk. Avoid weekends with scheduled news (G7, elections, OPEC) and three-day holiday weekends.
strategies.risks: Weekend gap risk (geopolitical or macro news) with no chance to adjust. Market makers already mark down Friday quotes (they trade in 'trading-day' time), so the edge may be priced away. Assignment and settlement on Monday expiries. Costs on 2-4 fills every week.
strategies.margin_note: Naked straddle: Reg T naked margin or portfolio margin (SPX); iron-fly version defined-risk and IRA-eligible. SPX/XSP are cash-settled 1256 contracts.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC trades 24/7, so there is no closure. The weekend question is whether weekend realised variance is lower than weekday variance (thinner liquidity, fewer macro releases): registry harness btc_weekend_variance (experiments/options_market.py) tests that. Deribit lists Saturday and Sunday dailies (Sat 17 / Sun 18 Oct 2026 in today's listing), so the market prices weekend days directly; compare their mark_iv with weekday dailies from captures.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI futures trade on Globex from Sunday evening, so the closure is shorter than SPY's and the effect should be smaller. GLD/SLV options have the full equity weekend gap. GC/SI options are 1256; GLD/SLV are not.

strategies.name: BTC covered call on coin inventory

legs.strike_rule: spot (1 BTC held, or 1 IBIT lot = 100 shares ~ 0.057 BTC)
delta 0.25 (at flat DVOL 50: ~5% OTM for 7 DTE, ~11% OTM for 30 DTE)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: USD-linear view (IBIT, USDC-linear options, or Deribit premium converted to USD at entry): min(S_T, K) - S_0 + C. Deribit inverse with the premium c (BTC per BTC) kept in coin: coins at expiry = 1 + c - max(S_T - K, 0)/S_T, USD value = min(S_T, K) + c*S_T, so P&L = min(S_T, K) + c*S_T - S_0 (above K the coin holding shrinks to K/S_T + c, USD value K + c*S_T).
strategies.max_profit: USD-linear: (K - S_0) + C at S_T >= K. Inverse with premium kept in BTC: no hard cap; P&L above K = K - S_0 + c*S_T, rising with slope c
strategies.max_loss: USD-linear: S_0 - C (S_T -> 0). Inverse with premium kept in BTC: S_0, because the coin premium also goes to zero
strategies.breakevens: USD-linear: S_0 - C. Inverse with premium kept in BTC: S_T = S_0/(1 + c)
strategies.when_to_use: You hold BTC/ETH and will cap the upside; DVOL is high relative to realised vol (BTC VRP positive); neutral-to-mildly-bullish view.
strategies.risks: Caps the upside on an asset with large upside jumps; in bull phases the call wing is bid. Inverse settlement means premium and payoff are in coin, so USD P&L carries the extra c*S_T term. IBIT calls are American and can be assigned early. IBIT trades only US hours while BTC trades 24/7.
strategies.margin_note: Deribit: coin collateral; the short call is fully covered by the 1 BTC (portfolio margin lowers this further). IBIT: covered call under Reg T, no extra margin. CME BTC options: SPAN/CORE on 5-BTC (or 0.1-BTC MBT) futures; CME pages timed out today, so unverified.

Settlement periods: day, week, month; expiries run to 24SEP27. European, 08:00 UTC. Not verified today: the fee cap of 12.5% of premium and the 30-min-average delivery price. USDC-linear options exist (BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, AVAX, TRX, HYPE). No dividends; 24/7 trading, so theta accrues over weekends. IBIT options: American, physical delivery of shares, OCC-cleared, position limits (verify the current OCC table).

OG/SO options on GC/SI are 1256 contracts, American, and exercise into a futures position; the covered position is a long future, not bullion.

strategies.name: BTC variance risk premium harvest (delta-hedged short straddle)

legs.strike_rule: dynamic delta hedge: qty = -(net option delta), rebalanced daily (a short ATM-forward straddle has small negative delta -(2N(d1)-1), so the hedge starts slightly long)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Unhedged (USD-linear): C + P - |S_T - K|. Hedged: P&L ~ sum_t 0.5 * Gamma_t * S_t^2 * (sigma_imp^2*dt - r_t^2), i.e. profits when realised variance < implied along the gamma-weighted path.
strategies.max_profit: Unhedged: C + P at S_T = K. Hedged: ~ C + P if the path is flat (theta fully collected)
strategies.max_loss: Unhedged USD: unlimited on the upside, K - (C + P) at S_T = 0. Inverse in BTC: call side bounded (-> 1 BTC per contract less premium), put side unbounded in BTC. Hedged: path-dependent, large on gaps between rehedges
strategies.breakevens: Unhedged: K - (C + P) and K + (C + P)
strategies.when_to_use: DVOL more than 10 vol points above trailing 30-day realised vol; no scheduled jump catalysts in the window (ETF decisions, FOMC, CPI).
strategies.risks: Crypto jump risk (-20% days); weekend gaps can only be hedged on 24/7 venues (Deribit yes, IBIT no); funding cost of a perp hedge; liquidation cascades; with inverse options the coin collateral shrinks as the put liability grows.
strategies.margin_note: Deribit portfolio margin for a delta-neutral short straddle is roughly the stress loss on a +/-15% move, in coin (unverified). US (IBIT): naked straddle under the Reg T 20% rule; position limits.

DVOL (verified from the Deribit whitepaper page): variance-swap methodology on the two expiries around 30 days, time-weighted interpolation, raw value every second, EMA of the last 240 points. strategies.name: Coin-secured / cash-secured put to accumulate BTC or metal

legs.strike_rule: delta -0.25 to -0.30 (OTM ~8-12% for 30 DTE at DVOL 50)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: USD-linear (USDC options, IBIT, GLD): P - max(K - S_T, 0), with K of cash collateral earning the bill rate. Deribit inverse: BTC P&L = p - max(K - S_T, 0)/S_T, unbounded in BTC as S_T -> 0; its USD value is p*S_T - max(K - S_T, 0).
strategies.max_profit: P (premium); inverse: p BTC, worth p*S_T in USD
strategies.max_loss: USD-linear: K - P at S_T = 0 (OIC: obligated to buy at the strike, loss reduced by the premium). Inverse with premium kept in BTC: K in USD, unbounded in BTC terms; with BTC collateral the USD equity also loses the collateral's value (double exposure)
strategies.breakevens: USD-linear: K - P (OIC: strike price - premium). Inverse with premium kept in BTC: S_T = K/(1 + p)
strategies.when_to_use: You want to buy BTC or GLD lower and are happy to own at K; IV rich vs realised; neutral-to-bullish view.
strategies.risks: Full downside below K, offset only by the premium; BTC can fall 30-50% quickly, leaving the put deep ITM. On Deribit inverse puts posted against BTC collateral, the collateral loses value while the liability grows; secure the trade with USDC-linear puts or over-collateralise.
strategies.margin_note: Deribit short option margin is roughly max(0.15 - OTM fraction, 0.10) + mark, in coin (unverified today). USDC options are collateralised in USDC. US: cash-secured = K x 100 in cash; Reg T naked ~20% otherwise. OG/SO puts: SPAN.
strategies.crypto_notes: A short inverse put is a short quanto put: the BTC loss (K - S)/S is convex in 1/S. USDC-linear puts (verified listed today: BTC_USDC, ETH_USDC, SOL_USDC, XRP_USDC, AVAX_USDC, TRX_USDC, HYPE_USDC) remove this and match the accumulate-at-K intent. IBIT puts are American and physically assigned (US hours).
strategies.metals_notes: GLD/SLV/IAU/PPLT puts: equity-style; assignment = long shares, which are taxed as collectibles. OG/SO: assignment = long GC/SI futures (physical delivery risk if held into first notice day); 1256 60/40 and year-end mark-to-market.

strategies.name: Conversion / reversal basis arbitrage on Deribit inverse options

legs.strike_rule: same-expiry BTC future (e.g. BTC-30OCT26). Sizing for an exact inverse lock: notional K USD (= K/F_0 BTC); for the USD-linear view, 1 BTC notional

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Deribit native (BTC): long future of notional K USD pays K/F_0 - K/S_T BTC; long put + short call pay (K - S_T)/S_T = K/S_T - 1 BTC. Total = (c - p) - (1 - K/F_0) BTC, deterministic. USD-linear view (USDC options, or premiums converted at entry, 1 BTC future): (K - F_0) + (C - P). The reversal is the mirror.
strategies.max_profit: Locked at entry: (c - p) - (1 - K/F_0) BTC net of fees (positive only when parity is violated by more than fees)
strategies.max_loss: Fees + legging slippage + any premium-currency drift (if premiums are not converted, the USD value of a BTC-denominated lock moves with S_T)
strategies.breakevens: Parity gap |(c - p) - (1 - K/F_0)| = round-trip fees: 2 option legs x min(0.0003 BTC, 12.5% of premium) + futures taker fee (~0.05% of notional, unverified) + delivery fees
strategies.when_to_use: Put-call parity breaks at illiquid strikes/expiries; funding or borrow dislocations push the futures basis away from the option-implied forward.
strategies.risks: Legging risk; any USD-view mismatch shows up as P&L drift if premiums stay in coin; low capacity. Deribit futures and options of the same expiry settle at the same 08:00 UTC delivery price, so there is no settlement mismatch.
strategies.margin_note: Deribit portfolio margin recognises the synthetic (near-zero margin). US: an IBIT conversion uses standard spread margin; early exercise on American IBIT options breaks the lock.
strategies.crypto_notes: Same-expiry dated futures verified listed (BTC-15OCT26..BTC-24SEP27 plus PERPETUAL). Inverse option parity is c - p = 1 - K/F in BTC (zero coin rate). For USDC-linear options the lock is in USD. DVOL's methodology also builds a synthetic forward from put-call parity (verified on the DVOL page).
strategies.metals_notes: GC futures vs OG options conversions exist on CME but are market-maker territory; GLD conversions suffer American exercise and borrow costs.
variants: Jelly roll (a calendar of synthetics) to trade the basis term structure

strategies.name: Deribit box spread (synthetic coin lending / implied rate)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: USD-linear: always K2 - K1. Deribit inverse: (K2 - K1)/S_T BTC, i.e. a fixed USD value of K2 - K1. Cost today b (BTC) = (K2 - K1)/S_0 x disc in the USD-forward sense; buying the box lends USD at r_implied, selling borrows.
strategies.max_profit: Long box (lender): (K2 - K1) - cost in USD = implied interest
strategies.max_loss: Long box: fees + counterparty risk (+ a loss if the implied rate is negative). Short box (borrower): (K2 - K1) - proceeds = interest paid
strategies.breakevens: r_implied = your alternative funding/lending rate

greeks_at_inception.delta: 0 in USD terms (in BTC terms the inverse box has BTC exposure, because its BTC payoff (K2 - K1)/S_T varies with S_T)

strategies.risks: Exchange counterparty risk (not a bank deposit); with inverse settlement the lender ends with a fixed USD value paid in coin; fee caps; thin capacity at wide boxes.
strategies.margin_note: Deribit portfolio margin treats a long box as nearly riskless (margin ~ fees; unverified). US IBIT boxes carry American exercise risk; SPX boxes are the cash-settled US analogue (not crypto).
strategies.crypto_notes: Compare r_implied with perp funding and the dated-futures basis. The futures-basis implied rate is testable now from history.deribit.com futures trades (index_price is included); the option box itself needs synchronous quotes. USDC-linear options give a clean USD box.

strategies.name: Inverse-settled short strangle with coin-payoff (quanto) correction

legs.strike_rule: spot or perp; qty = p + c, the BTC premium received (~0.015-0.022 BTC at flat DVOL 50 for 14-30 DTE); add the BTC collateral amount too if the account is USD-measured

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: In BTC (options only): p + c - max(K_p - S_T, 0)/S_T - max(S_T - K_c, 0)/S_T. In USD: (p + c)*S_T - max(K_p - S_T, 0) - max(S_T - K_c, 0); the hedge leg adds -(p + c)*(S_T - S_0), leaving roughly (p + c)*S_0 - max(K_p - S_T, 0) - max(S_T - K_c, 0).
strategies.max_profit: p + c BTC (USD ~ (p + c)*S_0 after the correction) for K_p <= S_T <= K_c
strategies.max_loss: Put side: unbounded in BTC (-> infinity as S_T -> 0), ~K_p in USD; plus any BTC collateral losing value (the double hit). Call side: bounded in BTC at 1 - (p + c) per contract, unbounded in USD
strategies.breakevens: Uncorrected, premium in coin: S_T = K_p/(1 + p + c) and S_T = K_c/(1 - p - c). Corrected (USD-hedged): S_T = K_p - (p + c)*S_0 and K_c + (p + c)*S_0

greeks_at_inception.delta: ~0 after correction (uncorrected USD delta is +(p + c) BTC from the coin premium)

strategies.when_to_use: Range-bound view with rich DVOL; the trader accounts in USD and must neutralise the coin-denominated premium and collateral exposure.
strategies.risks: Mis-hedging by using the BS delta alone on an inverse contract; the put wing is the dangerous side (collateral falls as the liability rises); liquidation in a crash.
strategies.margin_note: Deribit margin in BTC; the BTC-denominated requirement on the short put grows as BTC falls.
strategies.crypto_notes: Verified today via get_instruments: instrument_type 'reversed', settlement_currency BTC, contract_size 1 BTC, premiums in BTC (tick 0.0001, 0.0005 above 0.005). The USD value of an inverse option equals the standard BS value, so the BS delta is right for the option; the correction is only for the premium (and collateral) held in coin. USDC-linear options remove the quanto term entirely.
strategies.metals_notes: No analogue: GC/OG and GLD options are USD-linear.
variants: Iron condor (buy wings) to cap the put-side double hit
Delta-hedge via perp instead of spot
strategies.claim: Model-priced (BS at DVOL, daily rehedge on closes): for a short 15-delta inverse BTC strangle, the variance of 30-day USD P&L when hedged with the coin-corrected delta is at least 20% lower than when hedged with the naive BS delta, 2021-04 to 2026-09.

trial.statistic: Ratio of USD P&L variance (corrected hedge / naive hedge)
trial.procedure: Simulate daily-rehedged short strangles on BTC closes with IV = DVOL; book the premium in coin; compute USD P&L under both hedge rules; bootstrap the variance ratio
trial.data: BTC closes; DVOL from 2021-03-24
trial.pass: Upper end of the 95% CI of the variance ratio < 0.8
trial.controls: The same test on a USDC-linear strangle must give ratio ~1; vary collateral treatment (premium only vs premium + collateral)

strategies.name: Perpetual funding carry hedged with options

legs.strike_rule: BTC perpetual (receive funding when positive), notional = 1 BTC

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Over the holding period: sum of funding received - call premium + max(S_T - K, 0). The spot-vs-perp P&L is ~0 by construction (apart from the perp-index basis). The call pays only in a squeeze.
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded via the call above K (net delta +0.10); base case (no squeeze) = sum of funding - C
strategies.max_loss: C + cumulative negative funding + perp/index basis slippage + venue/counterparty loss
strategies.breakevens: Cumulative funding received = C (per roll period), absent a squeeze

greeks_at_inception.theta: negative from the call (funding carry is a separate positive accrual)

strategies.when_to_use: Annualised funding above 10-15% (bull-market leverage demand) and moderate option IV. The call only adds value when the short perp sits in a different margin pool from the spot, e.g. a USDC-margined linear perp with spot in custody, where a squeeze drains perp margin. On Deribit, BTC collateral against a short inverse BTC-PERPETUAL is already a USD-locked synthetic: equity in BTC is N/S_T and the margin requirement scales the same way, so a rally cannot liquidate it.
strategies.risks: Funding can flip negative for weeks (bear regimes); exchange/counterparty risk; the call hedges margin stress but not a funding reversal; on Deribit inverse perps, funding is paid in coin.
strategies.margin_note: Deribit: short perp margined in BTC against the BTC collateral (nets under portfolio margin). US: perps are mostly unavailable to retail; the substitute is CME BTC futures cash-and-carry (cash-settled, 5 BTC, SPAN) earning the basis instead of funding.
strategies.crypto_notes: get_funding_rate_history returns hourly records (interest_1h, interest_8h, index_price), verified back to 2019-05, so the carry history covers the whole DVOL era. Sum interest_1h for the realised funding rate. IBIT cannot earn funding.
strategies.metals_notes: No perps in US metals; the analogue is futures contango carry, which is roughly the bill rate minus the lease rate (see gold-contango-calendar). Deribit lists a PAXG_USDC perpetual (tokenised gold; seen in trade history), a crypto-native gold carry venue.
variants: Replace the call with a call spread (cheaper)
Collect funding only when the 7-day mean is above a threshold
Reverse carry: short spot / long perp when funding is deeply negative, hedged with an OTM put
Dated-futures cash-and-carry (lock the basis instead of floating funding)
strategies.claim: With the hedge model-priced (10-delta 30-DTE call at DVOL), long-spot/short-BTC-PERPETUAL funding carry net of the rolling call cost has a positive mean monthly return over 2021-04 to 2026-09, with a studentized block-bootstrap 95% CI above zero.

trial.statistic: Mean monthly carry net of hedge cost
trial.procedure: Pull get_funding_rate_history (hourly) for 2021-04..2026-09 and sum interest_1h per month; each month price a 10-delta 30-DTE call with BS at DVOL and add its expiry payoff; net; block bootstrap; walk-forward halves
trial.data: Deribit funding history (verified from 2019-05); DVOL; BTC closes; FRED DGS3MO for excess return
trial.pass: CI of net monthly carry > 0; Sharpe > 1 reported
trial.controls: Unhedged carry as comparison; months with negative funding included; call priced at DVOL + 5 vol points (the 10-delta call wing usually trades above DVOL)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(S_T, K) - S_0 - P
strategies.max_profit: Unlimited
strategies.max_loss: S_0 - K + P
strategies.breakevens: S_0 + P

strategies.name: Silver call backspread (squeeze convexity)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: cr - max(S_T - K1, 0) + 2*max(S_T - K2, 0), where cr = C(K1) - 2C(K2) (negative = debit). Flat cr below K1, falls to cr - (K2 - K1) at K2, then rises with slope +1
strategies.max_profit: Unlimited above K2 (cr + S_T - 2K2 + K1)
strategies.max_loss: (K2 - K1) - cr at S_T = K2
strategies.breakevens: Upper: 2K2 - K1 - cr = K2 + (K2 - K1) - cr. Lower: K1 + cr, only if cr > 0 (with a credit there is no loss below K1; with a debit, the loss below K1 is the debit)

greeks_at_inception.gamma: positive (2 OTM gammas exceed 1 ATM gamma at 60-120 DTE)

strategies.when_to_use: Silver's history of explosive upside (1980, 2011, 2021 squeeze): right-tail convexity entered near zero cost; also a GC version before a crisis.
strategies.risks: Worst case is silver drifting up to K2 and stopping there; SLV call skew is often already rich.
strategies.margin_note: US: margin on the 1x1 vertical (K2 - K1 - credit) plus the extra long call paid in full. SO on SI: SPAN, 1256.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC call backspreads are the crypto analogue (when the BTC call wing is bid they become a debit).
strategies.metals_notes: SI = 5000 oz; CME micro silver SIL = 1000 oz; SO options exercise into SI (American). SLV options: American, equity-taxed. At flat vol a 0.50/0.25 1x2 usually opens for a small credit.
variants: Put backspread on GLD for a crash (less relevant: gold tends to rally in crises)

strategies.name: Backspread (1x2 Long Ratio: Call or Put)

legs.strike_rule: K2 = ATM (call version: short 1 ATM call at K1)
K1 = delta -0.25 put (about 2-5% below spot at 30 DTE depending on vol); variant fixed 5% OTM. Call version: long 2 calls at delta 0.25, K2 > K1

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: put: 2*max(K1-S_T,0) - max(K2-S_T,0) + Cr, where Cr = P(K2) - 2P(K1). Call: 2*max(S_T-K2,0) - max(S_T-K1,0) + Cr, where Cr = C(K1) - 2C(K2)
strategies.max_profit: put: K1 - (K2-K1) + Cr, as S_T -> 0 (OIC: substantial). Call: unbounded
strategies.max_loss: (K2-K1) - Cr, at S_T = K1 (put) or S_T = K2 (call)
strategies.breakevens: put: lower S_T = 2K1 - K2 + Cr; upper (credit only) S_T = K2 - Cr. Call: upper S_T = 2K2 - K1 - Cr; lower (credit only) S_T = K1 + Cr

greeks_at_inception.delta: about 0 with 25-delta wings (-0.03 put version); with fixed 5%-OTM wings and VIX < ~28 the put version is net + delta (the short ATM put dominates)
greeks_at_inception.gamma: + with 25-delta wings at any vol. With fixed 5%-OTM wings at 30 DTE it is - when VIX < ~15
greeks_at_inception.vega: + (OIC: very positive) with 25-delta wings; - for fixed 5% wings when VIX < ~15

strategies.when_to_use: Expect a large move in the chosen direction with rising IV; IV low and skew flat so the two long wings are cheap; crash convexity funded by the ATM short.
strategies.risks: Loses most if the underlying drifts slowly to the long strike by expiry (the valley); theta bleed; needs the move before expiry.
strategies.margin_note: Reg T: one vertical spread margin (width - credit) plus one long option paid; small requirement. Deribit/CME: net long options, low margin.
strategies.crypto_notes: Put backspread on Deribit: each long inverse put pays (K1-S_T)/S_T BTC, unbounded in BTC as S -> 0, which makes it a strong BTC-denominated crash hedge. A call backspread buys the BTC call wing, which is often elevated (DVOL article).
strategies.metals_notes: A call backspread on GC/GLD buys the upside wing, which is costly when gold call skew is rich; a put backspread on gold is cheap when the put wing is flat.
strategies.claim: A 1-month 1x2 SPY put backspread (short 1 ATM put, long 2 delta -0.25 puts, priced at VIX IV; model-priced) has a negative mean P&L overall but a positive mean P&L in months entered with VIX below 15, over 1993-2026.

trial.statistic: mean P&L per unit spot, overall and conditional on VIX < 15 at entry, with block bootstrap CIs
trial.procedure: monthly cycles; solve the delta -0.25 strike at VIX IV; payoff from the SPY close; split by entry VIX
trial.data: SPY, VIX, DTB3
trial.pass: overall upper CI < 0 AND conditional (VIX < 15) lower CI > 0
trial.controls: The threshold of 15 is fixed before looking; report the number of low-VIX months (about 1/3 of the sample). Flat IV underprices the 25-delta puts relative to skew, which flatters the long wings: state this. With fixed 5% wings the position is short gamma at VIX < 15, which is why the strike rule is delta-based.

strategies.harness_suggestion: overlay_backtest(strategy='backspread_1x2', side='put', wing_delta=-0.25, condition='vix<15') using bs.strike_for_delta

strategies.name: Bear Call Spread (Credit)

legs.strike_rule: K2 = K1 + 3-5% of S (base case K2 = 1.06S)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Cr - min(max(S_T-K1,0), K2-K1), where Cr = C(K1) - C(K2) > 0
strategies.max_profit: Cr, for S_T <= K1
strategies.max_loss: (K2-K1) - Cr, for S_T >= K2
strategies.breakevens: S_T = K1 + Cr
strategies.when_to_use: Bearish-to-neutral with a ceiling in mind (resistance, after a rally); IV elevated; defined risk instead of a naked call.
strategies.risks: Equity drift and melt-ups make OTM call spreads the weakest credit spread; early assignment of K1 before ex-dividend; pin risk at K1 and K2.
strategies.margin_note: Reg T: (K2-K1) x 100 - credit. Deribit and CME: spread margin.
strategies.crypto_notes: The BTC call wing is often elevated (DVOL article: positive skew on both sides), so call credit spreads can collect more than on SPX; measure it. The inverse max loss in BTC, (K2-K1)/S_T, shrinks as the price rises (partial relief).
strategies.metals_notes: When gold call skew is rich, GC/GLD call credit spreads are the natural skew-selling trade in metals. GC options are American, so assignment delivers a short GC future.
strategies.claim: A 1-month 3%/6%-OTM SPY bear call spread priced at VIX IV (model-priced) has a mean P&L per unit of max loss that is not positive over 1993-2026 (equity drift exceeds the flat-IV call premium).

trial.statistic: mean P&L / max loss with block bootstrap CI
trial.procedure: monthly cycles; K1 = 1.03S, K2 = 1.06S at VIX IV; payoff from the SPY close
trial.data: SPY, VIX, DTB3
trial.pass: upper CI <= 0
trial.controls: Correction: flat IV overprices both OTM calls relative to the real smile; the sign of the bias on the net credit is indeterminate (depends on the smile slope between K1 and K2), so do not assume the real result is more negative. Compare with the bull put spread in the same months and with chain mids at 60 days.

strategies.name: Bear Put Spread (Debit)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: min(max(K2-S_T,0), K2-K1) - D, where D = P(K2) - P(K1) > 0
strategies.max_profit: (K2-K1) - D, for S_T <= K1
strategies.max_loss: D, for S_T >= K2
strategies.breakevens: S_T = K2 - D

greeks_at_inception.theta: - small (OIC: less than a plain long put)

strategies.when_to_use: Moderately bearish to a target near K1; a cheaper crash hedge than a long put when skew is steep (it sells the rich OTM put).
strategies.risks: Gain capped in a crash; early assignment of the short K1 when deep ITM; bid-ask on two legs.
strategies.margin_note: Debit paid in full. Deribit: debit in BTC. CME: SPAN spread credit.
strategies.crypto_notes: With inverse settlement the spread pays min(max(K2-S_T,0), K2-K1)/S_T BTC: its BTC value rises as the price falls, so the hedge is convex in BTC terms. How much the short K1 leg recovers depends on the put wing of the BTC smile; measure it from the Deribit book rather than assuming it is cheap.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold put skew is often flat, so bear put spreads on GC/GLD recover little from the short leg; GC option legs are American.
variants: collar-financed (sell a call to pay for it; hedging family)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: min(max(S_T-K1,0), K2-K1) - D, where D = C(K1) - C(K2) > 0
strategies.max_profit: (K2-K1) - D, for S_T >= K2

strategies.name: Risk Reversal (Directional, OTM Combo)

legs.strike_rule: K_c = OTM 5% or delta 0.25 (bearish version: short call)
K_p = OTM 5% or delta -0.25 (bearish version: long put)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(S_T-K_c,0) - max(K_p-S_T,0) + Cr, where Cr = P(K_p) - C(K_c) (a credit on equities with real skew; a debit under flat VIX pricing at equidistant strikes, because the forward is above spot)
strategies.max_profit: unbounded (bullish version)
strategies.max_loss: K_p - Cr at S_T = 0 (theoptionsguide: put strike plus net opening cost)
strategies.breakevens: credit: S_T = K_p - Cr (flat profit Cr between strikes). Debit (D = -Cr): S_T = K_c + D (flat loss D between strikes)

greeks_at_inception.vega: ~0 (slightly + under flat pricing); long skew (short put IV, long call IV)

strategies.when_to_use: Bullish and willing to own at K_p; equity skew steep (puts rich vs calls), so the position is entered for a credit; stock-like upside with no premium outlay. The 25-delta risk reversal IV spread is also the market's skew quote.
strategies.risks: Stock-like crash loss below K_p; margin on the short put; the dead zone between strikes earns only the credit; assignment on the put when deep ITM.
strategies.margin_note: Reg T: naked put margin (premium + 20% - OTM) plus the long call paid. Portfolio margin recognises the net delta. Deribit: BTC margin on the short put; CME: SPAN.
strategies.crypto_notes: The DVOL article describes a BTC smile with both wings elevated, not a fixed call-over-put skew. The sign of the 25-delta risk reversal on Deribit flips between regimes (bullish phases: calls richer, so a bullish RR is a debit), so read it from the book. Inverse settlement: the short put's BTC loss is unbounded as S -> 0.
strategies.metals_notes: When gold call skew is rich, bullish GC/GLD risk reversals cost a debit and the bearish one (short call / long put) earns a credit and is the skew-selling trade. GC option legs are American.
variants: collar (= bearish risk reversal + long stock; hedging family)

trial.data: SPY, VIX, CBOE SKEW daily, DTB3
trial.pass: lower CI of the difference > 0 in both the full-sample and expanding-window quintile definitions
trial.controls: Flat pricing means the entry premium does not vary with skew, so this isolates the conditional return of the underlying wings (a SKEW timing test). SPY starts in 1993, so the sample is 1993-2026, not 1990.

strategies.name: Seagull (Put-Financed Call Spread)

legs.strike_rule: K2 = ATM (bearish seagull: long 1 ATM put)
K3 = OTM 5% above K2 (bearish: short put 5% below)
K1 < K2 chosen so the net premium is about 0. Under flat VIX pricing at 30 DTE this is about 97-100% of S; with real equity skew about 3-6% OTM. Bearish seagull: short call above

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: min(max(S_T-K2,0), K3-K2) - max(K1-S_T,0) + Cr, where Cr = P(K1) - [C(K2) - C(K3)]
strategies.max_profit: (K3-K2) + Cr, for S_T >= K3
strategies.max_loss: K1 - Cr, at S_T = 0 (stock-like below K1)
strategies.breakevens: credit or zero: S_T = K1 - Cr (and any S_T >= K2 - Cr is profitable). Debit (D = -Cr): S_T = K2 + D

greeks_at_inception.gamma: ~0 to - (short put gamma offsets the call spread's)

strategies.when_to_use: Moderately bullish to a target with no premium outlay, willing to own (or go long the future) at K1; steep put skew makes the financing put rich; common in commodity and FX hedging (a producer or consumer hedge on GC/CL).
strategies.risks: Stock-like loss below K1 while upside is capped at K3; margin on the naked put; early assignment of the short put when deep ITM.
strategies.margin_note: Reg T: naked put margin plus the call spread debit (if any). Portfolio margin or SPAN: net risk. Deribit: BTC margin on the short put.
strategies.crypto_notes: With an elevated BTC put wing the financing put pays well, but the inverse short put's BTC loss is unbounded as S -> 0. The bearish seagull (long put spread financed by a short call) sells the BTC call wing.
strategies.metals_notes: The classic GC/SI hedger structure. With call-side gold skew the bullish version is harder to finance (rich K3 sold helps, cheap K1 sold hurts); the bearish version (long put spread + short call) is cheap. GC legs are American; 1256.
strategies.claim: A 1-month zero-cost SPY seagull (long ATM call, short 5%-OTM call, short put struck to make net premium zero; all at VIX IV, model-priced) has a positive mean monthly P&L per unit spot over 1993-2026, holding in both walk-forward halves.

trial.statistic: mean P&L per unit spot with block bootstrap CI, per half
trial.procedure: monthly cycles; solve K1 for zero cost at VIX IV; payoff from the SPY close
trial.data: SPY, VIX, DTB3
trial.pass: lower CI > 0 in the full sample and the mean > 0 in both halves
trial.controls: Under flat pricing the zero-cost put sits near ATM, whereas with real skew it sits 3-6% OTM, so the model trade is far more put-heavy than the traded one: a chain-based rerun at 60 days is required before any trading conclusion. Run at iv_scale 0.9.

strategies.name: Short (Naked / Cash-Secured) Put

legs.strike_rule: K = ATM (PUT-index style: strike closest to but not above spot; variants: OTM 5%, delta -0.20)
legs.expiry_rule: about 30 DTE, rolled on the third Friday (variants: weekly WPUT style, 7 DTE)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: P - max(K-S_T,0) (plus T-bill interest on the K collateral in the cash-secured form)
strategies.max_profit: P, for S_T >= K
strategies.max_loss: K - P (at S_T = 0)
strategies.breakevens: S_T = K - P
strategies.when_to_use: Bullish-to-neutral; harvests the equity variance and skew premium; you are willing to own the underlying at K - P; IV elevated vs realised.
strategies.risks: Crash exposure equals long stock below K; short gamma into events; early assignment when deep ITM; margin requirements spike exactly when losses occur.
strategies.margin_note: Cash-secured: K x 100 held in T-bills (the PUT index uses 1- and 3-month bills). Reg T naked: premium + 20% of underlying - OTM amount, minimum premium + 10% of strike. Deribit: short-put BTC margin rises as S falls (inverse payoff). CME: SPAN.
strategies.crypto_notes: An inverse short put loses (K-S_T)/S_T BTC, which is unbounded in BTC as S_T -> 0, while the BTC collateral also loses USD value: double exposure, so size in USD, not BTC. The DVOL article describes a two-sided BTC smile, so the put premium relative to realised has to be measured (DVOL vs realised gives the BTC variance premium); it cannot be assumed from equities.
strategies.metals_notes: A short put on GC futures is assigned into a long GC future (American); SPAN margin, 1256. GLD/SLV short puts are Reg T equity options.
strategies.claim: Selling a 1-month ATM SPY put at VIX IV (model-priced), fully collateralised in 3-month bills with the PUT-index construction, has a higher Sharpe ratio than SPY buy-and-hold over 1993-2026.

trial.statistic: annualised Sharpe difference (putwrite minus SPY) with studentized block bootstrap p-value; also the max drawdown ratio
trial.procedure: third-Friday roll; strike = nearest strike at or below spot; premium = BS put at VIX IV; collateral earns DTB3; settle at the SPY close (proxy for the SOQ); walk-forward halves; repeat at iv_scale 0.9
trial.data: SPY, VIX, DTB3; benchmark check against the actual Cboe PUT index daily history (cdn.cboe.com PUT_History.csv: 4,983 rows from 1991-03-04 to 2026-10-13, with gaps)
trial.pass: p < 0.05 at both iv_scale 1.0 and 0.9, holding in both walk-forward halves
trial.controls: Correction: VIX is usually above ATM IV, so pricing the ATM put at VIX overstates the premium and the result is optimistic, not conservative; the 0.9 x VIX run and the comparison with the real PUT index guard this. Sharpe flatters negatively skewed returns, so report skew, kurtosis and PSR. SPY is price-only unless total return is reconstructed; state the dividend convention.

strategies.name: Short (Naked) Call
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: C - max(S_T-K,0)
strategies.max_profit: C, for S_T <= K
strategies.max_loss: unbounded (S_T -> inf)
strategies.breakevens: S_T = K + C
strategies.when_to_use: Bearish-to-neutral view with IV rich vs expected realised; income against an expected ceiling; melt-up risk accepted.
strategies.risks: Unlimited loss on gaps and takeovers; short gamma near expiry; early assignment before ex-dividend (American); margin calls force covering at the highs.
strategies.margin_note: Reg T uncovered equity call: premium + 20% of underlying - OTM amount, minimum premium + 10% of underlying. Broad-based index: 15% instead of 20%, same 10% minimum. Portfolio margin is lower. Deribit standard margin for a short call (from a support article summarised in search; not fetched, unverified): IM = max(0.15 - OTM/Index, 0.10) + mark, MM = 0.075 + mark, in BTC. CME: SPAN.
strategies.crypto_notes: On an inverse short call the BTC loss is bounded by 1 BTC per contract as S_T -> inf, since (S_T-K)/S_T -> 1, but the USD loss is unbounded. Margin is held in BTC, so a rally also raises collateral value (partial natural hedge). Covered by spot BTC it becomes a covered call; covered by a perp it adds funding exposure.
strategies.metals_notes: A short call on GC futures can be assigned on any day (American) into a short GC future; SPAN margin; 1256 tax treatment.
variants: covered call (add long underlying; income family)

trial.pass: bootstrap p < 0.05 for Sharpe(call) < Sharpe(put), and the call mean's lower CI > 0
trial.controls: Flat IV overprices the OTM call relative to the real smile (optimistic for the call) and underprices the 5%-OTM put (conservative for the put), so the bias favours the null: a pass is robust. Recheck with chain mids after 60 days.

strategies.name: Stock Repair (Covered Ratio Spread)

legs.strike_rule: existing holding with cost basis B > S (per-share units; 1 option contract per 100 shares)
K2 = (B + S)/2, roughly zero cost (2C(K2) ~ C(K1))

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: S_T - B + max(S_T-K1,0) - 2*max(S_T-K2,0) + Cr (Cr ~ 0)
strategies.max_profit: 2K2 - K1 - B + Cr, for S_T >= K2 (= Cr when K2 = (B+K1)/2: the repair only restores breakeven)
strategies.max_loss: B - Cr at S_T = 0 (OIC: the original purchase price)
strategies.breakevens: S_T = (B + K1 - Cr)/2 when this lies in [K1, K2]; with K2 = (B+K1)/2 and Cr = 0 it equals K2 exactly (vs B for the unrepaired stock)

greeks_at_inception.delta: + (stock 1 + call 0.5 - 2 x delta(K2)): about 0.9 at VIX 20, above 1 when VIX < ~15 because the short calls are far OTM
greeks_at_inception.vega: - (OIC: somewhat neutral; BS gives a small negative)

strategies.when_to_use: Holding a loser, expect a partial rebound to K2 within the tenor, want to lower breakeven without adding cash; gives up upside above K2.
strategies.risks: No downside protection (OIC: the risk of continued ownership); upside capped at K2; early assignment of the second short call before ex-dividend.
strategies.margin_note: OIC: done for even money or a credit in a margin account; one short call is covered by the stock and the other by the long call, so no extra margin. Deribit: spot BTC plus options in the same account (cross margin).
strategies.crypto_notes: Holding spot BTC on Deribit as collateral, buy 1 ATM inverse call and sell 2 OTM inverse calls; an elevated BTC call wing makes the shorts pay more, so a zero-cost repair strike sits higher. BTC-denominated P&L differs from USD P&L.
strategies.metals_notes: On a losing GC future: long 1 ATM GC call, short 2 OTM GC calls; when gold call skew is rich, zero-cost repair strikes sit higher. GLD shares: equity-style.
variants: repair with puts on a short stock position
strategies.claim: After a 10%+ SPY drawdown from its 252-day high, a 3-month zero-cost stock repair (stock + long 1 ATM call + short 2 calls at K2 = (prior high + spot)/2, priced at VIX IV; model-priced) has a higher mean 3-month P&L than holding SPY alone, over 1993-2026.

trial.statistic: mean of (repair P&L - hold P&L)/S per episode, which equals the embedded 1x2 call ratio spread's P&L; studentized bootstrap over non-overlapping episodes
trial.procedure: detect the first day of each >= 10% drawdown from the trailing 252-day high (re-arm after 63 days); B = prior high; K1 = S, K2 = (B+S)/2 at VIX IV (VIX3M where available, since the tenor is about 63 days); mark both at the 63-day SPY close
trial.data: SPY, VIX, VIX3M, DTB3; QQQ as a second sample
trial.pass: lower CI of the mean difference > 0
trial.controls: Correction: the original 'recovers breakeven more often' claim was tautological, because the repaired breakeven K2 < B makes it true by construction; replaced with the mean-P&L comparison. Expect only about 25-40 SPY episodes, so report power; QQQ episodes overlap in time and are not independent. Flat IV misprices skew (stated).
