trial.pass: Mean > 0 with 95% CI excluding 0 after fees.
trial.controls: Mid vs executable prices; settlement-source mismatch cases flagged; random-entry baseline.

strategies.blocked_on: aligned chain + event-contract snapshot capture (~60 trading days of matched contracts).
strategies.harness_suggestion: Digital extractor (call-spread / w, plus Breeden-Litzenberger density) from the chain store, joined to the existing Polymarket/Kalshi market tables.

strategies.name: Post-earnings announcement drift (PEAD) with vertical spreads

legs.strike_rule: K1 = ATM after the gap (positive surprise); mirror with puts for a negative surprise

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Bull call: min(max(S-K1,0), K2-K1) - D. Bear put mirror (long put K2, short put K1): min(max(K2-S,0), K2-K1) - D.
strategies.max_loss: D.
strategies.breakevens: K1 + D (bull call); K2 - D (bear put).

greeks_at_inception.delta: positive (bull) / negative (bear), about +0.25 to +0.35 per spread
greeks_at_inception.theta: slightly negative (ATM long dominates), turning positive as spot moves through K2
greeks_at_inception.vega: small positive (ATM long vega > OTM short vega); the bet is direction

strategies.when_to_use: The day after a print where the surprise is in the top/bottom decile (or gap-size proxy) and the stock gapped in the same direction and closed near the day's extreme. Enter at the T+1 close, hold 20-40 trading days or until the spread reaches 70% of max.
strategies.risks: PEAD has weakened in large caps (remains in small caps with illiquid options); the gap already captures most news; the spread caps upside; market beta dominates single-name drift (hedge with SPY if needed).
strategies.margin_note: Debit spread, margin = debit. Credit alternatives (bull put spread) margin = width - credit.
strategies.crypto_notes: No earnings; weak analogue is post-upgrade / post-ETF-flow drift. Deribit call spreads (debit) in USD strikes; coin-settled payoff min(max(S-K1,0),K2-K1)/S_T BTC converts back to the vanilla USD payoff at S_T.
strategies.metals_notes: No analogue (no earnings); post-FOMC drift in gold is a separate macro idea.
variants: Bull call spread vs bull put credit spread
Beta hedge with SPY put spread
strategies.claim: A 30-45 DTE ATM/+5% call debit spread bought at the T+1 close after a top-decile positive earnings gap that closes in the top 20% of its day range earns a higher mean return on debit over 30 trading days than the same spread bought on matched random days for the same stocks.

trial.statistic: Mean return on debit minus matched random-day spread return, bootstrap CI; underlying 30-day drift as a sanity check.
trial.null: Event spread return <= random-day spread return.
trial.procedure: Underlying leg first: sort post-earnings gaps by size/direction, measure 30-day drift (single-name closes + earnings dates). Option leg: mark the spread at the T+1 close and 30 days later from chain captures (or BS-reprice with captured IV).
trial.data: Earnings dates (EDGAR) and gap size as surprise proxy (consensus is not free); single-name daily OHLC; chain captures.
trial.pass: Mean excess return > 0 with 95% CI excluding 0 over at least 2 non-overlapping seasons.
trial.controls: Match on SPY return over the holding period; size terciles; random-day placebo; bear-spread mirror after negative gaps.

strategies.blocked_on: earnings-date history + single-name daily OHLC (free, not wired); chain capture for option-level marks (30+ days after each entry).
strategies.harness_suggestion: Reuse an underlying 'event drift' harness for the stock leg; BS-reprice the spread with captured IV for the overlay.

strategies.name: Pre-earnings long calendar (sell pre-event expiry, buy event expiry)

legs.expiry_rule: NEAR: last expiry BEFORE the earnings date (3-10 DTE)
FAR: first expiry AFTER the earnings date

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At near expiry: C_far(S, K, tau, IV_far) - max(S-K,0) - D. Maximum near S=K with far IV elevated.
strategies.max_profit: About C_far(S=K, K, tau, IV_event) - D at near expiry; not closed-form, rises with far IV.
strategies.max_loss: D (net debit) when S moves far from K and both legs converge to parity (OIC). Exception: if an ex-dividend date falls between the expiries, the far call can be worth less than the near call's intrinsic, so a deep-ITM call calendar can lose more than D; use the put calendar there.
strategies.breakevens: S levels at near expiry where C_far(S) = max(S-K,0) + D; solve numerically with the BS pricer.

greeks_at_inception.vega: positive (long far vega; far IV is the one that ramps into earnings)

strategies.when_to_use: 2-3 weeks before earnings when the term structure is flat (pre-event expiry IV not far below event expiry IV); profits as event-expiry IV ramps and the pre-event week decays. Close at or just before near expiry; do not hold the long leg through the print.
strategies.risks: A large pre-print move kills both legs' extrinsic; early assignment on a deep-ITM short near leg before an ex-date; the event IV may already be fully ramped; if the earnings date moves before the near expiry the short leg is suddenly across the event.
strategies.margin_note: Long calendar is a debit spread (far expiry covers near); margin = debit. Portfolio margin treats it as a time spread.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit lists daily, weekly and monthly expiries (settlement_period day/week/month, all 08:00 UTC), so a calendar straddling a known catalyst is easy. Both legs settle in coin; calendar P&L is small relative to coin moves, so hedge coin premium/collateral delta if USD-accounted.
strategies.metals_notes: GC short-dated options allow a calendar around FOMC (sell the pre-FOMC weekly, buy the post-FOMC weekly). GLD route identical to equities.
variants: Double calendar (OTM call cal + OTM put cal)
Diagonal: far leg one strike OTM in the direction of drift
Reverse calendar for the crush (see earnings-reverse-calendar)
strategies.claim: An ATM calendar short the last pre-earnings weekly and long the first post-earnings expiry, opened 10-15 trading days before the print and closed at the near expiry, has a positive mean return on debit net of half-spreads.

trial.statistic: Mean return on debit, hit rate, bootstrap CI.
trial.procedure: From chain captures, mark both legs at entry and at the near-expiry close; compute return; test monotonicity across terciles of term-structure slope (IV_far - IV_near) at entry.
trial.data: Daily chain captures with weekly expiries for ~200 names; earnings dates.
trial.pass: Mean > 0 with 95% CI excluding 0; flattest-slope tercile outperforms steepest.
trial.controls: Same calendar in windows with no earnings between the expiries (placebo); exclude names with an ex-date between legs.

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture through 2+ earnings seasons; earnings-date history.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Store term-structure slope per symbol per day (IV_near vs IV_event); mark-to-market via BS reprice.

strategies.name: Pre-earnings long straddle (buy the IV ramp, exit before the print)

legs.expiry_rule: first expiry AFTER the earnings date (7-21 DTE at entry)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(S-K,0)+max(K-S,0)-D = |S-K|-D, D = call+put debit. Normally closed at the last close before the announcement, so realised P&L is mark-to-market: approx vega*(IV_exit-IV_entry) + 0.5*gamma*dS^2 + theta*dt (theta<0).
strategies.max_profit: If held: unlimited as S->inf; K-D as S->0. If exited pre-print: bounded by vega*dIV + gamma P&L - theta decay.
strategies.max_loss: D (net debit), at S_T=K. Pre-print exit loss is roughly theta decay minus the IV ramp.
strategies.breakevens: At expiry: K-D and K+D. Pre-print (flat spot): dIV >= |theta|*days/vega.

greeks_at_inception.delta: approx 0, slightly positive (for K=S the call delta N(d1) > 0.5 since d1=(r+sigma^2/2)sqrt(T)/sigma > 0)
greeks_at_inception.vega: positive (long event-expiry vega, the point of the trade)

strategies.when_to_use: 3-10 trading days before a scheduled earnings date when the event-expiry IV is below its own history of pre-earnings peaks (IV_now < median pre-print IV of the last 8 quarters). Published evidence (Gao-Xing-Zhang) is for T-3 to the announcement date. Exit at the last close before the announcement; never hold through (that is earnings-hold-through-straddle).
strategies.risks: Theta can exceed the IV ramp when the ramp is already priced; a pre-announcement (guidance warning, M&A) can gap the stock (good for long gamma) or crush IV early (bad); earnings dates move; single-name bid/ask can cost 2-5% of the straddle per round trip; no assignment risk (long only).
strategies.margin_note: Debit paid in full; no margin. Single-stock options are equity options, not Section 1256 (60/40 applies only to nonequity options such as SPX/XSP).
strategies.crypto_notes: No earnings, but the same ramp applies to scheduled catalysts (ETF decision dates, network upgrades, token unlocks). Buy the Deribit BTC/ETH straddle in the expiry after the date (expiries 08:00 UTC; daily/weekly/monthly listed). Deribit options are coin-settled: BTC payoff = max(S_T-K,0)/S_T or max(K-S_T,0)/S_T, which converted at S_T equals the vanilla USD payoff exactly; the inverse effect comes from premium and collateral held in coin (long-coin delta equal to the coin balance), so a USD-accounted book shorts that amount of perp/future. 24/7 trading: no overnight gap.
strategies.metals_notes: No earnings analogue. Nearest is buying GLD/GC straddles 3-5 days before FOMC/CPI when GVZ is below its pre-event median (see metals-macro-event-straddle). GC options are futures options: SPAN margin, Section 1256.
variants: T-3 to last pre-print close (published window)
T-7/T-10 to pre-print close (longer ramp, more theta)
Short-the-ramp inverse: sell straddle 10 days out, close day before
Calendarised: long event expiry, short same-strike expiry before earnings (see pre-earnings-calendar)
strategies.claim: For US large-cap stocks, an ATM straddle in the first expiry after earnings, bought at the close 3 trading days before the announcement and sold at the last close before it, has a positive mean return on debit net of half the quoted bid/ask spread.

trial.statistic: Mean per-trade return on debit with 95% studentized block-bootstrap CI (blocks by announcement week); secondary: mean dIV(T-3 -> T-1) vs mean theta decay as % of straddle.
trial.null: Mean net return <= 0 (IV ramp fully priced; theta >= ramp).
trial.procedure: For every earnings date in the capture window and every captured symbol: at close T-3 record the ATM straddle mid in the first post-earnings expiry; at the last pre-print close record the same straddle mid; return = (mid_exit - mid_entry - half-spread costs)/mid_entry. T-7 and T-10 entries are variants counted in the deflated-Sharpe trial count. Walk-forward: first season chooses any IV-percentile filter, later seasons test.
trial.data: Daily CBOE chain captures (bid/ask/IV) for ~200 liquid names from 2026-10-14; earnings dates from EDGAR 8-K Item 2.02 filings (free, not wired) or company IR calendars.
trial.pass: Bootstrap 95% CI for mean net return excludes 0 with point estimate > 1% of debit; deflated Sharpe p < 0.05.
trial.controls: Same structure on non-earnings 3-day windows for the same stocks (placebo); exclude windows with a VIX change > 10%; per-season sign test for stability.

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture through at least 1-2 earnings seasons (~90-180 days) for ~200 single names; earnings-date history (EDGAR, free, not wired).
strategies.harness_suggestion: Event-window harness: (symbol, event_date, offsets) -> straddle mid/IV path from the chain store; mark-to-market via BS reprice at captured IV with the payoff engine.

strategies.name: Pre-FOMC announcement drift call spread

legs.strike_rule: K1 ATM at the T-1 close (SPXW/XSP or SPY)
legs.expiry_rule: expiry on or just after FOMC day (1-3 DTE)

legs.strike_rule: K2 OTM 1% (about one event implied move)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: min(max(S-K1,0), K2-K1) - D; normally closed at 13:55 ET on FOMC day, before the statement.
strategies.max_loss: D.
strategies.breakevens: K1 + D.
strategies.when_to_use: Buy at the close the day before the FOMC decision, sell at 13:55 ET on decision day. Based on the Lucca-Moench pre-FOMC drift (large SPX excess return in the 24h before scheduled announcements, 1994-2011). The spread keeps the position cheap and less sensitive to the IV ramp.
strategies.risks: Follow-ups find the drift weakened after 2011; the short leg caps a large rally; 1-2 DTE theta is high; accidentally holding through the statement converts it into an event bet.
strategies.margin_note: Debit spread. SPX/XSP Section 1256; SPY not.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC's pre-FOMC pattern is weak and unstable; Deribit options expire 08:00 UTC, not near 14:00 ET, so use the weekly/daily after and close before the statement.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold's pre-FOMC drift is not documented as robust; test GLD separately before trading.
strategies.claim: SPY's close(T-1)-to-close(T) return on scheduled FOMC decision days exceeds its mean close-to-close return on non-FOMC days over the out-of-sample period 2012-2026.

trial.statistic: Mean return difference (FOMC minus non-FOMC), bootstrap/HAC CI; pre/post-2011 split.
trial.procedure: Daily closes only (the listed data has SPY closes, not opens), so close-to-close on day T, which includes the post-statement move (zero-mean noise for the drift test, but lower power). The true 13:55 ET window needs intraday data. Option overlay: BS-price the spread with VIX-as-IV at T-1 and at T (MODEL-PRICED).
trial.data: SPY daily closes since 1993, VIX, FOMC dates (Fed calendars).
trial.pass: Difference > 0 with 95% CI excluding 0 in 2012-2026 (about 120 meetings).
trial.controls: Random-date placebo; exclude unscheduled meetings; subtract the unconditional mean.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Event-window return harness over closes; flag that the 13:55 ET exit needs intraday capture.

strategies.name: SPX macro-event straddle (FOMC / CPI / NFP): event vol vs realised

legs.strike_rule: ATM (SPXW or XSP); side flips to SHORT when event IM/HM > 1.2
legs.expiry_rule: SPXW expiring the event day (0-1 DTE; PM-settled on the 4pm ET close) or the day after

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Long: |S_T - K| - D at SPXW settlement. Short: Cr - |S_T - K|.
strategies.max_profit: Long: unlimited upside; K-D as S->0. Short: Cr.
strategies.max_loss: Long: D. Short: unlimited upside; K-Cr downside (cash-settled, European, no assignment).
strategies.breakevens: K - premium and K + premium. Event implied move (mean-abs) = straddle/S; FOMC-day ATM straddles typically 0.8-1.3% of spot.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: strongly positive (long) / strongly negative (short) at 0-1 DTE
greeks_at_inception.vega: positive (long) / negative (short); IV collapses within minutes of the 14:00 ET statement or 8:30 ET CPI print

strategies.when_to_use: Long when the event-day straddle (bought at the prior close, or 13:55 ET on FOMC day) is cheap relative to trailing realised event moves and forecast dispersion is wide; short when rich. Variant: sell the 0DTE straddle at 14:05 ET after the statement to harvest the post-announcement crush.
strategies.risks: 0DTE gamma: a 1.5% move on the short side costs several credits; CPI/NFP at 8:30 ET fall inside SPX/SPXW Global Trading Hours (8:15 pm to 9:25 am ET), so the position can be adjusted then, but GTH liquidity is thin and spreads wide; FOMC presser can reverse the initial move.
strategies.margin_note: SPX/SPXW/XSP: cash-settled, European, Section 1256 nonequity options (60/40). Reg-T naked broad-index margin = premium + max(15%*index - OTM, 10%) ; portfolio margin stresses broad indexes about -8%/+6%. XSP (1/10 size) for sizing.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC/ETH react to FOMC/CPI; see crypto-macro-event-straddle.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold reacts strongly to FOMC/CPI/NFP; see metals-macro-event-straddle.
variants: Long event-day straddle bought prior close
Long straddle bought 13:55 ET on FOMC day
Short 0DTE straddle sold 14:05 ET after the statement
Short day-after straddle sold at the event-day close
strategies.claim: On scheduled FOMC decision days since 1994, a 1-day ATM SPY straddle model-priced with VIX-as-IV (sigma = VIX at the T-1 close, T = 1/252) and sold at the T-1 close has a lower mean P&L than the same model-priced straddle sold on non-FOMC days, i.e. the 30-day VIX does not embed the FOMC-day event variance.

trial.statistic: Difference in mean P&L (FOMC minus non-FOMC) of the MODEL-PRICED short straddle (BS, sigma=VIX_{T-1}, T=1/252, settled on |SPY_T - SPY_{T-1}|), bootstrap CI; also mean of |r_T|/(VIX_{T-1}/sqrt(252)) by group.
trial.null: FOMC-day mean P&L >= non-FOMC mean P&L.
trial.procedure: FOMC decision dates 1994-2026 (about 260, from Fed calendars, hardcoded); price and settle each day; compare with all non-FOMC days; stratify by VIX tercile; estimate on 1994-2010, confirm on 2011-2026. This is a proxy: traded event-expiry straddles carry an event premium that VIX-as-IV cannot see; the traded version needs SPXW chain capture.
trial.data: SPY daily closes since 1993, VIX daily since 1990, FOMC dates.
trial.pass: Difference < 0 with 95% CI excluding 0 in both halves.
trial.controls: Placebo dates (FOMC +/- 7 days); exclude 2008-09 and 2020-03; trailing ratio of 1-day to 30-day realised vol as a scale check.

strategies.harness_suggestion: VIX-as-IV straddle pricer over an event-date list, outputs labelled MODEL-PRICED; rerun for CPI/NFP when BLS release dates are hardcoded (bls.gov blocks plain fetches).

strategies.name: Triple witching / quarterly rebalance close (long gamma into the close)

legs.expiry_rule: SPXW PM-settled expiring that quarterly third Friday (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec), or SPY same-day

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: |S_T - K| - D at the 4pm settlement, when the closing auction carries index rebalance and expiry flows.
strategies.max_profit: Unlimited upside; K - D downside.
strategies.max_loss: D (one hour of ATM premium, about 0.8*sigma_day*sqrt(1/6.5)*S, roughly 0.2-0.3% of spot).
strategies.breakevens: K - D and K + D.
strategies.when_to_use: Quarterly triple-witching Fridays (index futures, index options and stock options expire; S&P quarterly rebalance trades at the close), plus Russell reconstitution and MSCI semi-annual closes. Buy at 15:00, hold to 4pm. Inverse: short the straddle if the last-hour move is historically smaller than implied. Do not trade before the test.
strategies.risks: Daily data cannot see the last hour; SPX monthlies settle on Friday's opening prices, so the PM move is only tradable via SPXW/SPY; premium is tiny so fees matter; the sign (pin vs imbalance move) is empirical.
strategies.margin_note: Debit; SPX/XSP Section 1256.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit quarterly expiry (last Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec, 08:00 UTC) is crypto's witching; buy the daily straddle at 07:00 UTC into settlement, noting that settlement uses a 30-minute index average before 08:00 UTC (per Deribit), which damps the final move.
strategies.metals_notes: GC quarterly option expiry and first-notice flows are the analogue; GC daily settlement window is around 13:29-13:30 ET.
variants: Long straddle from Thursday close through Friday close (daily-data proxy)
strategies.claim: A 1-day ATM SPY straddle model-priced with VIX-as-IV (sigma = VIX at Thursday's close, T = 1/252), bought at Thursday's close and settled at Friday's close, has a higher mean P&L on quarterly triple-witching Fridays than on other Fridays.

trial.statistic: Difference in mean MODEL-PRICED long-straddle P&L (witching minus other Fridays), bootstrap CI and permutation p-value.
trial.procedure: Quarterly third Fridays since 1993; SPY closes; VIX; settle on |SPY_Fri - SPY_Thu|. This tests the close-to-close proxy only; the 15:00-16:00 claim needs an intraday capture at 15:00 ET (blocked).
trial.data: SPY daily closes, VIX, computed calendar.
trial.pass: Difference > 0 with 95% CI excluding 0 and permutation p < 0.05.
trial.controls: Monthly non-quarterly opex Fridays as a separate control; exclude witching days with FOMC; pre/post-2010 split.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Event-day vs matched-weekday comparison harness with the VIX-as-IV pricer; add a 15:00 ET SPY/SPX snapshot to the daily job for the real test.

strategies.name: VIX settlement (Wednesday SOQ) call credit spread

legs.expiry_rule: VIX options expiring the next settlement Wednesday, entered 3-5 DTE

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Cr - min(max(VIX_SOQ - K1, 0), K2 - K1), settled in cash on the Special Opening Quotation computed from opening SPX option prices on the settlement Wednesday.
strategies.max_profit: Cr (if SOQ <= K1).
strategies.max_loss: (K2 - K1) - Cr (if SOQ >= K2).
strategies.breakevens: K1 + Cr.

greeks_at_inception.delta: negative to the VIX future (bearish vol)

strategies.when_to_use: VIX options settle to the SOQ calculated from the opening prices of the SPX series that define 30-day VIX on settlement morning (usually a Wednesday; the expiration is the Wednesday 30 days before the following month's standard SPX expiry). Two regularities to test: (1) under contango the front future tends to drift down into settlement; (2) SOQ deviations from the prior close and post-open VIX (Griffin-Shams). Trade (1) with this call credit spread. Variant (2) is selling far-OTM SPX puts into the opening auction, which is a separate, naked, high-risk trade.
strategies.risks: VIX spikes are discontinuous; max loss is several times the credit; Cboe has changed SOQ procedures over time, so historical deviations may not recur.
strategies.margin_note: VIX options: cash-settled, European; nonequity options so Section 1256. Spread margin = width - credit.
strategies.crypto_notes: No VIX-style settlement event; DVOL is an index with DVOL futures but no comparable SOQ. Deribit's 08:00 UTC expiry with a 30-minute index average is the closest settlement-window effect.
strategies.metals_notes: GVZ has no listed options with a settlement event; not applicable.
variants: Short VIX call spread into Wednesday (contango roll-down)
Short VIX straddle expiring Wednesday when VIX3M/VIX > 1.1
SOQ far-OTM SPX put sale at the Wednesday open (separate naked trade)
Long VIX call spread when VIX3M/VIX < 1 (backwardation)
strategies.claim: A VIX call credit spread (short front-future+2, long +5 higher) expiring at the Wednesday SOQ and sold 3 trading days before settlement when VIX3M/VIX > 1.1 has a positive mean return on max loss net of half-spreads.

trial.statistic: Mean return on max loss with bootstrap CI; preliminary: mean (VRO - VIX close on the prior day) on settlement days vs mean daily VIX change on other Wednesdays.
trial.procedure: Settlement calendar since 2006 (computable); front-future level from Cboe CFE settlement history; option entry credit from captured VIX chains (from today) or Black-76 with VVIX as vol-of-vol (MODEL-PRICED); settlement from VRO (free Cboe CSV since 2008).
trial.data: VIX, VIX3M daily OHLC (listed); VRO and VVIX daily history (free Cboe CSVs, not in the current list); VIX futures settlement history (free CFE files, not wired); VIX option chain captures from 2026-10-14.
trial.pass: Mean > 0 with 95% CI excluding 0.
trial.controls: Backwardation subsample; non-settlement Wednesdays for the SOQ-deviation check; exclude 2008, 2018-02, 2020-03 as robustness.

strategies.blocked_on: VIX futures settlement history (free CFE files, not wired) plus either VIX chain capture (~12+ monthly settlements) or a VVIX-based model price; VRO history (free) enables the preliminary SOQ test.
strategies.harness_suggestion: VIX settlement calendar generator; VRO/VIX/VIX3M event harness; CFE futures fetcher; Black-76 VIX option pricer with VVIX.

strategies.name: Weekend / holiday theta harvest (short straddle over non-trading periods)

legs.expiry_rule: weekly expiring the following week (3-8 DTE), sold at Friday's (or pre-holiday) close

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Cr - |S - K|; normally bought back at Monday's (post-holiday) close.
strategies.max_profit: Cr.
strategies.max_loss: Unlimited upside; K - Cr downside.
strategies.breakevens: K - Cr and K + Cr.

greeks_at_inception.theta: positive (calendar days elapse with little trading-day variance)

strategies.when_to_use: Jones-Shemesh find option returns are significantly lower over non-trading periods (mostly weekends): markets under-adjust prices for the low variance of weekends. Sell Friday close, cover Monday close; long weekends add a day.
strategies.risks: Weekend news gaps (geopolitical, policy) hit the short at Monday's open; the effect is known and may be arbitraged; spreads on entry and exit.
strategies.margin_note: Naked short straddle margin; defined-risk iron butterfly variant = wing width - credit. SPX/XSP Section 1256.
strategies.crypto_notes: Natural control: Deribit trades 24/7, so there is no non-trading period, yet weekend realised vol is lower; test whether Deribit marks decay over weekends as fast as realised vol falls.
strategies.metals_notes: GC options trade from Sunday evening; GLD follows equity hours (same weekend effect).
strategies.claim: Market-quoted ATM SPY straddles in the next weekly expiry lose a larger share of their mid value from Friday close to Monday close than from Monday close to Tuesday close, net of the realised move.

trial.statistic: Mean short-straddle P&L/credit (Fri->Mon) minus (Mon->Tue), paired by week, bootstrap CI.
trial.procedure: Chain captures at each daily close; mark the same contract on both windows; subtract half-spread costs.
trial.data: Daily SPY/SPX chain captures from 2026-10-14.
trial.pass: Difference > 0 with 95% CI excluding 0 over >= 30 weeks.
trial.controls: Holiday weekends separately; Deribit BTC weekend vs weekday as the 24/7 control; exclude weeks with Monday macro releases.

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture for at least 30 weeks (traded marks are required; VIX-as-IV cannot test a pricing anomaly).
strategies.harness_suggestion: Same-contract mark tracker (contract id -> daily mid path) on the chain store.

strategies.name: Call-spread overwrite (covered call with upside re-entry)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: S_T - S0 - max(S_T - K1, 0) + max(S_T - K2, 0) + cr, cr = C(K1) - C(K2) > 0. Slope 1 below K1, 0 between K1 and K2, 1 above K2
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded (S_T - S0 - (K2 - K1) + cr above K2)
strategies.breakevens: S_T = S0 - cr (and, if K1 - S0 + cr < 0, a second crossing at S_T = S0 + (K2 - K1) - cr above K2)

greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative near K1, positive near K2; net negative
greeks_at_inception.vega: negative, less than a plain covered call

strategies.when_to_use: An overwriter who fears missing a large rally (single stocks with event risk, BTC ETFs, gold) gives up part of the premium to restore upside above K2. It is a covered call plus a cheap OTM call.
strategies.risks: Lower premium than a plain covered call; the long wing decays to zero in most months; the dead zone K1..K2 still caps moderate rallies; the 1x1 call vertical carries pin and assignment risk at K1.
strategies.margin_note: The short K1 call is covered by stock; the long K2 call needs payment in full (or the pair is margined as a bear call spread, margin K2 - K1 - cr, if not treated as covered).
strategies.crypto_notes: Most useful on BTC, where right-tail months dominate returns. On Deribit the K2 wing is inverse, so its BTC payoff is (S - K2)/S, saturating at 1 BTC per contract.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold call skew makes the K2 wing relatively expensive on GLD/GC, so the overwrite gives up more premium there than on equities.
variants: overwrite + wing only when VIX percentile is high
strategies.claim: In a model-priced simulation on SPX from 1990 to 2026 (Black-Scholes at VIX, not market prices; this flat-IV pricer overprices OTM calls relative to the skewed market, so it is biased against the wing), a monthly short-ATM / long-5%-OTM call-spread overwrite has a higher Sharpe ratio than the plain ATM covered call priced the same way.

trial.statistic: Sharpe(call-spread overwrite) - Sharpe(ATM covered call), both model-priced on identical paths
trial.procedure: Model-priced on SPX daily with VIX-as-IV and DTB3, monthly 3rd-Friday rolls, 5 bps per leg slippage; calibration gate vs actual BXM (TE < 2%/yr); paired block bootstrap; walk-forward halves
trial.data: SPX daily, VIX 1990-, DTB3, SPY dividends, BXM for calibration
trial.pass: Calibration gate passed AND 95% CI of the Sharpe difference > 0 in both halves
trial.controls: SKEW-adjusted wing pricing as a sensitivity; a chain-priced re-test once ~24 monthly cohorts of SPY chain capture exist

strategies.harness_suggestion: Add as a two-call overlay in the model-priced overlay harness. Re-test with captured chains once ~24 monthly cohorts exist (from 2026-10-14) to remove the flat-IV bias.

strategies.name: Cash-secured put / put-write (Cboe PUT, PUTY, WPUT, PUTD)

legs.strike_rule: ATM (PUT: first strike at or below the index), 2% OTM (PUTY), or delta -0.30; cash = K held in T-bills
legs.expiry_rule: 1 month rolled on the 3rd Friday (PUT/PUTY); weekly (WPUT); dynamic (PUTD)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: P - max(K - S_T, 0) + T-bill interest on K
strategies.max_profit: P (+ interest)
strategies.max_loss: K - P (S_T -> 0), less interest
strategies.breakevens: S_T = K - P
strategies.when_to_use: Neutral to mildly bullish, willing to own the asset at K - P; harvests the variance premium on a fixed-income collateral base. By put-call parity it equals a covered call at the same strike and expiry plus T-bills; differences between the PUT and BXM indices come from implementation (strike rounding, roll timing, collateral).
strategies.risks: Substantial downside to zero; assignment leaves a long position in a falling market; margin calls if not fully cash-secured; weekly puts concentrate gamma; an IV spike marks the short put against you before expiry.
strategies.margin_note: Cash account: cash or escrow equal to the aggregate strike. Margin account (Cboe manual): 100% of premium + 20% of underlying (15% for broad-based index) minus the OTM amount, minimum premium + 10% of strike.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit inverse puts are collateralised in BTC, so a short BTC put is secured in a currency that falls exactly when the put goes ITM (wrong-way collateral). USDC linear puts (instrument_type 'linear', settlement USDC, verified) give a true cash-secured put.
strategies.metals_notes: Short OG/SO puts need SPAN margin, not full cash; GLD/SLV puts follow the 20% equity rule. An assigned GC put becomes a long GC future, not metal.
variants: PUT monthly ATM (Cboe CSV daily only from 2007-01)
defined-risk put-write (short put + long further-OTM put)
strategies.claim: Over 2007-01 to 2026-10, the Cboe PUT (ATM put-write) index has a higher monthly Sharpe ratio (excess over 3m T-bill) than the BXM (ATM buy-write) index.

trial.statistic: Sharpe(PUT) - Sharpe(BXM) on month-end excess returns, 2007-01 onward
trial.procedure: Cboe CDN PUT_History.csv. It has only 1-2 rows per year before 2007-01-03, with gaps up to 1,159 days, so start in 2007. Align with BXM_History.csv; excess returns over DTB3; studentized block bootstrap; walk-forward halves
trial.data: PUT (daily from 2007-01-03), BXM, FRED DTB3; PUTY 1986- and WPUT/PUTD 2006- as secondary arms
trial.pass: Bootstrap 95% CI of the Sharpe difference > 0 in the full sample, with the same sign in both halves
trial.controls: PUTY vs BXY (both 2% OTM, 1988-) as a longer parity check

strategies.harness_suggestion: Validate day counts before monthly sampling: PUT_History.csv is daily only from 2007-01-03 (its pre-2007 rows gave a spurious 25% vol). Recomputed today: WPUT 2006- CAGR 4.84% / vol 9.6% / maxDD -28.6%; PUTD 2006- 9.67% / 12.0%; PUTY 1986- 6.89% / 8.7% / maxDD -40.6%.

strategies.name: Cboe options-overlay benchmark family as replication targets (BXM/BXMD/BXY/BXMC/BXMH/BXMW/PUT/PUTY/CLL/CLLZ/CMBO/PPUT/BFLY/CNDR/VXTH)

legs.strike_rule: S&P 500 total-return basket (SPX; Nasdaq-100 for BXN; Russell 2000 for BXR)
per index: ATM at or above (BXM/BXN/BXR), delta 0.30 (BXMD), 2% OTM (BXY), ATM 0.5 unit (BXMH), ATM 0.5 or 1 unit by VIX < or >= 20 (BXMC), four staggered 4-week ATM tranches (BXMW)
legs.expiry_rule: 1 month; BXM written on the 3rd-Friday roll day at the 11:30-12:00 ET VWAP of the new call; expiring call settled at the SOQ

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: min(S_T, K) - S0 + C with the index's K rule; premium and dividends are 'functionally reinvested' (total return)
strategies.max_profit: K - S0 + C
strategies.max_loss: S0 - C
strategies.breakevens: S_T = S0 - C
strategies.when_to_use: Use as the realised, free, multi-decade ground truth for calibrating Mandel's model-priced overlays: any VIX-as-IV simulation must reproduce BXM and PUT within tolerance before its results are trusted.
strategies.risks: Indices are hypothetical: no fees, VWAP fills, SOQ settlement. ETF replication (XYLD on BXM since Aug 2020, QYLD on BXNT) lags by 0.60% fees plus tracking. Price-only SPX understates the benchmark (dividends ~1.3-2%/yr). Several free CSVs start later than the index base date (BXM 2002-03, CLL 2008-08, BXN/GVZ/VIX3M 2009-09), and PUT is sparse before 2007.
strategies.margin_note: n/a (benchmark); replication margin per covered-call rules.
strategies.crypto_notes: No official benchmark; DVOL-based model replication is needed (and must be labelled model-priced).
strategies.metals_notes: No Cboe gold buy-write index in the free CDN set; GVZ (CSV from 2009-09) is the vol reference.
strategies.claim: A Black-Scholes overlay simulation on SPX (model-priced, with VIX as the implied vol and FRED DTB3 as the rate) reproduces the monthly returns of BXM (2002-2026) and PUT (2007-2026) with R^2 > 0.95 and annualised tracking error below 2%.

trial.statistic: R^2 and annualised tracking error between simulated and actual monthly returns for BXM and PUT (secondary: BXMD, CNDR)
trial.null: R^2 <= 0.95 or TE >= 2%/yr for either BXM or PUT
trial.procedure: Simulate each index's strike/roll rule on SPX daily with VIX (SKEW-based OTM adjustment for BXMD/CNDR as a documented sensitivity), compare with downloaded histories, and report by sub-period. Use SPX price plus SPY dividends (Yahoo chart events=div) for the total-return leg.
trial.data: SPX daily, VIX, SKEW, DTB3, SPY dividends, Cboe benchmark CSVs
trial.pass: R^2 > 0.95 and TE < 2%/yr for both BXM and PUT; document the shortfall for BXMD/CNDR (skew)
trial.controls: Price-only vs total-return SPX; VWAP vs close fill assumption

strategies.harness_suggestion: Run this first: extend options.py with a CBOE_BENCHMARKS list (all of the above return HTTP 200 on the CDN today; the CDN 307-redirects to cdn-api.cboe.com) and gate every model-priced claim on this calibration.

strategies.name: Collar (protective collar; Cboe CLL 95-110)

legs.strike_rule: OTM 5% (CLL: 95% of index, closest listed at or below) or delta -0.20 to -0.30
legs.expiry_rule: CLL: quarterly (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec); generic: same expiry as the call

legs.strike_rule: OTM 10% (CLL: 110%) or delta 0.20-0.30; K_p < S0 < K_c
legs.expiry_rule: CLL: monthly, rolled on the 3rd Friday; generic: same expiry as the put

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: (same-expiry version) max(K_p, min(S_T, K_c)) - S0 - (P - C)
strategies.max_profit: K_c - S0 - (P - C) (i.e. minus a net debit, or plus a net credit)
strategies.max_loss: S0 - K_p + (P - C)
strategies.breakevens: S_T = S0 + (P - C), valid when K_p <= S0 + (P - C) <= K_c

greeks_at_inception.gamma: mixed: positive near K_p, negative near K_c; small net
greeks_at_inception.theta: small; usually slightly negative for CLL 95-110 (the put is nearer spot and longer-dated)
greeks_at_inception.vega: small; slightly positive for CLL 95-110 (a 5% OTM quarterly put carries more vega than a 10% OTM monthly call); long put skew

strategies.when_to_use: The holder wants a hard floor (concentrated stock, pre-earnings, tax-deferred holding) and will give up upside above K_c to pay for it. Cheapest when skew is flat.
strategies.risks: The floor is only at K_p, and upside is capped. In CLL, the monthly call and quarterly put force cross-rolls when the call strike falls below the standing put strike. Early assignment on the call before dividends. Collars on employer or appreciated stock can raise constructive-sale and legal issues.
strategies.margin_note: Cboe manual 'Collar' requires the put and call to share an expiry with put strike < call strike. Margin account: pay for the put in full, no requirement on the call, 50% on the stock. Maintenance on the stock is the lower of 10% of the put strike plus any put OTM amount, or 25% of the call strike (American-style). CLL's mixed expiries (quarterly put, monthly call) do NOT qualify for collar treatment; margin it as covered call plus long put.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit collars are quoted and settled in BTC. The inverse put's BTC payoff (K - S_T)/S_T converts to (K - S_T) USD only at S_T, so the USD floor holds per contract, but the BTC premium paid shrinks in USD. Use USDC linear options (instrument_type 'linear', verified) for a clean USD collar.
strategies.metals_notes: GC collars via OG puts/calls settle into futures; GLD collars are equity-style. Gold often has call-side skew, so 95-110 collars on gold are rarely cheap on the call side.
variants: CLL1M Risk Managed Income (5% OTM put + ATM call, monthly; 2004-)
strategies.claim: Over 2008-08 to 2026-10, the Cboe CLL 95-110 collar index has a lower CAGR than a beta-matched (OLS beta ~0.63) SPY-total-return/T-bill blend.

trial.statistic: CAGR(CLL) - CAGR(blend), where blend = beta*SPY TR + (1-beta)*T-bill, rebalanced monthly
trial.procedure: Cboe CDN CLL_History.csv (2008-08-26 onward; the methodology base date is 1986 but the free CSV starts 2008; it has gaps up to 11 days, so use month-ends); SPY TR from the Yahoo chart adjclose; DTB3; estimate beta on the first half and apply it out of sample to the second; block bootstrap
trial.data: CLL 4,520 rows, SPY closes plus dividends, FRED DTB3
trial.pass: Bootstrap 95% CI of the CAGR difference entirely below 0
trial.controls: CLL1M and CLL3M (2004-) as alternative collars; PPUT (put only) to isolate the call leg; CLLZ (1986-) as the long-history collar

strategies.harness_suggestion: Recomputed today on 2008-08-26 to 2026-10: CLL CAGR 6.96% / vol 12.3% / maxDD -26.3% / beta 0.63 / worst month -20.6% (check that month for CSV gaps); SPX price CAGR 10.53% / maxDD -48.0% (the 2009 low is in-sample); PPUT on the same window 10.00% / maxDD -27.3%.

strategies.name: Covered call / buy-write (ATM, BXM-style)

legs.strike_rule: ATM (BXM rule: first listed strike at or above the last S&P 500 value before 11:00 ET on roll day)
legs.expiry_rule: 1 month; written on the 3rd-Friday roll day at the 11:30-12:00 ET VWAP of the new call, old call settled at the SOQ; weekly variant 7 DTE

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: S_T - S0 + C - max(S_T - K, 0) = min(S_T, K) - S0 + C
strategies.max_profit: K - S0 + C (for any S_T >= K)
strategies.max_loss: S0 - C (S_T -> 0). Upside above K is forgone, which is an opportunity cost and not a loss
strategies.breakevens: S_T = S0 - C
strategies.when_to_use: The holder is neutral to mildly bullish and believes implied vol is rich relative to the realised vol to come; the only economic edge is the variance risk premium. OIC: the strategy is not appropriate for a very bearish or a very bullish investor.
strategies.risks: Full downside of the stock less premium; capped upside and tracking error in sharp rallies (BXM lags SPX strongly in up months); early assignment before an ex-dividend date; the ATM strike resets each month, which locks in path dependence (assigned after rebounds, overwritten at lows); mark-to-market vega loss when IV spikes.
strategies.margin_note: Cboe Margin Manual: a short call against long underlying needs no margin on the call; the stock needs 50% initial and 25% maintenance (Reg T), and is valued at the lower of market or strike for margin equity. In a cash account the stock is paid in full. Broker APIs (IBKR/Schwab/Tasty) treat it as a strategy-based covered position.
strategies.crypto_notes: On IBIT it is an ordinary American-style equity option. On Deribit the call is inverse: premium and P&L are in BTC, settlement_currency BTC, contract_size 1 BTC (min 0.1), European, cash-settled at 08:00 UTC to the 07:30-08:00 index TWAP. It is therefore a true covered call only in coin terms (see the deribit-covered-call-inverse entry). No dividends; trades 24/7; daily, weekly and monthly expiries (verified via public/get_instruments today: settlement_period day/week/month).
strategies.metals_notes: GLD/SLV: equity-style American options under Reg T; the ETF leg is taxed as a collectible (28% max LT rate). GC/SI: options on futures (OG/SO) on 100 oz / 5,000 oz contracts that exercise into the future, SPAN margin, Section 1256 60/40 on both the future and the option. The OG option termination rule was not verified this pass (CME page 403).
variants: ATM monthly (BXM; Cboe CSV history from 2002-03-22)
conditional overwrite (BXMC: full unit if VIX >= 20 on roll day, else half unit)
futures-based: long ES + short ES call
strategies.claim: Over 2002-03 to 2026-10, monthly excess returns of the Cboe BXM index over the 3-month T-bill have a positive Jensen alpha against SPY total-return excess returns (beta ~0.63), i.e. ATM overwriting adds return beyond its reduced equity exposure.

trial.statistic: Intercept (annualised alpha) of an OLS regression of BXM monthly excess return on SPY total-return monthly excess return
trial.null: alpha <= 0 (overwriting is just de-risking; no variance premium captured)
trial.procedure: Pull BXM_History.csv (Cboe CDN; it redirects to cdn-api.cboe.com and starts 2002-03-22). Build SPY total return from the Yahoo chart endpoint with events=div / adjclose (the archived daily-history-SPY rows hold only the unadjusted close). Take FRED DTB3, sample month-ends, run OLS with HAC standard errors, stationary block bootstrap (12-month blocks) of alpha, and split into walk-forward halves.
trial.data: BXM 2002-03-22 onward (6,177 daily rows); SPY closes plus dividends 1993 onward; FRED DTB3
trial.pass: Bootstrap 95% CI of annualised alpha > 0 in the full sample, with a positive point estimate in both halves
trial.controls: Israelov & Nielsen decomposition: compare with a beta-matched SPY-TR/T-bill blend; price-only SPX as a sensitivity (it biases against SPX by ~2%/yr of dividends)

strategies.harness_suggestion: Add BXM, BXMD, BXY, BXMC, BXMH, BXMW, BXN, BXR, PUT, PUTY, WPUT, PUTD, CLL, CLL1M, CLL3M, CLLZ, PPUT, PPUT3M, CMBO, BFLY, CNDR, BXMVM and VXTH to a CBOE_BENCHMARKS list in mandel/data/options.py (same single-column CSV format; CBOE_INDICES currently holds only vol indices). Re-pull SPY with adjclose/dividends. Sanity figures recomputed today: BXM 2002-03 to 2026-10 CAGR 6.23%, vol 10.6%, maxDD -40.1%, beta 0.63, vs SPX price-only CAGR 8.11%, vol 14.9%.

strategies.name: Covered call on gold/silver (GLD/SLV equity route; GC/SI futures-options route)

legs.strike_rule: GLD/SLV shares at S0, or a long GC future (100 oz) / SI future (5,000 oz)
OTM 3-5% or delta 0.25-0.30 (gold call-side skew makes OTM calls relatively rich)
legs.expiry_rule: monthly or weekly; OG options expire before the underlying futures month (exact termination rule not verified this pass, CME page 403)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: min(S_T, K) - S0 + C (futures version in $/oz x contract size)
strategies.max_profit: K - S0 + C
strategies.max_loss: S0 - C
strategies.breakevens: S_T = S0 - C
strategies.when_to_use: A holder of bullion exposure wants carry. Metals pay no dividend, and the futures route also pays contango roll cost. A positive gold variance premium (GVZ above realised), if present, is the overwrite's edge.
strategies.risks: Gold rallies are often gap-like (macro shocks), which is why the skew is to calls. GLD option gains are taxed as equity options while GLD itself is a collectible (28% LT): a mismatch. GC route: futures margin calls, rolls, and exercise into a futures position. SLV IV is materially higher than GLD's.
strategies.margin_note: GLD/SLV: equity covered-call treatment (no margin on the call). GC/SI: SPAN on the futures+option combination; both legs Section 1256 (60/40).
assets: futures-options (GC/OG, SI/SO, MGC micro gold options)
strategies.crypto_notes: n/a
strategies.metals_notes: Fetched (KGI mirror of the CME GC FUTURES spec): 100 troy oz, Globex Sun-Fri 18:00-17:00 ET; futures listed for 3 consecutive months plus Feb/Apr/Aug/Oct within 23 months and Jun/Dec within 72 months; futures trading terminates on the third last business day of the contract month. Option (OG) listing and termination were not verified (CME page returned 403).
variants: gold collar (GLD put + call) for bullion treasuries
strategies.claim: From 2009-09 to 2026-10, Cboe GVZ exceeds the subsequent 21-trading-day realised volatility of GLD daily closes by at least 2 vol points on average.

trial.statistic: Mean of (GVZ_t - RV_GLD,{t, t+21}), RV annualised with 252 days
trial.procedure: Cboe GVZ history (the free CSV starts 2009-09-18) vs realised vol from archived GLD closes; HAC (lag 21) or stationary block bootstrap; walk-forward halves; report the SPX VRP (VIX vs SPY RV) on the same dates for scale
trial.data: GVZ 2009-09 onward, GLD daily closes (archived daily-history-GLD, 2004-11 onward), VIX, SPY
trial.pass: Lower 95% CI of the mean > 2 vol points, with the same sign in both halves
trial.controls: Exclude 2011 and 2020 spikes one at a time; OVX/USO as another commodity reference

strategies.harness_suggestion: GVZ is already in CBOE_INDICES and GLD/SLV closes are already archived, so reuse the VRP harness directly. GC futures closes are not free; use GLD as the proxy.

strategies.name: Covered call on IBIT / spot-bitcoin ETF

legs.strike_rule: OTM 5-10% or delta 0.25-0.30 (BTC IV makes ATM caps tight)
legs.expiry_rule: weekly to monthly; IBIT lists weeklies

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: min(S_T, K) - S0 + C
strategies.max_profit: K - S0 + C
strategies.max_loss: S0 - C
strategies.breakevens: S_T = S0 - C

greeks_at_inception.theta: positive, large in absolute terms (high IV)

strategies.when_to_use: A holder of a spot-BTC ETF wants yield from BTC's high implied vol (Deribit DVOL closed at 38.6 on 2026-10-14) on a regulated US venue. IBIT options are American and physically settled in ETF shares, with OCC position limits.
strategies.risks: BTC upside is fat-tailed, so caps forfeit the largest months. The ETF trades only in US hours while BTC moves 24/7 (gap risk at the open, weekend gaps). IV can collapse after rallies; no dividends; IBIT options are not Section 1256 (ordinary equity-option treatment).
strategies.margin_note: Equity covered-call rules (no margin on the call; shares 50%).
strategies.crypto_notes: Compared with Deribit: USD-denominated premium, no inverse convexity, no funding, but no weekend trading and OCC position limits. Mandel captures the IBIT chain daily (IBIT is in CHAIN_SYMBOLS) and has IBIT closes since 2024-01-11 archived.
strategies.metals_notes: n/a
variants: covered call + protective put (BTC collar) for treasury holders
strategies.claim: From 2021-03-24 to 2026-10, Deribit BTC DVOL exceeds the subsequent 30-calendar-day realised volatility of BTC daily closes by more than 5 vol points on average.

trial.statistic: Mean of (DVOL_t - RV_{t, t+30d}), RV annualised with 365 days
trial.procedure: Page public/get_volatility_index_data backwards (it returns at most ~1000 daily rows per call) to get the full 2021-03-24 onward series (2,031 rows today). Compute forward 30-day realised vol from BTC daily closes. Use non-overlapping or HAC (lag 30) inference, stationary block bootstrap, walk-forward halves. Repeat for ETH.
trial.data: DVOL BTC/ETH 2021-03 onward (paged), BTC/ETH daily closes (archived), Deribit get_historical_volatility (384 rows) as a cross-check
trial.pass: Lower 95% CI of the mean gap > 5 vol points, with the same sign in both halves
trial.controls: The same statistic for SPX (VIX vs forward RV) as the known-positive reference; crash months (May-21, Nov-22) kept in. The IBIT-vs-DVOL IV basis is measured separately from the daily IBIT chain capture.

strategies.harness_suggestion: The BTC-VRP harness exists. Make deribit_dvol_history page backwards by end_timestamp: the endpoint 400s without start/end timestamps and caps rows per call. Report the expected premium capture of a 30-delta covered call via Black-Scholes at DVOL as a labelled model-priced extra.

strategies.name: Covered put (short stock + short put)

legs.strike_rule: OTM (K < S0) or ATM; OIC's arbitrage variant uses a deep-ITM put trading near intrinsic

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: S0 - S_T - max(K - S_T, 0) + P = S0 - max(S_T, K) + P. By parity this is the payoff of a naked short call at K
strategies.max_profit: S0 - K + P (S_T <= K), plus interest on short proceeds
strategies.max_loss: Unlimited (S_T rises; short stock)
strategies.breakevens: S_T = S0 + P

greeks_at_inception.delta: negative (-1 + |put delta| ~ -0.5 ATM to -0.7 for 30-delta OTM)

strategies.when_to_use: A bearish-to-neutral holder of a short position wants income and a target cover price; the mirror image of the covered call. Used by short sellers to offset borrow cost; OIC also describes a deep-ITM interest-arbitrage variant.
strategies.risks: Unlimited upside loss; borrow fees and recalls; dividends owed on the short; put assignment buys stock at K and closes the short (ending the position).
strategies.margin_note: Cboe manual 'Short Put and Short Underlying': not permitted in a cash account. Margin account: no requirement on the put; short sale proceeds plus 50% initial; maintenance on the short is 100% of market value plus the greater of $5/share or 30% (stocks >= $5), plus any amount by which the put strike exceeds the stock price.
assets: futures-options (short GC future + short OG put)
strategies.crypto_notes: A short Deribit perpetual replaces short stock, with funding received or paid replacing borrow; the short put is inverse.
strategies.metals_notes: Short GC future + short OG put is the clean version (no borrow); SPAN recognises the hedge.
variants: covered put with protective long call (reverse collar)
strategies.claim: In a model-priced simulation (Black-Scholes at VIX, not market prices) of short SPX + short monthly ATM SPX puts with T-bill interest on proceeds, the CAGR is negative in at least 90% of rolling 120-month windows from 1990 to 2026.

trial.statistic: Fraction of rolling 120-month windows with negative CAGR (model-priced)
trial.procedure: Model-priced with VIX-as-IV on SPX daily, monthly rolls, T-bill interest on short proceeds, dividends owed on the short; pricer must first pass the BXM/PUT calibration gate
trial.data: SPX price 1975-, SPY dividends (Yahoo chart events=div), VIX 1990-, FRED DTB3
trial.pass: Fraction of negative windows >= 0.9
trial.controls: Short SPX alone to isolate the put income

strategies.harness_suggestion: Low priority: include for completeness of the payoff library. The claim is mostly a sign-convention check of the engine (it is the parity twin of a naked short call).

strategies.name: Covered ratio spread / 1x2 ratio write

legs.strike_rule: K1: OTM ~5% (OIC example: stock 60, short 2x 65 calls)
K2 > K1 (OIC example 70): caps the second short call

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: S_T - S0 - 2*max(S_T - K1, 0) + max(S_T - K2, 0) + cr (cr = net credit). Slope +1 below K1, -1 between K1 and K2, 0 above K2. The naked 1x2 (no K2 call) has slope -1 above K1
strategies.max_profit: K1 - S0 + cr (at S_T = K1)
strategies.max_loss: S0 - cr (stock to zero). The plateau above K2 is 2*K1 - K2 - S0 + cr, which is a loss only if K2 - K1 > K1 - S0 + cr; the naked version has unlimited upside loss
strategies.breakevens: Downside: S_T = S0 - cr. Upside: S_T = 2*K1 - S0 + cr, which exists in the covered version only when 2*K1 - S0 + cr < K2 and always exists in the naked 1x2
strategies.when_to_use: Expect a slight rise to around K1; lowers the breakeven of an underwater holding (stock repair when the long call is ATM instead). Rich call skew (crypto bull regimes, gold) enlarges the 1x2 credit.
strategies.risks: The second short call is covered only up to K2 (or not at all in the naked version). Assignment on both calls leaves a short stock position until the K2 call is exercised. A sharp rally can turn the plateau into a loss if K2 is far from K1.
strategies.margin_note: One short call is covered by stock. The other is spread against the long K2 call: no requirement since it is a debit-or-even bear call vertical, margin = K2 - K1 if a credit vertical. Naked version: 20% of underlying + premium - OTM amount, minimum 10%.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC call skew in bull regimes pays well for 1x2 call writes. In BTC terms the naked short call's loss (S_T - K)/S_T is bounded by 1 BTC per contract, but in USD it is unbounded; cap it with the K2 call.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold call skew makes GLD/GC 1x2s credit-rich; uncovered OG calls take SPAN margin.
variants: OIC covered ratio (2 short K1, 1 long K2)
stock repair (long 1 ATM call, short 2 OTM calls; separate entry)
strategies.claim: For SPY, the mean monthly P&L of the 1x2 overlay (short 2x 5%-OTM calls, long 1x 10%-OTM call, 30 DTE, held to expiry) minus a single 5%-OTM covered call overlay is higher when the prior 5%-to-10% OTM call IV slope is in its top quartile than when it is in its bottom quartile.

trial.statistic: Difference in mean overlay-P&L spread (1x2 minus single OTM call) between the top and bottom quartiles of the entry-day call-skew slope
trial.procedure: Daily SPY chain capture: on each capture day record 5%/10% OTM ~30-DTE call mids and IVs; settle each overlapping cohort at expiry with SPY closes; stratify by entry skew slope; block bootstrap by expiry cohort
trial.data: Daily chain capture (from 2026-10-14) + SPY closes
trial.pass: 95% CI of the top-minus-bottom quartile difference > 0
trial.controls: The same test on GLD and IBIT, where the skew sign differs

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture, ~24 monthly expiry cohorts (~730 days); daily overlapping entries help but remain cohort-correlated
strategies.harness_suggestion: Store 5%/10% OTM call mids and IVs at 30 DTE per capture day for SPY/GLD/IBIT.

strategies.name: Covered strangle / covered combination (Cboe CMBO)

legs.strike_rule: ATM (CMBO) or OTM x% / delta -0.30; cash = K_p in 1-month T-bills

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: min(S_T, K_c) - S0 - max(K_p - S_T, 0) + C + P
strategies.max_profit: K_c - S0 + C + P
strategies.max_loss: S0 + K_p - C - P (stock to zero and put assigned)
strategies.breakevens: If S0 - C - P >= K_p: S_T = S0 - C - P. Otherwise (e.g. ATM put): S_T = (S0 + K_p - C - P)/2

greeks_at_inception.delta: positive, ~1.0-1.2 (1 from stock + ~0.5 short ATM put - ~0.35 short 2% OTM call; ~1.0 for symmetric 30-delta)
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive, roughly double a covered call

strategies.when_to_use: Range-bound view with willingness to double the position lower; collects two premiums. CMBO is the index benchmark: 2% OTM call over SPX plus an ATM put over T-bills.
strategies.risks: Leveraged downside (two units of exposure below K_p); needs cash for assignment; losses accelerate exactly when IV rises; early assignment on both legs.
strategies.margin_note: The covered-call portion needs no margin. The short put is cash-secured (strike) or uses the 20%/15% rule; OIC and CMBO hold T-bills equal to the put strike.
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit both legs are inverse; a short BTC put collateralised in BTC has wrong-way risk, so margin rises sharply as spot falls.
strategies.metals_notes: GC covered strangle = long GC future + short OG call + short OG put; SPAN recognises offsets. GLD/SLV follow equity rules.
variants: 2:1 (two puts per call) when scaling in
strategies.claim: Over 1988-06 to 2026-10, the Cboe CMBO covered combo index has a higher monthly Sharpe ratio (excess over 3m T-bill) than the BXY 2% OTM buy-write, i.e. adding the ATM short put on T-bill collateral improves risk-adjusted return.

trial.procedure: Cboe CDN CMBO_History.csv (1986-06) and BXY_History.csv (1988-06); align; excess over DTB3; studentized block bootstrap; walk-forward halves; report worst-5% months as a secondary description
trial.data: Cboe CDN histories, FRED DTB3
trial.pass: Bootstrap 95% CI of the Sharpe difference > 0, with the same sign in both halves
trial.controls: Beta-matched SPY-TR blend (CMBO beta ~0.66); PUTY 2% OTM put-write as the put-only arm

strategies.name: Deribit covered call on BTC/ETH inventory (inverse options)

legs.strike_rule: 1 BTC held in the Deribit account (collateral) or spot elsewhere
OTM: delta 0.20-0.30 or +10-20% (BTC-DDMMMYY-K-C; strikes in USD, premium quoted in BTC, contract_size 1 BTC, min 0.1, tick 0.0001 BTC)
legs.expiry_rule: monthly or weekly/daily; European, cash-settled at 08:00 UTC to the 07:30-08:00 UTC index average (delivery price)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: In BTC: 1 + c - max(S_T - K, 0)/S_T, where c = premium in BTC. In USD: S_T*(1 + c) - max(S_T - K, 0) - S0 = min(S_T, K) + c*S_T - S0
strategies.max_profit: In USD, unbounded: K - S0 + c*S_T for S_T >= K (slope c above K). In BTC terms, the premium c is retained when S_T <= K
strategies.max_loss: In USD, S0 (S_T -> 0; the BTC premium is then also worth 0), a larger loss than a USD covered call's S0 - C
strategies.breakevens: USD: S_T = S0/(1 + c), for S_T <= K
strategies.when_to_use: A long-term BTC/ETH holder measuring returns in coin wants coin-denominated yield. mark_iv is published per strike for delta targeting, and rolls can happen any time (24/7).
strategies.risks: Inverse settlement: the short call costs (S_T - K)/S_T BTC (capped at 1 BTC per contract), and the collateral falls in USD with spot. Coin premium shrinks in a crash. Exchange and custody risk (offshore venue; US persons restricted, a venue matter). Per-contract fees (the Deribit schedule, capped as a fraction of option price, was not verified this pass: KB is JS-rendered). Liquidity thins beyond ~3 months.
strategies.margin_note: Margin is in BTC; holding the BTC in the account offsets the short call under portfolio margin. Standard-margin short options need an initial margin of roughly 0.10-0.15 BTC plus the mark per contract. No Reg T.

strategies.name: Dividend-aware covered call (ex-dividend management, qualified covered call)

legs.strike_rule: strike >= lowest qualified benchmark (not deep-in-the-money) so the call is a QCC; prefer OTM, because an ITM QCC suspends the stock holding period; keep remaining time value > the upcoming dividend going into the ex-date
legs.expiry_rule: granted more than 30 days before expiry and not more than 12 months before expiry (or meets the published term/benchmark rules); expiry after the ex-dividend date

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: min(S_T, K) - S0 + C + D, where D = dividend kept if not assigned before the ex-date
strategies.max_profit: K - S0 + C + D
strategies.max_loss: S0 - C - D
strategies.breakevens: S_T = S0 - C - D
strategies.when_to_use: A holder of dividend stock wants premium plus dividend. They must avoid early assignment the day before the ex-date when the call is ITM and the dividend exceeds the remaining time value, and keep the call qualified so straddle loss-deferral rules do not apply.
strategies.risks: Early assignment strips the dividend. Writing an in-the-money QCC suspends the stock holding period while the call is open (Pub 550). Non-qualified (deep ITM, or 30 days or less) calls trigger straddle loss-deferral and can disrupt the qualified-dividend holding period. Special dividends adjust strikes.
strategies.margin_note: Covered-call rules; in a cash account the stock must be fully paid.
strategies.crypto_notes: Not applicable: BTC/ETH pay no dividends. The closest analogue is the futures basis or funding carried by the long inventory.
strategies.metals_notes: Not applicable: GLD/SLV/GC pay nothing. The analogue is the gold lease rate embedded in the futures curve.

strategies.name: Iron butterfly benchmark overlay (Cboe BFLY: short ATM straddle, long 5% wings, over T-bills)

legs.expiry_rule: 1 month, AM-settled SPX, rolled on the 3rd Friday

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: cr - max(S_T - K_atm, 0) - max(K_atm - S_T, 0) + max(S_T - K_c5, 0) + max(K_p5 - S_T, 0) (cr = net credit), plus T-bill interest on collateral equal to 10x the worst possible option payoff
strategies.max_profit: cr (at S_T = K_atm)
strategies.max_loss: max(K_c5 - K_atm, K_atm - K_p5) - cr per unit. BFLY holds T-bills = 10x the worst possible payoff, so the index loses at most ~10% per month
strategies.breakevens: S_T = K_atm +/- cr
strategies.when_to_use: A pure variance-premium harvest with a capped tail; the 'holding' is a T-bill account. Cboe's benchmark since 1986 for comparing non-equity-linked index-option income.
strategies.risks: Moves beyond the wings; ATM pin and gamma into expiry; low capital efficiency as benchmarked (10x collateral); historically weak returns relative to equity-linked overlays.
strategies.margin_note: Defined-risk four-leg spread: margin = wider wing width minus credit. SPX options are cash-settled, European and Section 1256.
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit all four legs are inverse; in BTC terms the downside wing pays more BTC per USD as BTC falls, so the BTC-denominated P&L is skewed relative to the USD one.
strategies.metals_notes: GC iron flies via OG options; 5% wings are often inside gold's monthly move range in high-vol regimes.

strategies.name: Multi-week / laddered covered call (Cboe BXMW)

legs.expiry_rule: ~4 weeks at write; ~3 weeks remaining at inception of the ladder (tranche 2)
~1 week remaining (tranche 4). Each week the expiring tranche is re-written ATM ~4 weeks out (BXMW = four independent buy-write sub-indices on SPX/SPXW)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Tranches expire on different dates, so there is no single expiry. Each tranche i, at its own expiry T_i, contributes 0.25*(min(S_Ti, K_i) - S0 + C_i); the caps are staggered across four strikes
strategies.max_profit: sum_i 0.25*(K_i - S0 + C_i), reached only if S >= K_i at each tranche's own expiry
strategies.breakevens: For a terminal S below every K_i: S = S0 - sum_i 0.25*C_i

greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative, concentrated in the nearest tranche
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive; higher theta per unit vega than a single monthly call because average remaining tenor is ~2.5 weeks
greeks_at_inception.vega: negative, less vega per premium than a monthly

strategies.risks: 4x the rolls, so 4x transaction costs and bid-ask; gamma around events in the near tranche; short-dated IV is more often below realised around earnings and macro days; operational load.
strategies.margin_note: Covered: no option margin. Each tranche needs 25 shares-equivalent of cover, so use 100-share lots per tranche (400 shares) or XSP/mini contracts.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit lists daily, weekly and monthly expiries (verified), so the ladder can be daily or weekly. strategies.max_profit: K - S0 + C
strategies.max_loss: S0 - C
strategies.breakevens: S_T = S0 - C

strategies.name: Partial overwrite / overwriting-ETF mechanics (BXMH, BXMC, QYLD, XYLD, JEPI)

legs.strike_rule: index basket (QYLD/XYLD: full index; JEPI: low-vol active basket ~80-85% of NAV)
ATM (BXMH writes 0.5 unit; BXMC writes 1 unit if VIX >= 20 on roll day, else 0.5). JEPI: ~15-20% of NAV in ELNs embedding OTM S&P 500 calls. QYLD/XYLD: ~100% notional ATM calls; set qty = w
legs.expiry_rule: 1 month, rolled on the 3rd Friday (JEPI: ELNs issued on a weekly ladder)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: S_T - S0 + w*(C - max(S_T - K, 0)), where w = overwrite fraction
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded for w < 1 (slope 1-w above K); equals K - S0 + C for w = 1
strategies.max_loss: S0 - w*C
strategies.breakevens: S_T = S0 - w*C
strategies.when_to_use: The investor wants a target distribution yield while keeping some upside. The fraction w trades income against the cap.

QYLD tracks the Cboe Nasdaq-100 BuyWrite V2 (BXNT) since Oct 2015; XYLD tracks BXM since Aug 2020.

strategies.crypto_notes: Bitcoin covered-call funds replicate this with IBIT or CME BTC options. On Deribit, w < 1 simply means selling fewer contracts than coins held.
strategies.metals_notes: Replicate on gold with w*GLD calls per 100 GLD shares.

strategies.name: Protective put / married put (Cboe PPUT 5% OTM)

legs.strike_rule: OTM 5% (PPUT) or ATM / delta -0.30; tail variant 10% OTM quarterly (PPUT3M)
legs.expiry_rule: 1 month rolled on the 3rd Friday (PPUT); 3 months (PPUT3M); LEAPS 12 months

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(S_T, K) - S0 - P
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded (S_T - S0 - P)
strategies.max_loss: S0 - K + P
strategies.breakevens: S_T = S0 + P
strategies.when_to_use: A bullish holder fears a sharp temporary decline and needs a defined floor (margin, mandate or taxes prevent selling). Economically it is a bet that realised vol will exceed implied over the hedge horizon (AQR 'Still Not Cheap': buying an option is a bet that realised volatility will rise above the option's implied volatility).
strategies.risks: Persistent negative carry from the variance and skew premium; roll timing; the floor resets each month, so a slow grind lower is not protected; a deep-ITM put on appreciated stock can be a constructive sale.
strategies.margin_note: Cboe manual 'Long Put and Long Underlying': pay for the put in full; stock maintenance is the lower of 10% of the put strike plus the OTM amount, or 25% of stock value (American-style put).
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit the inverse put pays (K - S_T)/S_T BTC, which is exactly K - S_T USD at expiry, but the premium is paid in BTC and margin is in BTC. USDC linear puts give a clean USD hedge. DVOL vs realised shows BTC puts also carry a variance premium on average.
strategies.metals_notes: GC puts settle into short futures; GLD puts are equity-style. Gold put IV is often at or below call IV, so downside protection on gold is comparatively cheap.

strategies.name: Put-spread collar / seagull (Cboe CLLZ zero-cost put-spread collar)

legs.strike_rule: K1 < K2: OTM 5% (CLLZ); generic seagull 10-20% OTM
K3 > S0: CLLZ picks the call whose bid equals ask(2.5% put) - bid(5% put), i.e. net premium 0

strategies.max_profit: K3 - S0
strategies.max_loss: S0 - (K2 - K1) (S_T -> 0; protection only in the band K1..K2, where the payoff is flat at K2 - S0)

greeks_at_inception.delta: positive, higher than a plain collar

strategies.when_to_use: The holder wants protection against a small (2.5-5% for CLLZ) monthly decline and more upside than a plain collar, and accepts full re-exposure below K1.

strategies.margin_note: Long stock + short call is covered. The put vertical's margin is the width (K2 - K1) because it is a debit spread paid in full. Collar maintenance treatment does not apply to the vertical.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC's crash frequency makes the uncovered tail below K1 more costly in realised terms; Deribit portfolio margin recognises the vertical.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold's lower crash frequency makes put-spread collars relatively cheaper to run on GLD/GC.

trial.controls: CLL and PPUT as full-floor comparators; price-only SPX as a sensitivity
