strategies.name: The wheel (cash-secured put -> assignment -> covered call -> called away)

legs.strike_rule: phase 1: OTM put, delta -0.20 to -0.30, cash-secured; repeat until assigned
legs.expiry_rule: 30-45 DTE, close at 50% profit or roll at 21 DTE

legs.strike_rule: phase 2: assigned at K_put, cost basis K_put - cumulative premiums
phase 2: OTM call, delta 0.20-0.30, optionally constrained to strike >= cost basis
legs.expiry_rule: 30-45 DTE, repeat until called away; then restart phase 1

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Cycle P&L = sum of put premiums + sum of call premiums + (K_call - K_put) on completion. While holding stock: min(S_T, K_call) - K_put + cumulative premiums
strategies.max_profit: Per cycle: K_call - K_put + sum of premiums
strategies.max_loss: K_put - sum of premiums (stock to zero while held)
strategies.breakevens: S_T = K_put - cumulative premiums (declines with each cycle)

greeks_at_inception.delta: positive: 0.2-0.3 in the put phase, 0.7-0.8 in the call phase

strategies.when_to_use: A range-bound or slowly rising underlying the trader is happy to own; a disciplined way to sell both sides of the variance premium sequentially rather than simultaneously (compare the covered strangle).
strategies.risks: By parity the covered-call phase is a short put, so the trader is always short a put and takes a crash in full. The never-below-basis rule can trap the trader overwriting far OTM (little premium) after a drop. Path dependence and tax (short-term gains, QCC rules); fees from frequent rolls.
strategies.margin_note: Phase 1: cash-secured put rules; phase 2: covered-call rules. A margin-secured variant uses the 20%/15% rule.
assets: index (XSP is cash-settled: no share assignment, so the wheel is synthetic)
crypto (Deribit: cash-settled, no assignment; emulate by buying BTC when the put expires ITM)
futures-options (GC/SI: assignment gives a futures position)
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit options are cash-settled (no delivery), so the 'assignment' step is manual. 24/7 markets mean no closing auction. Funding or basis on perpetuals can replace the T-bill yield of the cash leg.
strategies.metals_notes: Assigned SO/OG puts produce long futures (margin, roll yield), not metal; GLD/SLV assignment is ordinary shares.
variants: ATM both phases (alternating PUT and BXM)
strategies.claim: In a model-priced simulation (Black-Scholes with VIX as the implied vol, not market prices) on SPX from 1990 to 2026, a wheel whose call strike is constrained to be >= the cost basis has a lower Sharpe ratio than the same wheel writing an unconstrained 30-delta call.

trial.statistic: Sharpe(basis-constrained wheel) - Sharpe(unconstrained 30-delta wheel), model-priced
trial.null: Difference >= 0 (the basis rule helps or is neutral)
trial.procedure: Model-priced backtest on SPX daily since 1990 (IV = VIX, with an OTM adjustment from SKEW as a sensitivity), 30-45 DTE cycles, 10 bps slippage. Gate: the same pricer must first reproduce BXM (2002-) and PUT (2007-) monthly returns with tracking error < 2%/yr, or results do not count. Block bootstrap of the paired Sharpe difference.
trial.data: SPX daily 1975-, VIX 1990-, SKEW 1990-, BXM/PUT histories for calibration, FRED DTB3
trial.pass: Calibration gate passed AND the 95% CI of the Sharpe difference < 0
trial.controls: Constant-IV pricer to show sensitivity; ATM-both-phases wheel vs the actual PUT index as an external check

strategies.harness_suggestion: Reuse the model-priced overlay harness; run the BXM/PUT calibration gate first and report the calibration error alongside the verdict, with the result labelled model-priced.

strategies.name: VIX-call tail-hedge overlay on an equity holding (Cboe VXTH)

legs.strike_rule: VIX call with Black delta closest to 0.30 (inputs as of 9:30 ET on the VIX roll date). Notional weight PctCall set by the forward 1-month VIX future level F per the Cboe schedule (0% when F is low, up to ~1% of portfolio in mid regimes; table verified only as present in the methodology). qty here is the portfolio weight, not a contract count
legs.expiry_rule: 1 month, rolled at VIX option expiration

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: S_T - S0 + N*(max(VIX_settle - K, 0) - C_ask), where N = (S&P500 + Div)*PctCall / (100*C_ask*(1 - PctCall)) contracts per index unit
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded (equity upside plus convex VIX-call payoff in a crash)
strategies.max_loss: S0 + N*C_ask (equity to zero; the VIX calls would pay off in that scenario, so the realistic floor is better)
strategies.breakevens: S_T = S0 + N*C_ask - N*max(VIX_settle - K, 0), i.e. the hedge costs N*C_ask per month when VIX settles below K

greeks_at_inception.delta: positive (equity) reduced slightly by the VIX calls' negative equity beta
greeks_at_inception.gamma: positive in a crash through VIX convexity (VIX call gamma)

strategies.when_to_use: An equity holder wants crash convexity cheaper than SPX puts. VIX calls price off VIX futures (contango), not spot VIX, and pay most in sudden vol spikes. Hedge size scales with the vol regime.
strategies.risks: Persistent bleed in calm years; VIX options settle to a special opening quotation of the VIX futures expiry, not spot VIX, so the hedge can miss a spike that mean-reverts before settlement; basis between VIX futures and spot; weighting-rule model risk.
strategies.margin_note: Long VIX calls are paid in full (cash-settled, European); the equity leg follows normal Reg T.
strategies.crypto_notes: No listed VIX-style crypto vol-index options with depth; the analogue is long OTM BTC calls/puts on Deribit or long DVOL futures where listed.
strategies.metals_notes: No liquid GVZ options; a gold holder would use OTM GLD puts instead.
variants: VIX call spread to cut bleed
SPX put tail hedge (PPUT3M) as the comparator
strategies.claim: Over 2006-03 to 2026-10, the Cboe VXTH index has a smaller maximum drawdown than the PPUT3M 10%-OTM quarterly put index's companion period, measured on the common 2006-03 onward sample against SPX total return: maxDD(VXTH) is at least 10 points shallower than maxDD(SPY TR).

trial.statistic: maxDD(SPY TR) - maxDD(VXTH) on the common sample, daily
trial.procedure: Cboe CDN VXTH_History.csv (2006-03-31 onward); SPY TR from the Yahoo chart adjclose; compute daily maximum drawdowns; bootstrap the drawdown difference with stationary block resampling of daily returns (block 63 days)
trial.data: VXTH 5,163 rows; SPY closes plus dividends
trial.pass: Bootstrap 90% CI of the drawdown difference > 10 points
trial.controls: PPUT3M (2004-) and PPUT over the same window as put-based tail hedges; CAGR cost reported alongside

strategies.harness_suggestion: Add VXTH and PPUT3M to the benchmark list. Recomputed today: VXTH 2006- CAGR 9.93% / vol 17.2% / maxDD -43.3% / worst month -10.7%. The hedge's 2008 drawdown is large, so the claim may fail; that is the point of testing it.

strategies.name: Zero-cost collar

legs.strike_rule: chosen floor, e.g. OTM 5-10% or delta -0.25
solve K_c so that C(K_c) = P(K_p) (net premium 0); with equity put skew K_c sits closer to spot than K_p does

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(K_p, min(S_T, K_c)) - S0
strategies.max_profit: K_c - S0
strategies.max_loss: S0 - K_p
strategies.breakevens: S_T = S0

greeks_at_inception.gamma: mixed: positive near K_p, negative near K_c; slightly negative net on equities (the call is nearer spot)
greeks_at_inception.theta: small, NOT zero by construction (zero premium does not mean zero theta); on equities usually slightly positive because the nearer short call decays faster
greeks_at_inception.vega: small; slightly negative on equities (the nearer call has more vega); long skew (long put wing, short call wing)

strategies.when_to_use: Hedge a holding with no cash outlay. The price paid is asymmetry: with equity skew the cap is nearer than the floor. Common for concentrated positions and crypto treasuries.
strategies.risks: Asymmetric band (the skew cost is hidden); capped upside; pin risk at either strike; dividend assignment; constructive-sale risk if the band is too tight (US tax).
strategies.margin_note: Cboe manual collar treatment (same expiry, put strike < call strike): no margin on the call, reduced stock maintenance.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC skew changes sign with regime (calls richer in bull runs), so the zero-cost band on Deribit is often wider on the upside than on equities. Holding BTC in the account collateralises the short call; the long put lowers portfolio-margin risk.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold often has call-side skew, so zero-cost collars on GLD/GC can have K_c farther from spot than K_p (the opposite of equities).
variants: zero-cost with put spread (put-spread collar entry)
strategies.claim: For 30-DTE SPX options, the call strike whose mid price equals the mid price of the 5%-OTM put lies closer to spot than the put does: the time-averaged ratio (K_c - S)/(S - K_p) is below 1.

trial.statistic: Mean over capture days of (K_c - S)/(S - K_p), with K_c interpolated between listed strikes at equal mid to the 95% put, nearest-30-DTE expiry
trial.procedure: From the daily CBOE SPX chain capture, select the ~30-DTE expiry, interpolate the 95% put mid, solve the equal-mid call strike, and record the ratio. HAC (Newey-West, lag 21) CI on the mean. A model-priced version from VIX-as-IV with a parametric skew is NOT acceptable evidence.
trial.data: Daily chain capture SPX/SPY from 2026-10-14; Cboe SKEW history for later conditioning
trial.pass: Upper 95% HAC CI of the mean ratio < 1, with the same sign in both halves
trial.controls: The same statistic on GLD (expect ratio > 1) and IBIT (regime-dependent)

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture, ~120 trading days
strategies.harness_suggestion: Have surface_summary store, per capture, the equal-premium call strike for 5%/10% OTM puts at 30/60/90 DTE for SPX, GLD and IBIT.

strategies.name: 1-day (0DTE) variance premium: short SPX daily straddle vs VIX1D

legs.expiry_rule: next session's daily expiry (0-1 DTE), entered at the prior close or the open

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: C0 - |S_T - K|; the straddle is about 0.8*sigma_1d*S with sigma_1d ~ VIX1D/100/sqrt(252).
strategies.max_profit: C0 (close at K).
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded above; K - C0 below.
strategies.breakevens: K - C0 and K + C0.

greeks_at_inception.vega: negative but small in absolute terms (vega scales with sqrt(T))

strategies.when_to_use: Harvest the one-day variance premium on days without scheduled macro releases; the iron-butterfly version caps the tail.
strategies.risks: Intraday jumps on news; gamma at the close; the 0DTE premium may be compressed by heavy retail selling; a single bad day can erase months of premium.
strategies.margin_note: Naked SPX straddle (PM +6%/-8%); most brokers require the defined-risk version for 0DTE. SPX is cash-settled, European and Section 1256; SPY daily expiries are American and physically settled.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit daily expiries (08:00 UTC) give the crypto analogue; there is no 1-day vol index, so use the daily expiry's ATM mark_iv; inverse settlement, 24/7.
strategies.metals_notes: GC short-dated weekly options (American on futures, SPAN) are the nearest analogue; there is no 1-day gold vol index.
strategies.claim: The VIX1D close implies a next-day S&P 500 variance, (VIX1D/100)^2/365 (the conservative calendar-day convention), that exceeds the next trading day's squared ^GSPC close-to-close log return on average.

trial.statistic: Mean of (VIX1D_t/100)^2/365 - r_{t+1}^2; repeat with /252 as the liberal convention.
trial.procedure: Daily VIX1D (history from 2022-05-13) and ^GSPC closes; daily non-overlapping one-day windows (~1,100); studentized block bootstrap (5-day blocks); walk-forward halves; report event days separately.
trial.data: CBOE VIX1D (archive), ^GSPC/SPY closes. Index-implied variance, no option prices; the straddle P&L itself is model-priced.
trial.pass: Mean > 0 with the 95% CI excluding zero under the /365 convention, positive in both halves.
trial.controls: Same test with VIX/sqrt(21)-scaled daily variance (shows whether the 1-day premium differs from the 30-day one); event-day exclusion.

strategies.harness_suggestion: New harness_vix1d in the harness_vrp_spx style, using archive cboe-VIX1D-history and daily-history--GSPC.

strategies.name: BTC/ETH volatility premium (DVOL vs realised) via Deribit inverse straddles

legs.strike_rule: ATM (strike nearest the BTC forward of that expiry)
BTC-PERPETUAL hedge of the premium-adjusted delta, rebalanced daily or each 8h funding interval

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Inverse: the call pays max(S_T - K, 0)/S_T BTC and the put max(K - S_T, 0)/S_T BTC. Short straddle in BTC: C0_btc - |S_T - K|/S_T; in USD about C0_usd - |S_T - K|, with a convexity correction from the BTC denomination. Delta-hedged: about Vega*(DVOL - RV_365) per cycle, plus or minus funding on the perp.
strategies.max_profit: The straddle premium (in BTC, converted at S_T).
strategies.max_loss: Upside unbounded in USD. On the downside the inverse put's BTC payoff (K - S_T)/S_T grows hyperbolically as S_T goes to 0 (the BTC-denominated loss is convex), though the USD loss is bounded by K.
strategies.breakevens: About K - C0_usd and K + C0_usd in USD; hedged: RV = DVOL.

greeks_at_inception.delta: 0 after the premium-adjusted perp hedge (the BTC premium received is itself long BTC delta)
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive (accrues on a 365-day calendar, including weekends)

strategies.when_to_use: When DVOL exceeds 30-day realised BTC vol by a wide margin, with no scheduled catalyst (FOMC, large quarterly expiries); funding affects the hedge's carry.
strategies.risks: BTC moves 10-20% in a day with no circuit breakers; 24/7 trading replaces gaps with continuous but violent moves; exchange and counterparty risk (offshore venue, which does not onboard US persons); portfolio-margin liquidations; funding can flip sign.
strategies.margin_note: Deribit portfolio margin (SPAN-like, in BTC); options are European and cash-settled in BTC at 08:00 UTC; option fees capped at 12.5% of the option price. US-regulated routes: IBIT options (American, physically delivered IBIT shares, equity margin, not Section 1256), CME BTC options on futures (Section 1256), Coinbase Derivatives.
strategies.crypto_notes: DVOL is Deribit's 30-day implied vol index (a VIX-like strip on BTC options). The archive holds daily DVOL from 2021-03-24 (~2,030 days, ~67 non-overlapping 30-day cycles) via public/get_volatility_index_data. Realised vol uses 365 days; no dividends; the hedge is a perpetual with 8-hourly funding, booked as carry; weekend realised vol is real P&L. ETH twin via ETH DVOL. IBIT options are the US-regulated, USD-settled, American route: equity hours only, so BTC's weekend moves arrive as gaps.
strategies.metals_notes: n/a
variants: DVOL-gated (trade only when DVOL - RV > 10 points)
Weekly BTC straddles (Friday expiries) harvesting weekend theta
strategies.claim: Over the Deribit DVOL history (2021-03 to 2026-10), (DVOL/100)^2 exceeds the subsequently realised 30-calendar-day BTC variance (365-day annualisation) on average.

trial.statistic: Mean of (DVOL_t/100)^2 - RV_BTC(t..t+30 calendar days); secondary: win rate, share of cumulative premium lost in the worst decile of months, and a model-priced hedged straddle with funding at 0 and +/-10% p.a.
trial.procedure: Non-overlapping 30-calendar-day cycles over the archived DVOL history (~67); studentized block bootstrap; walk-forward halves; cross-check the implied level against today's deribit_book ATM mark_iv.
trial.data: Deribit DVOL history (archive, deribit_dvol_history), BTC/ETH daily closes (archive), deribit_book snapshot.
trial.pass: Mean > 0 with the 95% CI excluding zero, positive in both halves.
trial.controls: Buy-and-hold BTC; shuffled-DVOL placebo; the SPX VRP over the same dates for scale.

strategies.harness_suggestion: harness_vrp_btc (T-49) and harness_vrp_eth (T-67) exist; add the worst-decile share, a funding sensitivity parameter and an inverse-payoff conversion in the payoff engine (payoff_btc = payoff_usd / S_T).

strategies.name: Calendar vol spread (ATM time spread, long or reverse)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At the near expiry: V = C_far(S_T, T_far - T_near, sigma_far') - (S_T - K)^+ - D0, with D0 = C_far - C_near the debit. Tent-shaped, peaking near S_T = K; in both tails V tends to -D0 (the far option keeps only time value). The reverse calendar (long near, short far, credit C0) is the mirror.
strategies.max_profit: Long calendar: about C_far(K, T_far - T_near, sigma_far') - D0 at S_T = K, depending on far IV at the near expiry. Reverse: C0 when S_T is far from K and far IV collapses.
strategies.max_loss: Long calendar: D0 (European, no dividends). Reverse: C_far(K, T_far - T_near, sigma_far') - C0 at S_T = K. Bounded by S_T - C0 because a call is worth at most S, but large if far IV rises.
strategies.breakevens: Two points where C_far(S_T, T_far - T_near, sigma_far') = (S_T - K)^+ + D0, solved numerically on the near-expiry grid with the far leg marked at its IV (engine breakevens()).

greeks_at_inception.delta: about 0, slightly positive (the far ATM call's d1 grows with sqrt(T), so its delta is larger)
greeks_at_inception.gamma: long calendar: negative (short near gamma dominates); reverse: positive
greeks_at_inception.vega: long calendar: positive net vega, concentrated in the far expiry (long term-structure slope); reverse: negative

strategies.when_to_use: Long calendar when the term structure is flat or inverted (VIX >= VIX3M) and near realised vol is expected below near implied. Reverse calendar when the curve is steep and a front-end vol event (earnings, FOMC, CPI) is expected, or to sell the forward term premium.
strategies.risks: Long calendar: a large move takes spot away from K and both legs lose; far IV can fall when markets calm; an American short near leg can be assigned early. Reverse calendar: the far leg's vega blows up in a crash.
strategies.margin_note: Long calendar: debit only (same strike, long leg later-dated, so covered). Reverse calendar: the short far leg is naked under Reg-T; PM stresses it with price moves (+6%/-8% for SPX/SPY) and implied-vol shifts.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit lists daily, weekly, monthly and quarterly expiries, so calendars can be very short-dated. All legs are European, settle in BTC at 08:00 UTC and cannot be assigned early. BTC term structure is in steep contango in calm markets and inverts violently in crashes; funding matters only if the position is delta-hedged with the perp.
strategies.metals_notes: GC calendars pair options on different futures (serial vs quarterly), so a futures-spread basis sits inside the calendar; American exercise means an ITM short near leg can be assigned into futures. GLD/SLV calendars are plain equity calendars; Section 1256 applies on GC.
variants: Double calendar (put calendar below, call calendar above)
strategies.claim: Conditional on VIX3M/VIX > 1.10 at entry, the 1-to-3-month SPX forward variance F^2 = (93*VIX3M^2 - 30*VIX^2)/63 exceeds the SPY variance realised over trading days 22-63 after entry on average, so the far leg of a reverse calendar is sold above its subsequent realised variance.

trial.statistic: Mean of F^2 - RV(22..63), both annualised, over entries with VIX3M/VIX > 1.10.
trial.procedure: Daily VIX and VIX3M from 2009-09-18 (the free VIX3M file starts there, not 2007) and SPY closes. Non-overlapping 63d cycles (~68 in total, fewer conditional), plus all daily starts with a 63-day-block studentized bootstrap. Walk-forward over declared thresholds 1.05/1.10/1.15, deflated.
trial.data: CBOE VIX and VIX3M (archive), SPY closes. Index-implied variance, not option prices; the calendar's own P&L needs chain history.
trial.pass: Conditional mean > 0 with the 95% CI excluding zero, positive in both halves of 2009-2026.
trial.controls: Unconditional forward premium (harness_forward_variance); shuffled-ratio placebo; sensitivity run excluding 2020.

strategies.harness_suggestion: harness_forward_variance (T-148, uses 93/30/63) and harness_term_vs_spot (T-231, uses the cruder (3*VIX3M^2 - VIX^2)/2) already compute this gap; add the VIX3M/VIX gate and unify both on the 93/30/63 formula. The calendar P&L comes from build_position with two expiries once captures exist.

strategies.name: Conditional VRP: trade only when the implied-minus-realised spread is wide

legs.strike_rule: ATM; notional scaled by the entry spread z = (IV - RV_hat)/sd (flat or reversed to long when z < -z*)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Per active cycle, the same as the delta-hedged straddle: approx. N_t*Vega/(2*sigma)*(IV^2 - RV^2), about N_t*Vega*(IV - RV), with N_t a function of the entry z-score. When z < -z* the position reverses (long straddle, gamma scalping).
strategies.max_profit: Short cycles: about the straddle credit times N_t. Long cycles: unbounded.
strategies.max_loss: Short cycles: unbounded (jumps). Long cycles: the premium paid.
strategies.breakevens: RV over the cycle = IV at entry.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative when short, positive when reversed
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive when short, negative when reversed
greeks_at_inception.vega: negative when short, positive when reversed

strategies.when_to_use: Treat the IV-RV spread as the single statistic: sell vol only when the premium is wide relative to a realised-vol forecast (HAR/EWMA), and stand aside or go long when implied sits below forecast realised (pre-crisis cheap-vol regimes).
strategies.risks: The forecast is backward-looking; the widest spreads come right after spikes when vol-of-vol is highest; overfitting the threshold; long-vol cycles bleed theta.
strategies.margin_note: Same as the short straddle when active (naked straddle margin; PM +6%/-8% for SPX/SPY); long cycles are debit only.
strategies.crypto_notes: Use DVOL minus 30-day realised (365-day annualisation) as the statistic, with Deribit inverse straddles and a perp hedge with funding. The DVOL-RV spread is much noisier than VIX-RV, and its sign flips in bull runs when realised outruns implied.
strategies.metals_notes: GVZ minus GLD realised for gold and OVX minus USO realised for oil; the GC/SI route is futures options (American, SPAN, Section 1256).
variants: Threshold on the raw spread (vol points) vs z-score
Continuous sizing proportional to the spread
Spread on the VIX3M-implied forward vs a realised forecast
strategies.claim: Scaling a short 21-day S&P 500 variance position struck at VIX^2 by max(z, 0), where z is the entry z-score of VIX minus a walk-forward HAR realised-vol forecast, gives a higher Sharpe ratio than the constant-notional short over the same months.

trial.statistic: Sharpe(scaled) - Sharpe(constant) of the monthly P&L N_t*((VIX_t/100)^2 - RV_{t,t+21}).
trial.null: Sharpe difference <= 0 (the spread carries no timing information).
trial.procedure: HAR(1,5,22) fitted walk-forward (expanding window, refit monthly); monthly cycles since 1991 using ^GSPC closes; studentized bootstrap of the Sharpe difference; PBO across the declared scaling rules (on/off at z > 0.5, z > 1, linear max(z,0)).
trial.data: CBOE VIX and ^GSPC/SPY closes. Model-free variance P&L: the straddle implementation is model-priced and reported separately. Twins: DVOL + BTC, GVZ + GLD (archive).
trial.pass: Sharpe difference > 0 at p < 0.05 and PBO < 0.3.
trial.controls: VIX-level-only scaling (shows the realised forecast adds information beyond the VIX level); random-z placebo; top-tercile share of P&L reported descriptively.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Add a gate/scale argument to harness_vrp_spx and harness_vrp_btc that takes a HAR z-score, and report the Sharpe difference with PBO across the declared rules.

strategies.name: Correlation trade via index vs sector straddles (SPY vs sector ETFs, QQQ vs XLK)

legs.strike_rule: ATM on each sector ETF (XLK, XLF, XLE, XLV, XLY, XLP, XLI, XLU, XLB ...), qty_i = w_i * Vega_SPY/Vega_i
ATM on each sector ETF, same weights
daily delta hedge on every straddle

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Vega-weighted: P&L ~ sum_i w_i*Vega_SPY*(RV_i - IV_i) - Vega_SPY*(RV_SPY - IV_SPY): short implied cross-sector correlation. Fewer legs than single-stock dispersion and no earnings jumps, at the cost of a smaller correlation premium.
strategies.max_profit: About the SPY straddle credit when sectors move against each other and the index stays flat.
strategies.max_loss: Large when all sectors move together (correlation goes to 1 in risk-off).
strategies.breakevens: Realised cross-sector correlation = implied, rho = (sigma_SPY^2 - sum w_i^2 sigma_i^2)/(sum_{i!=j} w_i w_j sigma_i sigma_j).

greeks_at_inception.gamma: short SPY gamma, long sector gamma; summed in dollars, net short (sectors have higher sigma and so less dollar gamma per vega)

strategies.when_to_use: In sector-rotation regimes when sector vols are high relative to index vol; implementable with about ten liquid ETF chains.
strategies.risks: Risk-off correlation spikes; weight drift; ETF option spreads wider than SPY's; hedging costs across ~20 legs.
strategies.margin_note: The SPY short straddle is naked (PM +6%/-8%); sector ETFs are narrow-based (PM +/-15%) and get only partial offset. American, physically settled ETF options.
strategies.crypto_notes: Crypto twin: there is no liquid crypto-index option in the US; the practical version is ETH vs BTC only (see cross_index_vol_spread).
strategies.metals_notes: GDX (miners) vs GLD and SLV straddles: miners' vol embeds gold vol plus equity beta.
variants: Long correlation (reverse) ahead of macro shocks
strategies.claim: Implied cross-sector correlation computed from SPY and the nine original SPDR sector ETFs' 30-day ATM IVs exceeds the subsequently realised 21-day correlation of the same ETFs (same formula on realised vols, SPY sector weights) by more than 0.05 on average.

trial.statistic: Mean of rho_implied(t) - rho_realised(t..t+21).
trial.procedure: Daily chain captures of SPY and the 9 sectors give implied correlation per day; realised correlation from the archived sector closes; non-overlapping 21d cycles; studentized block bootstrap; walk-forward after 2 years.
trial.data: Daily CBOE chain capture of SPY plus XLB/XLE/XLF/XLI/XLK/XLP/XLU/XLV/XLY (sector chains are NOT yet in CHAIN_SYMBOLS); sector closes are archived (XLRE and XLC are missing and have short histories).
trial.pass: Lower 95% bound of the mean > 0.05 over at least 36 cycles; positive in > 65% of non-crisis months (reported).

strategies.name: Cross-asset implied vol ratio trades (GVZ/VIX, DVOL/VIX, OVX/VIX)

legs.strike_rule: ATM on the cheap-vol asset (GLD when GVZ/VIX is at a low percentile)
ATM on the rich-vol asset (SPY), qty = Vega_long/Vega_short
daily delta hedge on both legs

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Hedged: P&L ~ Vega*[(RV_A - IV_A) - (RV_B - IV_B)]: a bet that the realised vol ratio RV_A/RV_B ends above an extreme-low implied ratio IV_A/IV_B (mirror at the high extreme).
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded (long straddle leg) less the short straddle's losses.
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded if the short-vol asset realises far more than the long one (e.g. long GLD vol / short SPY vol into an equity crash).
strategies.breakevens: RV_A - RV_B = IV_A - IV_B.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: long gamma in A, short gamma in B (different underlyings, so not netted)
greeks_at_inception.theta: about 0; sign set by the vols (theta ~ 0.5*Vega*sigma/T per leg)
greeks_at_inception.vega: about 0 net; long the vol ratio A/B

strategies.when_to_use: When a cross-asset implied vol ratio (GVZ/VIX, DVOL/VIX, OVX/VIX) is at a multi-year extreme while the realised-vol ratio has not moved. Also as a hedge: long gold vol vs short equity vol when both are cheap but gold vol is cheaper.
strategies.risks: Ratios shift regime (e.g. the 2024-26 repricing of gold vol); the correlation between the two vol spikes is unstable; two hedging programmes; the short leg can be the one that explodes.
strategies.margin_note: The short straddle leg is naked. PM offsets across asset classes are minimal (GLD and SPY sit in different product groups). The GC/SI route uses SPAN; the Deribit route margins separately at its venue, with no cross-margin against US equity options.
strategies.crypto_notes: DVOL/VIX ratio: long a BTC straddle on Deribit (inverse, BTC-settled) vs short a SPY straddle. The legs settle in different currencies and venues, so convert the BTC leg's vega at spot and rebalance; IBIT options make a single-venue USD version possible. Sample from 2021-03 only.
strategies.metals_notes: GVZ/VIX is the cleanest pair: both are Cboe indices with free history from 2009-09 (common sample). GC vs ES options on CME allow a futures-only version (limited SPAN offset between different products); both Section 1256.
strategies.claim: After GVZ/VIX falls below its trailing 3-year 10th percentile (s = +1) or rises above its 90th (s = -1), s*[ln(RV_GLD/RV_SPY) - ln(GVZ/VIX)] over the next 21 trading days is positive on average: the realised vol ratio ends on the far side of the extreme implied ratio.

trial.statistic: Mean of s*[ln(RV_GLD/RV_SPY)_{t,t+21} - ln(GVZ_t/VIX_t)] over event entries; secondary: model-priced vega-neutral straddle-pair P&L.
trial.procedure: Daily GVZ and VIX from 2009-09-18, GLD and SPY closes; the trailing 3-year window makes 2012-09 the first usable entry; event entries with non-overlapping 21d holds; studentized block bootstrap; walk-forward; deflated over the 10/90 and 20/80 cut pairs. Repeat for DVOL/VIX on its shorter sample.
trial.data: CBOE GVZ, VIX, OVX and VXTLT (archive); Deribit DVOL (archive); GLD, SPY, USO, TLT and BTC closes (archive). Model-free for the statistic.
trial.pass: Mean > 0 with the 95% CI excluding zero and win rate > 0.6 for GVZ/VIX; DVOL/VIX reported with its own n.
trial.controls: Unconditional ratio drift; random-entry placebo; VIX-level stratification.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Combine harness_vrp_gold and harness_vrp_spx inputs into harness_vol_ratio; the DVOL/VIX version joins harness_vrp_btc.

strategies.name: Cross-index vol spread (QQQ vs SPY, IWM vs SPY straddle pairs)

legs.strike_rule: ATM on the index whose implied vol is CHEAP relative (SPY when the VXN-VIX z > +2; QQQ when z < -2)
ATM on the RICH index (QQQ when z > +2), qty = Vega_cheap/Vega_rich (vega-neutral)
ATM on the rich index, same qty
daily delta hedge on both legs

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Delta-hedged, for z > +2 (long SPY vol, short QQQ vol): P&L ~ Vega*[(RV_SPY - IV_SPY) - (RV_QQQ - IV_QQQ)]. It profits when the implied spread VXN - VIX was too wide relative to the realised spread RV_QQQ - RV_SPY. Mirror for z < -2.
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded (long straddle leg) less the short straddle's losses.
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded if the rich (short) index realises far more than the cheap one (e.g. a tech-specific shock when short QQQ vol).
strategies.breakevens: RV_QQQ - RV_SPY = IV_QQQ - IV_SPY (realised vol spread equals the entry implied spread).

greeks_at_inception.gamma: long the cheap index, short the rich one; vega-neutral means more dollar gamma on the lower-vol (long SPY) leg, since dollar gamma = Vega/(sigma*T)
greeks_at_inception.theta: slightly positive when short the higher-vol leg (theta ~ 0.5*Vega*sigma/T per leg)
greeks_at_inception.vega: about 0 net; long the vol spread cheap-minus-rich

strategies.when_to_use: When the implied vol spread between two correlated indices (VXN-VIX, RVX-VIX, VXD-VIX) is at an extreme z-score relative to its history and to the realised vol spread; bets on mean reversion of the spread.
strategies.risks: The spread is regime-dependent (tech-led markets keep VXN-VIX wide for long periods); two hedging programmes; basis between ETF options and the Cboe indices.
strategies.margin_note: The short straddle leg is naked; PM offsets correlated broad indices within the same class group (+6%/-8% stress); Reg-T gives no offset.
strategies.crypto_notes: Crypto twin: the ETH DVOL / BTC DVOL ratio (historically ~1.2-1.5) mean-reverts. Both are inverse and each is hedged with its own perp; IBIT vs ETHA options are the US-regulated route.
strategies.metals_notes: Metals twin: the silver vs gold vol ratio (SLV IV / GLD IV, or SI vs GC). GC/SI are American on futures, and SPAN cross-margins the pair; GLD/SLV are equity options.
variants: VXN-VIX via QQQ vs SPY straddles
strategies.claim: After the 60-day z-score of VXN - VIX passes +/-2, the statistic s*[(VXN - VIX) - (RV_QQQ - RV_SPY)] over the next 21 trading days, with s = +1 for z > +2 and -1 for z < -2, is positive on average: the realised spread falls short of an extreme-wide implied spread and exceeds an extreme-narrow one.

trial.statistic: Mean of s*[(VXN_t - VIX_t) - (RV_QQQ - RV_SPY)_{t,t+21}] over event entries; secondary: model-priced vega-neutral straddle-pair P&L.
trial.null: Mean <= 0 (the implied spread is an unbiased forecast of the realised spread).
trial.procedure: Daily VXN from 2009-09-14 (the free file starts there, not 2001), VIX, SPY and QQQ closes; event entries with non-overlapping 21d holds; studentized block bootstrap; walk-forward z-window (40/60/120 declared, deflated).
trial.data: CBOE VIX, VXN and RVX (archive); SPY, QQQ and IWM closes (archive). Index-implied vols, model-free for the statistic.
trial.pass: Mean > 0 with the 95% CI excluding zero, win rate > 0.6, same sign in both halves.
trial.controls: Unconditional spread (no signal); random-entry placebo with a matched count; RVX-VIX replication with IWM.

strategies.harness_suggestion: New harness_vol_spread pairing harness_vrp_nasdaq and harness_vrp_spx inputs: implied-minus-realised spread differential conditioned on the VXN-VIX z-score; RVX twin from harness_vrp_russell.

strategies.name: Dispersion trade (short index vol, long component vol)

legs.strike_rule: ATM on each top-N component, qty_i = w_i * Vega_idx / Vega_i (vega-weighted, so the component vegas sum to the index vega)
ATM on each component, same weights
daily delta hedge on every straddle

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: P&L ~ sum_i w_i*Vega_idx*(RV_i - IV_i) - Vega_idx*(RV_idx - IV_idx). Since sigma_idx^2 = sum_i sum_j w_i w_j rho_ij sigma_i sigma_j, this is short correlation: it profits when realised correlation is below implied correlation (components move idiosyncratically while the index stays calm).
strategies.max_profit: About vega notional x the gap between implied and realised correlation x average component vol. Best case: the index straddle credit is kept while the components move.
strategies.max_loss: Large when correlation goes to 1 in a crash: the short index straddle loses full gamma while the component straddles gain less; plus hedging costs on N legs.
strategies.breakevens: Realised correlation = implied correlation, with rho = (sigma_idx^2 - sum w_i^2 sigma_i^2) / (sum_{i!=j} w_i w_j sigma_i sigma_j) evaluated on IVs (implied) or RVs (realised).

greeks_at_inception.gamma: short index gamma, long single-name gamma. Summed in dollars the vega-weighted book is net short gamma: dollar gamma = Vega/(sigma*T), and components have higher sigma, so they carry less dollar gamma per unit vega. The gamma-weighted variant flattens this
greeks_at_inception.theta: net negative (component theta ~ 0.5*Vega*sigma_i/T summed exceeds the index's 0.5*Vega*sigma_idx/T because sum w_i sigma_i > sigma_idx)

strategies.when_to_use: When implied correlation (Cboe COR1M/COR3M) is high relative to realised, i.e. index vol is rich relative to the component basket; typically in calm markets where structured-product flows sell single-name vol and buy index vol.
strategies.risks: Correlation spikes to 1 in crises (the trade is short crash correlation); execution and hedging costs across N legs; component earnings moves; weight drift; capacity.
strategies.margin_note: The short index straddle is naked; the component straddles are long (debit). PM nets vega across legs within limits (+6%/-8% index stress, +/-15% single stocks); Reg-T does not net. The SPX leg is cash-settled with Section 1256; component legs are American equity options.
strategies.crypto_notes: No liquid crypto-index options in the US; the practical twin is a 2-asset correlation trade on Deribit (long ETH straddle vs short BTC straddle, vega-weighted, correlation ~0.8). Inverse settlement in each coin, each hedged with its own perp.
strategies.metals_notes: Long GLD and SLV straddles vs a short GDX (miners) straddle, or the gold-silver vol ratio. GC/SI options are American on futures with SPAN; GLD/SLV are equity options.
variants: Variance-swap dispersion (short index strip, long component strips)
Vega- vs gamma- vs theta-weighted dispersion
Reverse dispersion (long correlation) ahead of macro shocks
strategies.claim: Cboe COR1M (implied correlation of the top-50 SPX constituents) exceeds the subsequently realised 21-day correlation of the same constituents, computed with the same formula on realised vols and index weights, on average.

trial.statistic: Mean of COR1M_t/100 - rho_real(t..t+21), with rho_real = (RV_idx^2 - sum w_i^2 RV_i^2) / (sum_{i!=j} w_i w_j RV_i RV_j).
trial.procedure: COR1M daily since 2006-01 (archive) vs realised correlation from constituent closes and point-in-time weights; non-overlapping 21d windows (~240); studentized block bootstrap; walk-forward. The P&L leg runs once 60+ daily captures of the top-20 components exist.
trial.data: CBOE COR1M and DSPX history (archive); daily closes and weights of the top-50 SPX constituents (NOT in the archive); constituent chain capture for the P&L.
trial.pass: Mean gap > 0.05 with the 95% CI excluding zero; positive in both halves; crisis months (VIX > 30) reported separately.
trial.controls: VIX-tercile stratification; equal-weight vs cap-weight realised correlation; sector-ETF realised correlation (archive) as a cross-check.

strategies.blocked_on: daily closes and point-in-time weights of the top-50 SPX constituents (implied side COR1M is reachable now); constituent chain capture ~60 days for a first P&L read.
strategies.harness_suggestion: New harness_dispersion: COR1M/DSPX via cboe_index_history, constituent closes via the fetch layer, realised correlation by the Cboe formula; P&L via build_position per component once captures exist.

strategies.name: Event vol: implied move vs realised move (earnings / macro straddles)

legs.expiry_rule: first expiry after the event (1-7 DTE), entered the day before the event

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: C0 - |S_T - K|, where C0/S is the implied move (the straddle is about 0.8*IV*sqrt(T) of spot); it profits when the post-event move |S_T - K| is smaller than C0. The reverse (long straddle) is used when the implied move is below the name's historical event moves.
strategies.max_profit: C0 (zero realised move).
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded above; K - C0 below.
strategies.breakevens: K - C0 and K + C0 (the implied move).

greeks_at_inception.theta: very positive (the event premium collapses at the print)

strategies.when_to_use: Single-name earnings when the implied move exceeds the stock's own historical mean absolute earnings move; index or macro versions around FOMC, CPI and NFP using 0-2 DTE SPY/SPX; gold around FOMC; BTC around macro prints.
strategies.risks: Fat-tailed outcomes (a 20-30% earnings gap on an 8% implied move); binary, one-shot risk per event; American assignment on the short ITM leg after the print; wide spreads near the close.
strategies.margin_note: Naked straddle margin on single names (high; PM +/-15%); the iron-butterfly variant defines the risk. SPX event straddles are cash-settled with Section 1256; GC via SPAN.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit daily expiries let you trade the straddle expiring at 08:00 UTC after a scheduled US print (CPI at 12:30 UTC falls inside the next daily). Inverse settlement in BTC; the move is realised continuously 24/7.
strategies.metals_notes: GC weekly options span FOMC and CPI (American on futures, SPAN); GLD short-dated equity options are the ETF route.
variants: Short straddle into earnings (sell the implied move)
Long straddle when the implied move < historical realised move
Event calendar: short event-week straddle, long next-month straddle

trial.statistic: Mean of |S_T - K|/C0 per event; equivalently, mean short-straddle P&L as a fraction of C0 = 1 - mean ratio, after a 5% spread cost.
trial.procedure: Implied move from the captured chain the day before each earnings date; realised move to the first post-event expiry; pooled across names; studentized bootstrap clustered by date; walk-forward across seasons; deflated over the name filters tried.

trial.controls: Non-event days with the same DTE (should show the ordinary, smaller VRP); shuffled event-date placebo.

strategies.name: Forward-start variance / term-premium strip (short far strip, long near strip)

legs.strike_rule: all K < F_far, weight 2*dK/((T_far - T_near)*K^2) (unit forward-variance notional)
all K < F_near, the same weight 2*dK/((T_far - T_near)*K^2)
daily delta / log-contract hedge as in the variance strip

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Short forward variance over [T_near, T_far] at strike F^2 = (T_far*K_far - T_near*K_near)/(T_far - T_near); for SPX 30d/93d, F^2 = (93*VIX3M^2 - 30*VIX^2)/63. Both strips carry the same per-strike weight (total-variance strips differenced and divided by T_far - T_near), so after T_near the position is a plain short variance swap over the forward window: P&L = N*(F^2 - RV(T_near..T_far)).
strategies.max_profit: N*F^2 (forward realised variance zero).
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded in forward realised variance.
strategies.breakevens: RV(T_near..T_far) = F^2.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: about 0 until T_near (equal per-strike weights give equal constant dollar gamma in both strips), then negative
greeks_at_inception.theta: sign of sigma_far^2 - sigma_near^2 (theta ~ -0.5*dollar gamma*sigma^2 per strip): positive in contango, negative in backwardation; positive after T_near
greeks_at_inception.vega: negative to far-dated vol, positive to near-dated: short the term-structure slope

strategies.when_to_use: When the VIX curve is steep (VIX3M well above VIX): the forward variance embeds the VRP plus a term premium, and isolating the forward window means a near-term event does not hurt. It is the variance-swap analogue of the reverse calendar.
strategies.risks: A shock inside the forward window; the near strip must be hedged until it expires; executing two strips (40-100 strikes); truncation error on the far strip.
strategies.margin_note: The short far strip is naked; PM nets it against the long near strip until T_near (+6%/-8% SPX stress). SPX is cash-settled, European and Section 1256; the ES futures hedge uses SPAN.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit lists monthly and quarterly expiries, so forward variance strips can be built; convert inverse prices to USD before applying the 1/K^2 weights; hedge with the perp. The BTC curve is in steep contango in calm bull markets (large forward premium) and inverts in crashes.
strategies.metals_notes: GC options on serial and quarterly futures: the forward window spans different futures contracts (calendar basis), and American exercise complicates the strip; the GLD strip is cleaner.
variants: Long forward variance as a hedge for a short near-term VRP book
VIX futures spread (M1 vs M3) as the futures analogue
strategies.claim: Since 2009-09, the 1-to-3-month SPX forward variance premium as a fraction of implied, (F^2 - RV(22..63))/F^2 with F^2 = (93*VIX3M^2 - 30*VIX^2)/63, exceeds the spot 30-day premium fraction (VIX^2 - RV(1..21))/VIX^2 on average.

trial.statistic: Mean paired difference [(F^2 - RV_fwd)/F^2] - [(VIX^2 - RV_spot)/VIX^2] per entry.
trial.procedure: Daily VIX and VIX3M from 2009-09-18, SPY closes; non-overlapping 63d cycles (~68) plus all daily starts with a 63-day-block studentized bootstrap; walk-forward halves. Strip discretisation error is measured on the captured SPX chain at the two expiries.
trial.data: CBOE VIX and VIX3M (archive), SPY closes, captured SPX chain. Model-free.
trial.pass: Paired difference > 0 with the 95% CI excluding zero; forward win rate > 0.7 (reported).
trial.controls: Shuffled-VIX3M placebo; sensitivity run excluding 2020; level (not ratio) version as in harness_term_vs_spot.

strategies.harness_suggestion: harness_term_vs_spot (T-231) computes the level difference with (3*VIX3M^2 - VIX^2)/2; switch to 93/30/63 and add the ratio form; add a two-expiry strip builder in mandel/options.

strategies.name: Gold volatility premium (GVZ) via GLD straddles / GC strangles

legs.strike_rule: ATM on GLD (or delta 0.15 on GC for the strangle variant)
ATM on GLD (or delta -0.15 on GC)
daily delta hedge in GLD shares (or GC/MGC futures)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Unhedged: C0 - |S_T - K|. Delta-hedged: about Vega/(2*sigma)*(GVZ^2 - RV_GLD^2), roughly Vega*(GVZ - RV). GVZ applies the VIX methodology to GLD options, so it is the natural variance strike.
strategies.max_profit: The straddle credit C0 (unhedged, at S_T = K); hedged, bounded by about C0.
strategies.max_loss: Unhedged: unbounded above, K - C0 below. Hedged: unbounded in realised variance (gold gaps on geopolitical events and liquidity squeezes, e.g. March 2020).
strategies.breakevens: Unhedged: K - C0 and K + C0. Hedged: RV = GVZ.
strategies.when_to_use: When GVZ exceeds gold's trailing realised vol by a wide margin and no scheduled catalyst (FOMC, CPI) falls inside the window. Gold's VRP is smaller and less reliable than equity's because gold vol spikes on upside moves too.
strategies.risks: Two-sided jumps (gold rallies violently in crises and also sells off in liquidations); GC assignment creates an overnight futures position; silver is much jumpier.
strategies.margin_note: GLD: naked straddle under Reg-T, or PM at +/-15% (non-index ETF). GC/SI options: American, exercise into futures, SPAN margin cross-margined with the futures hedge, Section 1256 60/40. MGC (micro gold) options exist for small size. GLD shares are a grantor trust taxed as collectibles; GLD options are equity options.
strategies.crypto_notes: The BTC twin is the DVOL VRP entry (btc_dvol_vrp).
strategies.metals_notes: GVZ has free daily history on Cboe, but the CSV starts on 2009-09-18. Silver: SLV straddles or SI options; there is no silver vol index in Mandel's free index set, so compute 30-day ATM IV from the SLV chain capture. PL/PA options are thin.
variants: GC 15-delta strangle with a futures hedge
Gold/silver vol ratio (long SLV vol, short GLD vol, vega-neutral)
GVZ-gated: trade only when GVZ - RV > 5 points
Long GLD straddle into FOMC when GVZ < 14
strategies.claim: Since 2009-09, the 30-day gold variance premium, (GVZ/100)^2 minus the subsequently realised 21-trading-day variance of GLD, is positive on average.

trial.statistic: Mean of (GVZ_t/100)^2 - RV_GLD(t..t+21) (annualised); secondary: the premium as a fraction of implied variance compared with the SPX figure (VIX/SPY) on the same dates.
trial.procedure: Non-overlapping 21d cycles from 2009-09-18 (~200); studentized block bootstrap; walk-forward thirds; side-by-side with harness_vrp_spx on common dates.
trial.data: CBOE GVZ (archive), GLD closes (archive). Model-free (index-implied variance).
trial.pass: Mean > 0 with the 95% CI excluding zero, positive in at least 2 of 3 thirds.
trial.controls: Buy-and-hold GLD (harness_controls); shuffled-GVZ placebo; GC=F front-futures closes (archive) instead of GLD.

strategies.harness_suggestion: harness_vrp_gold (T-50) runs this; add the ratio-to-SPX secondary and a 15-delta strangle pricer, and add SLV ATM IV from surface_summary for the silver twin.

strategies.name: Oil and bond volatility premium (OVX via USO, VXTLT via TLT) and cross-asset VRP portfolio

legs.strike_rule: daily delta hedge (USO/TLT shares or CL/ZB futures)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Unhedged: C0 - |S_T - K|. Delta-hedged: about Vega*(IV_index - RV), with OVX (Cboe crude oil ETF vol index, from USO options) or VXTLT (TLT vol index) as the implied.
strategies.max_profit: The straddle credit C0.
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded (oil: the April 2020 negative WTI print and USO's restructuring; bonds: the March 2020 and 2022 rate shocks).
strategies.breakevens: Unhedged: K - C0 and K + C0. Hedged: RV = IV.
strategies.when_to_use: To diversify a vol-selling book across asset classes whose VRPs are imperfectly correlated with equity's. The oil VRP is large but has extreme tails; the bond VRP depends on the rates regime.
strategies.risks: USO is a futures roll fund (contango drag, a 1:8 reverse split in 2020, restructuring); CL options settle into futures; TLT's duration is ~16, so a 50bp rate shock moves it ~8%.
strategies.margin_note: USO/TLT: equity options, Reg-T or PM at +/-15%. CL/ZB options: American, SPAN, Section 1256; CL weekly options exist.
strategies.crypto_notes: n/a (see btc_dvol_vrp; BTC is excluded from the main portfolio test because DVOL starts in 2021-03).
strategies.metals_notes: Same structure as the gold entry; copper (HG) options are the thin base-metal route.

CL 20-delta strangle with a futures hedge
Equal-vega cross-asset VRP portfolio SPX/GLD/USO/TLT (+BTC on its shorter sample)

trial.pass: Sharpe difference > 0 with bootstrap p < 0.05, positive in both halves.
trial.controls: Equal-weight buy-and-hold of the underlyings; shuffled-index placebo; drop-one-asset sensitivity.

strategies.name: Put-call IV spread (parity-deviation) stock selection

legs.strike_rule: ATM on each name in the top quintile of (call IV - put IV) at the same strike and expiry
ATM, same top-quintile names (long call + short put = synthetic long)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Per top name: S_T - K - (C0 - P0) (synthetic long forward). Per bottom name: K - S_T + (C0 - P0) (synthetic short). The equal-weight basket is long high-spread names and short low-spread names (Cremers-Weinbaum).
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded on the long synthetics; K + (C0 - P0) per short synthetic.
strategies.max_loss: K + (C0 - P0) per long synthetic (stock to zero); unbounded on the short synthetics.
strategies.breakevens: Per name: S_T = K + (C0 - P0).

greeks_at_inception.delta: +1 per top name and -1 per bottom name; about 0 for a dollar-neutral basket
greeks_at_inception.vega: about 0 (the call and put vegas cancel at the same strike)

strategies.when_to_use: Cross-sectional signal: call-minus-put IV spreads at the same strike reflect informed option demand or short-sale constraints and have predicted next-week stock returns in the literature. Express it with stock or with synthetics.
strategies.risks: Hard-to-borrow names make put IV > call IV mechanically (borrow cost, not information); early-exercise premium in American puts; dividends; transaction costs on weekly rebalancing; decay of the anomaly after publication.
strategies.margin_note: Synthetic positions are margined like stock (naked short puts and calls under Reg-T; PM +/-15% for single stocks).
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit the put-call IV gap at the same strike mostly reflects the forward/basis; compute IVs against the future of that expiry. Not a cross-section with only BTC and ETH.
strategies.metals_notes: GLD/SLV are only two names (no cross-section); a GC put-call IV gap reflects futures basis.
variants: Smirk signal (OTM put IV - ATM call IV, Xing-Zhang-Zhao)
strategies.claim: Weekly, equal-weight long-short portfolios of US large caps formed on the ATM call-minus-put IV spread (top minus bottom quintile) earn a positive mean return over the following week.

trial.statistic: Mean weekly long-short return; t-stat with Newey-West errors.
trial.procedure: Weekly IV spreads from the captured chains (same strike and expiry, nearest-ATM, ~30 DTE), next-week returns from closes; exclude names with no bid; walk-forward; deflated Sharpe over the spread definitions tried.
trial.data: Daily chain capture of >= 100 US large caps (CHAIN_SYMBOLS has 3 single names today) and their daily closes.
trial.pass: Mean > 0 at p < 0.05 after 10 bps per side, positive in both halves.
trial.controls: Borrow-cost proxy exclusion (drop names with put IV - call IV > 5 points from known hard-to-borrow lists); size and momentum-neutral version; random-quintile placebo.

strategies.blocked_on: chain capture of >= 100 large caps (add to CHAIN_SYMBOLS) and their daily closes; >= 52 weekly cycles (~1 year).
strategies.harness_suggestion: New harness_iv_spread_xs on surface_summary extended with same-strike call/put IVs per name; weekly portfolio sorts in the underlying-library style.

strategies.name: Put-skew richness sale (1x2 put ratio spread, delta-hedged)

legs.strike_rule: spot S0; offsets the -0.05 option delta (-0.25 + 2*0.10) to zero

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: C0 = 2P(K1) - P(K2), signed. With 25d/10d strikes it is usually a small DEBIT (C0 < 0); a zero-cost ratio needs a nearer short strike (about 15d). Options only: S_T >= K2: C0. K1 <= S_T < K2: C0 + (K2 - S_T). S_T < K1: C0 + K2 - 2K1 + S_T (slope +1 from the extra short put). The static 0.05-share leg adds 0.05(S_T - S0).
strategies.max_profit: (K2 - K1) + C0 at S_T = K1 (options only; the share leg adds 0.05(K1 - S0)).
strategies.max_loss: 2K1 - K2 - C0 at S_T = 0 (options only); if C0 < 0 the loss above K2 is only |C0|.
strategies.breakevens: Lower: S* = 2K1 - K2 - C0. Upper: none if C0 >= 0; if C0 < 0, S* = K2 + C0 = K2 - |C0|.

greeks_at_inception.delta: -0.05 from the options (-0.25 + 2*0.10); 0 after the +0.05 share leg
greeks_at_inception.gamma: about flat at spot (short 2*phi(1.28)/sigma_10 vs long phi(0.67)/sigma_25, i.e. 0.351/sigma_10 vs 0.318/sigma_25: slightly positive when the 10d IV exceeds the 25d IV by more than ~10%); strongly negative in the tail near and below K1
greeks_at_inception.vega: small negative (vega ~ phi(d1): 2*0.176 short vs 0.318 long); short skew steepness (10d IV vs 25d IV)

strategies.when_to_use: When the 10d-25d put IV slope is steep relative to its own history (SKEW high, VIX moderate). It harvests the premium in far OTM puts, which the CBOE SKEW white paper converts into implied tail probabilities well above realised frequencies.
strategies.risks: A gap or crash below K1: losses accelerate just as skew and IV explode and liquidity vanishes; hedging costs; assignment on American ETF options; the second short put is naked for margin.
strategies.margin_note: One short put is covered by the long higher-strike put (a bear put spread); the extra short put is naked (Reg-T 20% equity / 15% broad-based index rule). Portfolio margin (FINRA 4210(g)) stresses SPX/SPY at +6%/-8%. SPX is cash-settled with no early assignment and Section 1256 treatment.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC put skew steepens in drawdowns and flattens or inverts in rallies. On Deribit's inverse options a short put pays out (K-S_T)/S_T BTC, so the BTC-denominated tail loss is convex as BTC falls. Settlement is at 08:00 UTC, options are European, and the perpetual hedge carries funding.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold's downside skew is usually flatter than equity's, so the credit is smaller; silver has fat two-sided tails. GC/SI options are American on futures; SPAN margins the ratio as a single risk array; Section 1256 applies.
variants: Broken-wing 1x2x1 (buy a third, lower put to cap the tail)
Christmas tree put (long K3, short K2, short K1)
Call-side ratio for call-skewed assets (gold, BTC)
Zero-cost version with a 15d short strike
strategies.claim: The CBOE SKEW-implied risk-neutral probability of a 30-day S&P 500 log return below -2 sigma, P = 0.0228 + 0.0270*(SKEW-100)/10 (the white paper's Gram-Charlier mapping: 2.3% at SKEW 100, 14.45% at 145), exceeds the realised frequency of 21-trading-day returns below -2*(VIX/100)*sqrt(21/252) by more than 2 percentage points on average.

trial.statistic: Mean over windows of P_SKEW(t) - 1{r_{t,t+21} < -2*(VIX_t/100)*sqrt(21/252)}.
trial.procedure: Non-overlapping 21d windows since 1990 (^GSPC closes before SPY's 1993 start); studentized block bootstrap; require the gap to be positive in each of three sub-periods. Report the SKEW > 135 conditional gap only as a secondary, with PBO across thresholds 125/130/135/140.
trial.data: CBOE SKEW and VIX history and ^GSPC/SPY closes (archive). Index-only: this tests the tail premium the strategy sells, not the 1x2's P&L, which needs 10d/25d IVs from chain capture.
trial.pass: Lower 95% bound of the mean gap > 0.02, and the gap is positive in at least 2 of 3 sub-periods.
trial.controls: Constant-normal benchmark (P = 2.28%) to show SKEW adds information; shuffled-SKEW placebo. SKEW readings above 145 (154.7 on 2026-10-13) are outside the white-paper table and use the formula's extrapolation; report them separately.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Add skew_implied_tail (the closed form above, no table interpolation) to harness_skew_tail. For the 1x2 P&L, extend surface_summary to store 10-delta put/call IVs: it stores only ATM and 25d today, so 10d history is not accumulating yet.

strategies.name: Risk reversal (25-delta skew trade)

legs.strike_rule: spot S0; static hedge of the +0.50 option delta at inception (the delta-hedged variant re-hedges daily)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Options only: (S_T-Kc)^+ - (Kp-S_T)^+ + C0, with C0 = P(Kp) - C(Kc) signed (C0 > 0 is a net credit, usual when put skew is rich). Flat at C0 between Kp and Kc, slope +1 above Kc and below Kp. With the static 0.5-share short (what the engine draws): V = (S_T-Kc)^+ - (Kp-S_T)^+ - 0.5(S_T-S0) + C0, slope +0.5 below Kp, -0.5 between Kp and Kc, +0.5 above Kc (local max C0 + 0.5(S0-Kp) at Kp, local min C0 - 0.5(Kc-S0) at Kc). The daily re-hedged version isolates skew-vega plus gamma/theta carry: it gains when 25d put IV minus 25d call IV compresses.
strategies.max_profit: Options only: unbounded, S_T - Kc + C0 above Kc. Static-hedged: unbounded, 0.5*S_T - Kc + 0.5*S0 + C0 above Kc. Daily-hedged: approx. Vega_25d*(skew_entry - skew_exit) plus carry.
strategies.max_loss: Options only: Kp - C0 at S_T = 0. Static-hedged: max(Kp - 0.5*S0 - C0 at S_T = 0, 0.5*(Kc - S0) - C0 at S_T = Kc). Daily-hedged: gap risk below Kp, made worse because skew widens as spot falls.
strategies.breakevens: Options only: if C0 >= 0, S* = Kp - C0 (no upside breakeven); if C0 < 0 (debit), S* = Kc - C0 = Kc + |C0| only. Static-hedged: up to three, S1 = 2Kp - S0 - 2C0 (valid if < Kp), S2 = S0 + 2C0 (valid if in [Kp,Kc]), S3 = 2Kc - S0 - 2C0 (valid if > Kc); profit on (S1,S2) and above S3.

greeks_at_inception.delta: +0.50 from the options (short -0.25d put gives +0.25, long 0.25d call +0.25); 0 after the 0.5-share short
greeks_at_inception.gamma: about zero; slightly positive when put IV > call IV (at equal |delta| gamma = phi(d1)/(S*sigma*sqrt(T)), so the higher-IV put carries less gamma); turns negative as spot falls toward Kp
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive when put IV > call IV (per-leg theta ~ -S*phi(d1)*sigma/(2*sqrt(T)); the short higher-IV put dominates)
greeks_at_inception.vega: about zero net (equal-delta legs have equal BS vega S*phi(d1)*sqrt(T)); short skew-vega: loses when put IV rises relative to call IV

strategies.when_to_use: When the 25d put-call IV skew (or CBOE SKEW) is at a high percentile of its own history and the trader thinks the left tail is overpriced; the unhedged form also works as a cheap synthetic long in uptrends.
strategies.risks: A crash hits the short put while skew widens; pin/assignment risk on American ETF and stock options; the hedge bleeds in whipsaw markets; margin rises with VIX.
strategies.margin_note: Equity/ETF Reg-T: the short put is naked (20% of underlying minus OTM amount plus premium, minimum 10% of strike; broad-based index 15%). Portfolio margin (FINRA 4210(g)) stresses high-cap broad-based indices (SPX, SPY) at +6%/-8%, non-high-cap broad indices at +/-10% and single stocks or narrow ETFs at +/-15%. SPX/XSP are cash-settled and European, with Section 1256 60/40 tax treatment.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC skew on Deribit is often call-rich in bull markets, so the trade often runs the other way (short 25d call, long 25d put). Deribit options are European and inverse: premium and settlement are in BTC at 08:00 UTC, the market trades 24/7 and there are no dividends. Because the premium is in BTC it carries BTC delta, so hedge with a premium-adjusted delta through the perpetual, whose funding adds a carry term the equity version does not have.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold skew is usually call-rich (the fear bid is on the upside), so the metals risk reversal is often short call / long put. GC options are American, exercise into a futures position, use SPAN futures-style margin and get Section 1256 60/40. GLD/SLV options are the equity route (American, physically settled in ETF shares); GLD shares are taxed as collectibles.
variants: Zero-cost risk reversal (choose Kc so C(Kc)=P(Kp))
Skew calendar: short near-dated 25d put skew vs long far-dated (see skew_term_structure)
strategies.claim: Since 1991, the frequency of 21-trading-day S&P 500 log returns below -2 VIX-implied sigma is not higher, by 1 percentage point or more, in windows starting with CBOE SKEW above its trailing 252-day 80th percentile than in windows starting with SKEW below its 20th percentile (the extra put premium a high-SKEW risk reversal sells is not paid back by more realised left-tail events).

trial.statistic: Difference (high-SKEW minus low-SKEW) in the frequency of r_{t,t+21} < -2*(VIX_t/100)*sqrt(21/252) on ^GSPC; secondary: difference in realised 21d skewness of daily returns.
trial.null: freq_high - freq_low >= 0.01 (SKEW carries real information about future left tails).
trial.procedure: Daily SKEW and VIX since 1990-01; ^GSPC closes (archive daily-history--GSPC, because SPY only starts in 1993-01); trailing 252-day SKEW percentile, so the first usable window is in 1991. Use overlapping daily-start 21d windows with a 21-day-block studentized bootstrap, because non-overlapping windows leave only ~85 per quintile and a handful of tail events. Reject the null if the bootstrap 95% upper bound of the difference is < 0.01. Deflate for the two cut pairs tried (80/20 and 90/10).
trial.data: CBOE SKEW and VIX daily history and ^GSPC daily closes, all in the archive. Index data only, no option prices.
trial.pass: 95% upper bound of (freq_high - freq_low) < 0.01, and the realised-skewness difference is not significantly negative (p > 0.1) in both halves 1991-2008 and 2009-2026.
trial.controls: Shuffled-SKEW placebo; VIX-tercile stratification (SKEW must not proxy for the VIX level); sensitivity run excluding Oct-2008 and Mar-2020; repeat with the 21-day SKEW change instead of its level.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Extend harness_skew_tail (it already joins SKEW to SPY tails) with trailing-percentile buckets, the ^GSPC pre-1993 splice and the upper-bound equivalence decision rule. Log the skew-vega P&L from surface_summary iv_put25d/iv_call25d once 60+ captures exist.

strategies.name: Skew term-structure trade (near vs far 25-delta risk reversal)

legs.strike_rule: delta -0.25 (far, Kp_f); qty q = sqrt(T_near/T_far) for vega matching
daily delta hedge (option delta at inception = +0.5*(1 - q))

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At the near expiry: (S_T - Kc_n)^+ - (Kp_n - S_T)^+ plus the marked far reverse risk reversal q*[P_far(S_T) - C_far(S_T)] (time value at the far IVs), net of the entry credit. The trade is short near-dated skew and long far-dated skew: it profits when the near skew flattens relative to the far skew.
strategies.max_profit: Not closed form: bounded near expiry by the near risk reversal's credit plus far skew gains (mark the far legs).
strategies.max_loss: In a crash (S_T -> 0): about Kp_n - q*Kp_f - net entry credit (the near short put loses 1:1, the far long put recovers only q times its intrinsic plus time value); numerical with the far legs marked.
strategies.breakevens: Numerical on the engine grid with the far legs marked at their IVs.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: about 0 at inception (each equal-delta risk reversal is nearly gamma-neutral; slightly positive in the near leg when put IV > call IV); turns negative as spot falls toward Kp_n
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive when the near skew is steeper than the far (short the near higher-IV put)
greeks_at_inception.vega: about 0 flat vega; short near skew-vega, long far skew-vega

strategies.when_to_use: When the near-dated 25-delta skew (in vol points) is steeper than the far-dated one, as happens in stress or ahead of events when hedging flows concentrate in front months. In delta terms SPX skew is usually flat to rising with maturity, so this trade is a conditional one, not a standing position.
strategies.risks: A crash before the near expiry; skew-term inversion (near skew can flatten because spot falls, not because puts cheapen); four legs plus a hedge.
strategies.margin_note: The near short put is partly covered by the far long put (diagonal treatment under Reg-T when the far expiry is later); the far short call is naked unless PM. SPX is cash-settled with Section 1256.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC skew term structure flips sign often (near-dated put skew in drawdowns, far-dated call skew in bull markets); deribit_book mark_iv per strike makes it observable; inverse, European, perp hedge.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold skew is on the call side, so the trade mirrors (short near call skew, long far call skew). GC is American into futures with SPAN; GLD trades as equity options.
variants: Put-only skew calendar (short near 25d put, long far 25d put)
Long near skew / short far skew ahead of a dated event
strategies.claim: Conditional on SPY's 30-day 25-delta put-minus-call IV skew exceeding its 90-day skew at entry, the delta-hedged short-near/long-far skew position held for 21 trading days has a positive mean P&L.

trial.statistic: Mean 21-trading-day P&L of the hedged four-leg position (build_position on captured mids), per unit of near vega; secondary: mean 21d change in skew_30d - skew_90d.
trial.procedure: Daily captures give surface_summary skew25 at the expiries nearest 30 and 90 DTE; entries on signal days, non-overlapping 21d holds; studentized bootstrap clustered by entry month; walk-forward after 2 years.
trial.data: Daily CBOE chain capture (SPY, _SPX, GLD, IBIT) from 2026-10-14; SKEW index history as a level control.
trial.pass: Mean P&L > 0 at p < 0.05 over at least 36 signal cycles.
trial.controls: Flat-vega single-expiry risk reversal; unconditional (all days) version; SKEW-level stratification.

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture: ~90 days to see how often the signal fires, and ~36 signal cycles (likely 3+ years) for the P&L test.
strategies.harness_suggestion: surface_summary already stores skew25 per expiry; add a per-day near-vs-far skew series and feed build_position with two expiries.

strategies.name: SKEW-conditioned tail hedge (put spread when skew is cheap)

legs.expiry_rule: 45-90 DTE, same (30 DTE in the trial)

strategies.max_profit: (K2 - K1) - D0 for S_T <= K1.
strategies.max_loss: D0 for S_T >= K2.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: net positive at inception (long 25d gamma phi(0.67)/sigma_25 > short 10d gamma phi(1.28)/sigma_10); negative only near and below K1
greeks_at_inception.vega: net positive (vega ~ phi(d1): 0.318 long vs 0.176 short); short the 10d-minus-25d wing slope, since it sells the richest far wing

strategies.when_to_use: Buy protection when SKEW is low (tail cheap) and VIX is low. A spread rather than an outright put, because the short 10d leg sells the part of the smile that is structurally richest.
strategies.risks: Protection is capped below K1 in a true crash; theta bleeds when nothing happens; low SKEW can persist for long stretches.
strategies.margin_note: Debit spread: pay the debit, no further margin. SPX/XSP are cash-settled with Section 1256 treatment; SPY/GLD are American, so a deep-ITM short leg can be assigned early.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit BTC put spreads are quoted and settled in BTC, so a hedge for a BTC holding pays out in a coin whose USD value is falling (payoff (K2-K1)/S_T BTC below K1); size it in USD-equivalent. 24/7 trading with no weekend gaps.
strategies.metals_notes: GC put spreads exercise into futures (American); GLD put spreads are equity options. Gold's put wing is cheaper than equity's, so the hedge is relatively inexpensive against bullion or GLD; Section 1256 applies on GC.
variants: Outright 25d put when SKEW < 15th pct and VIX < 15
Put ladder (long K3, short K2, short K1) at near-zero cost
Collar version with a short 25d call (hedging family)
strategies.claim: Model-priced: a 30-DTE 25d/10d SPX put spread bought only in months when CBOE SKEW is below its trailing 252-day 20th percentile has a higher mean ratio of expiry payoff to entry debit than the same spread bought every month.

trial.statistic: mean(payoff/debit | SKEW < p20) - mean(payoff/debit | all months). The debit is model-priced with BS: ATM IV = VIX/100 times the ATM-to-VIX ratio measured on the captured SPX chain; strike IVs come from a linear-in-log-moneyness smile with slope kappa*(SKEW-100), kappa calibrated once on the 2026-10-14 SPX surface. Payoff from ^GSPC at expiry.
trial.procedure: Monthly 30-DTE entries since 1991, held to expiry (21 trading days, non-overlapping); walk-forward trailing percentile; studentized block bootstrap of the difference; deflated Sharpe of the conditional series. Rerun with kappa x0.5 and x2, because the smile model drives the debit.
trial.data: CBOE SKEW and VIX, ^GSPC/SPY closes (model-priced, not market prices); today's SPX surface for kappa. Switch to captured 25d/10d IVs once surface_summary stores 10d and 36+ monthly captures exist.
trial.pass: Difference > 0 with the 95% CI excluding zero, at least 60 low-SKEW entries, and the sign unchanged at kappa x0.5 and x2.
trial.controls: Random-timing placebo with the same entry count; VIX-tercile stratification; a VIX < 15 gate as an alternative rule counted in the deflation.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Reuse the monthly model-priced overlay of harness_short_straddle/_overlay_pair with a SKEW gate and a skew-slope pricer; swap in real 25d/10d IVs from surface_summary when available.

strategies.name: Smile curvature trade (credit iron butterfly, implied kurtosis)

legs.expiry_rule: 30-60 DTE, same (7 DTE weekly as a secondary)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Credit C0 = Straddle(K2) - P(K1) - C(K3). V = C0 - |S_T - K2| for K1 <= S_T <= K3; C0 - (K2 - K1) below K1; C0 - (K3 - K2) above K3. OIC calls this a short iron butterfly. The debit mirror (long straddle, short wings) is OIC's long iron butterfly and is long implied kurtosis. 25d wings are asymmetric in strike: with put skew, K2 - K1 > K3 - K2.
strategies.max_profit: C0 at S_T = K2. Mirror: max(K2-K1, K3-K2) - C0.
strategies.max_loss: max(K2 - K1, K3 - K2) - C0. Mirror: C0.
strategies.breakevens: K2 - C0 and K2 + C0 (provided C0 < each wing width); same points for the mirror.

greeks_at_inception.delta: about 0 (ATM straddle delta of +0.05 to +0.1 partly offset by the asymmetric wings)
greeks_at_inception.vega: net negative: short two ATM vegas (phi(0)=0.399 each) vs long two wing vegas (phi(0.674)=0.318 each). The vega-neutral variant buys ~1.25x the wings. Short implied curvature (wing IV minus ATM IV)

strategies.when_to_use: Trade the 25-delta butterfly (average wing IV minus ATM IV) against realised excess kurtosis: sell the wings' richness when the butterfly is at a high percentile, and buy the wings (the mirror) when the smile is flat ahead of events.
strategies.risks: A large move loses the full wing width; realised kurtosis clusters (crashes); pin risk near K2 on American options; wide bid/ask on the wings.
strategies.margin_note: Defined risk: margin equals the max loss (wider wing minus credit) under both Reg-T and PM. Index versions are cash-settled with Section 1256 treatment.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC smiles are fairly symmetric and very curved (high implied kurtosis). Deribit's public book gives mark_iv per strike, so the 25d butterfly is observable from deribit_book. Inverse settlement: payoffs are paid in BTC at S_T.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold smile curvature is low and silver's high. GC/SI options are American on futures, and SPAN margins the four legs as one array; GLD/SLV trade as equity options.
variants: Call butterfly / put butterfly (same payoff on one side)
Butterfly vs variance strip to isolate kurtosis
strategies.claim: 30-DTE SPY credit iron butterflies (short ATM straddle, long 25-delta strangle) entered at the captured mid and held to expiry have a positive mean P&L per unit of max loss after paying half the quoted bid/ask on every leg.

trial.statistic: Mean of P&L / max loss per cycle; secondary: regression of the entry 25d butterfly (average wing IV minus ATM IV) on realised 30d excess kurtosis.
trial.procedure: Daily SPY/_SPX captures (surface_summary has ATM and 25d IVs and straddle mids; strike-level mids come from the raw chain). One entry per monthly expiry, held to expiry. A 7-DTE weekly version is a declared secondary that reaches 36 cycles in ~36 weeks. Studentized bootstrap clustered by expiry; walk-forward once 2 years exist.
trial.data: Daily CBOE chain capture (SPY, _SPX) from 2026-10-14; SPY/^GSPC closes.
trial.pass: Mean P&L/max loss > 0 at p < 0.05 over at least 36 cycles, with the same sign in both halves.
trial.controls: ATM short straddle alone over the same cycles (separates the level VRP from the curvature premium); vega-neutral variant; BS flat-smile control (zero curvature premium by construction).

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture: ~36 monthly cycles (~3 years) for the 30-DTE test, ~36 weeks for the 7-DTE secondary; a 90-day capture gives a first read on butterfly levels vs realised kurtosis.
strategies.harness_suggestion: New harness_smile_curvature: compute the 25d butterfly per capture day from surface_summary and the P&L via build_position plus the payoff engine on strike-level mids.

strategies.name: Static-arbitrage scan of the surface (negative butterflies, calendar inversions, vertical bounds)

legs.expiry_rule: same expiry for all three legs

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Long call butterfly: V = (S_T-K1)^+ - 2(S_T-K2)^+ + (S_T-K3)^+ - D0, a tent from 0 at K1 up to h at K2 and back to 0 at K3. No-arbitrage requires D0 >= 0 (call prices convex in strike). If the executable ask-side D0 is < 0, the trade is paid to hold a non-negative payoff. Sister checks: calendar (C_far >= C_near at the same strike for European options without dividends; total variance non-decreasing in T at fixed forward moneyness) and vertical (0 <= C(K1) - C(K2) <= (K2 - K1)*discount).
strategies.max_profit: h - D0 at S_T = K2.
strategies.max_loss: D0 if D0 > 0; none if the executable D0 < 0 (the arbitrage case), apart from early-assignment risk on American short legs.
strategies.breakevens: K1 + D0 and K3 - D0 (when D0 > 0).

greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative when centred at spot (positive when the body is far OTM)

strategies.when_to_use: Daily scan of every captured chain for executable static-arbitrage violations after fees; in practice it mostly serves as a data-quality filter for the surface feeding the other harnesses.
strategies.risks: Stale or crossed delayed quotes create false positives; American early exercise and dividends break the European bounds for ETFs and stocks; fees and legging risk.
strategies.margin_note: Long butterfly: debit, defined risk. Calendars on American options have assignment risk on the short near leg.
strategies.crypto_notes: deribit_book gives bid/ask per strike in BTC; apply the convexity bounds to USD-converted prices (price_btc x index) and include Deribit fees (capped at 12.5% of the option price).
strategies.metals_notes: GLD/SLV chains are captured daily; GC options are not captured (CME data is not in the free set).
variants: Put-call parity / box bounds (see harness_parity, harness_box_*)
strategies.claim: On at least 10% of capture days, the SPY or SPX chain contains at least one butterfly, calendar or vertical spread that violates static no-arbitrage bounds at executable bid/ask prices after $0.65/contract fees.

trial.statistic: Share of capture days with >= 1 executable violation (SPY or _SPX), plus the count and size of violations per day.
trial.procedure: For each capture and expiry, check monotonicity and convexity of call and put asks/bids in strike, vertical bounds, and calendar monotonicity of total variance at matched forward moneyness. Drop quotes with zero bid or crossed markets. Exact binomial CI over capture days.
trial.data: Daily CBOE chain capture (SPY, _SPX) from 2026-10-14 (the first day is available now); deribit_book for the crypto twin.
