strategies.name: Straddle-vs-VIX basis (ATM implied vol vs variance-swap strike)

legs.strike_rule: all K < F, weight 2*dK/(T*K^2), scaled so strip vega = straddle vega

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Long ATM straddle, short vega-matched 1/K^2 strip: isolates the gap between ATM implied vol (straddle ~ 0.8*sigma_ATM*S*sqrt(T)) and the variance-swap vol (VIX). VIX - sigma_ATM is positive, driven by skew and convexity; the trade is short that smile premium while flat to the vol level.
strategies.max_profit: About the strip's wing premium in excess of the straddle's theta, earned when moves stay moderate.
strategies.max_loss: Large moves: the strip's short wings lose quadratically (constant dollar gamma) while the straddle gains only linearly, so the position is short convexity in large moves.
strategies.breakevens: A realised path whose quadratic wing loss equals the straddle's linear gain plus the premium; numerical.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: 0 at spot (in BS, Vega = sigma*T*S^2*Gamma for every option, so vega-matched means dollar-gamma-matched at inception); increasingly negative away from spot as the straddle's gamma decays and the strip's stays constant
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive (the strip's wings are priced at higher IVs than ATM)

strategies.when_to_use: When VIX minus 30-day ATM IV (the smile premium) is at a high percentile (SKEW high, wings rich) and you want to be short the smile but neutral to the vol level: the wing-only expression of the skew/kurtosis premium.
strategies.risks: Crash convexity; many legs; the straddle drifts away from ATM as spot moves and turns directional.
strategies.margin_note: Short strip legs are naked under Reg-T; PM nets them against the long straddle (+6%/-8% SPX stress). SPX is cash-settled, European and Section 1256.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit: DVOL minus ATM mark_iv gives the same basis for BTC; BTC's smile premium is large because its smiles are very convex; inverse settlement.
strategies.metals_notes: GVZ minus GLD ATM IV; gold's smile premium is smaller.
variants: Long straddle vs short strangle (fewer legs)
Long straddle vs short 25d butterfly wings
strategies.claim: The 30-day SPX smile premium VIX - sigma_ATM(30d) exceeds the subsequently realised convexity premium RV_21d - sqrt(pi/2)*mean|r_daily|*sqrt(252) on average.

trial.statistic: Mean of [VIX_t - 100*sigma_ATM,t] - [RV_{t,t+21} - sqrt(pi/2)*mean|r|*sqrt(252)] (vol points). The second bracket is the excess of realised vol over its MAD-implied normal vol, i.e. the realised fat-tail contribution.
trial.procedure: Daily captures of SPX 30d ATM IV (surface_summary atm_iv, interpolated to 30 DTE) alongside VIX; non-overlapping 21d cycles; studentized block bootstrap. The realised-convexity series can be computed on history now to pre-register its distribution.
trial.data: Daily _SPX chain capture from 2026-10-14; CBOE VIX (archive); ^GSPC closes.
trial.pass: Mean > 0 with the 95% CI excluding zero over at least 36 cycles.
trial.controls: BS flat-smile control (premium zero by construction); SKEW stratification.

strategies.blocked_on: daily SPX chain capture: ~90 days for a first read of the basis series, ~36 monthly cycles (~3 years) for the test. The realised-convexity side can be computed on history now.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Add VIX minus surface_summary 30d ATM IV as a daily series next to harness_implied_move; add the realised-convexity statistic to harness_vrp_spx today.

strategies.name: Variance swap replication by 1/K^2 strip (log contract)

legs.strike_rule: every listed strike K < F0, weight 2*dK/(T*K^2)
every listed strike K > F0, weight 2*dK/(T*K^2)
static 2/(T*F0) forward units per unit variance notional; with the short strip this is a long log contract. Re-hedge daily by shorting 2/(T*S_t) units, so net delta is ~0 at inception

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: The long strip pays (2/T)[(S_T-F0)/F0 - ln(S_T/F0)], so short strip plus 2/(T*F0) long forwards pays the long log contract (2/T)ln(S_T/F0). Adding the daily -2/(T*S_t) hedge turns it into short realised variance: P&L = N_var*(K_var - RV^2), with K_var = (2e^{rT}/T)[int_0^{F0} P(K)/K^2 dK + int_{F0}^inf C(K)/K^2 dK]. That is the VIX^2 construction for SPX, which also subtracts (1/T)(F/K0 - 1)^2.
strategies.max_profit: N_var*K_var (if realised variance is zero).
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded: realised variance has no ceiling (one daily return x adds about x^2*252/n to annualised RV^2 over an n-day window).
strategies.breakevens: RV^2 = K_var (for SPX, K_var ~ (VIX/100)^2).

greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative, with constant dollar gamma (the log contract's Gamma = 2/(T*S^2), so S^2*Gamma = 2/T at every spot level)
greeks_at_inception.vega: negative and spread across all strikes: short the whole smile, not just ATM

strategies.when_to_use: The cleanest expression of the variance risk premium: the strike is VIX^2 by construction and the position is exposed to the whole smile. The long version (buy the strip) is the crash-convex hedge whose payoff is quadratic in moves.
strategies.risks: Truncation: listed strikes do not reach zero, so the replication under-weights the far put tail (the part that pays most in a crash); discretisation error; execution across 20-60 strikes; the payoff is convex in vol (doubling vol quadruples the variance loss).
strategies.margin_note: Every short option is margined; PM stresses the strip as one position (+6%/-8% for SPX), while Reg-T is punitive. SPX/XSP are cash-settled, European and Section 1256; the ES/MES hedge is SPAN-margined.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit's DVOL uses the same strip logic on BTC options, so a strip at the DVOL expiries replicates DVOL^2 as the strike. Inverse options pay in BTC, so convert strip prices to USD (price_btc x index) before applying the 1/K^2 identity. Hedge with the perp (funding is a carry term); realised variance uses 365 days; settlement at 08:00 UTC.
strategies.metals_notes: GVZ applies the VIX methodology to GLD options, so a GLD 1/K^2 strip replicates GVZ^2. GC options have sparser strikes (larger discretisation error), and American early exercise breaks strict replication; SPAN margin, Section 1256.
strategies.claim: VIX^2 exceeds the subsequently realised 21-trading-day S&P 500 variance in more than 75% of non-overlapping months since 1990.

trial.statistic: Win rate of 1{(VIX_t/100)^2 > RV_{t,t+21}}; secondary: mean ln(RV/VIX^2) and the dollar P&L of a short variance swap with vega notional 1.
trial.procedure: Monthly non-overlapping cycles since 1990-01, with VIX as the strike and ^GSPC closes for RV (SPY from 1993 as a check; price returns, no dividends); exact binomial CI plus a block bootstrap; walk-forward thirds. Measure the strip-vs-VIX^2 truncation error on the captured SPX chain.
trial.data: CBOE VIX (archive), ^GSPC/SPY closes. Model-free: VIX is the strip's fair strike. Today's SPX chain (29,918 contracts) for the discretisation check.
trial.pass: Lower 95% bound of the win rate > 0.75 and positive in all three thirds; truncation error < 5% of the strike on the captured chain (reported, not part of the pass).
trial.controls: ATM-straddle-only VRP (should be smaller: the smile adds premium); shuffled-returns placebo; dividend-adjusted SPY as a check on the ^GSPC price-return RV.

strategies.harness_suggestion: harness_vrp_spx (T-48) computes VIX^2 - RV; add the win-rate statistic and log form, plus a strip_from_chain function in mandel/options that sums 2*dK/(T*K^2)*mid over the captured SPX chain for comparison with VIX^2.

strategies.name: Vega-neutral gamma-positive straddle swap (long near / short far straddle)

legs.strike_rule: ATM (K); qty q = sqrt(T_near/T_far) zeroes net vega (0.5 is a placeholder; e.g. 14/75 DTE gives 0.43)
daily delta hedge to zero (qty starts at ~0)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At the near expiry: V = |S_T - K| - q*Straddle_far(S_T, T_far - T_near, sigma_far') + C0, with C0 = q*Straddle_far,0 - Straddle_near,0 (signed). Because the ATM straddle scales with sqrt(T), q*Straddle_far,0 ~ Straddle_near,0 in a flat term structure, so C0 ~ 0. Re-hedged P&L accrues as sum of 0.5*Gamma_net*(dS)^2 - Theta_net*dt with net vega ~0 at inception.
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded in a large move (near gamma dominates), less the far straddle's residual value.
strategies.max_loss: If spot does not move: q*Straddle_far(K, T_far - T_near, sigma_far') - C0 at the near expiry (the net theta paid). Larger if far IV rises after the near leg dies, because the position is then net short vega.
strategies.breakevens: Near-window realised variance must exceed near implied by enough to pay the net theta (roughly RV_near^2 > IV_near^2 plus the theta imbalance); solved numerically on the engine grid.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: positive: gamma scales with 1/sqrt(T), so near gamma / (q * far gamma) = T_far/T_near > 1
greeks_at_inception.vega: about 0 by construction; becomes short vega once the near leg expires

strategies.when_to_use: When near-dated realised vol is expected to exceed near implied (event clustering, VIX9D below realised, dated catalysts) without exposure to the level of implied vol: a pure realised-vs-implied gamma bet with the vega sold off.
strategies.risks: Vega neutrality is only instantaneous and drifts with time and spot; after the near expiry the book is a naked short far straddle; daily hedging costs.
strategies.margin_note: The short far straddle is naked under Reg-T; PM partly offsets it with the long near straddle (stress +6%/-8% for SPX/SPY). Index versions are cash-settled with Section 1256 treatment.
strategies.crypto_notes: Natural on Deribit: daily or weekly vs monthly straddles, with gamma hedged 24/7 through the perpetual (funding adds to theta). The inverse payoff makes USD gamma asymmetric; DVOL vs short-dated realised vol is the public signal.
strategies.metals_notes: GC weekly vs monthly options give the near/far pair; the short far leg is American; SPAN margin. GLD/SLV: same construction with equity options.
variants: Calendar straddle swap with both legs delta-hedged
Gamma-swap replication (1/K-weighted strip) long near vs short far
Vega-neutral strangle swap (OTM) for cheaper gamma
Three-expiry version neutral in both vega and theta
strategies.claim: Conditional on VIX9D closing below the trailing 10-day realised SPY volatility, the SPY variance realised over the next 9 calendar days exceeds VIX9D^2 on average.

trial.statistic: Mean of RV(next 9 calendar days, ~6-7 trading days, annualised) - (VIX9D/100)^2 over signal days.
trial.null: Conditional mean <= 0 (implied still exceeds realised even when it sits below trailing realised).
trial.procedure: Daily VIX9D from 2011-01-04 and SPY closes; non-overlapping 9-calendar-day windows (VIX9D is a 9-calendar-day measure, not 9 trading days); studentized block bootstrap; walk-forward. The trailing-RV windows 5/10/20 are declared and deflated. Secondary: the swap's gamma-scalp P&L simulated with BS (model-priced: VIX9D as near IV, VIX3M as far IV).
trial.data: CBOE VIX9D and VIX3M (archive), SPY closes.
trial.pass: Conditional mean > 0 with the 95% CI excluding zero; the model-priced swap Sharpe after a 0.5 vol-point round-trip cost is reported separately and is not part of the pass.

strategies.name: VIX call hedge (rolling long OTM VIX calls)

legs.strike_rule: K = F_fut + 5 to F_fut + 10 vol points (delta ~0.20-0.30 vs the VIX future)
legs.expiry_rule: 30-60 DTE VIX monthly, rolled 1-2 weeks before expiry

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(SOQ - K, 0) - C0, convex in VIX: a 10-point SOQ above K pays 10 x $100 = $1,000 per contract. Against an equity book the payoff approximates a short-equity hedge in large shocks.
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded in VIX (VIX closed at 82.69 in March 2020).
strategies.max_loss: C0 per cycle, bled every month the shock does not come.
strategies.breakevens: SOQ* = K + C0.

greeks_at_inception.delta: positive to the VIX future (negative to SPX)
greeks_at_inception.theta: negative and large (high vol-of-vol premium, plus roll-down drag in contango)

strategies.when_to_use: Tail hedge for an equity or short-vol book when VIX and VVIX are low (calls cheap in points) and the curve is in contango. The convex payoff avoids picking an SPX strike, and can be cheaper per unit of crash protection than SPX puts when skew is rich.
strategies.risks: Persistent negative carry (the future rolls down toward spot); the SOQ can be far from the prior close; the hedge is on the future, not spot, so in a slow grind lower the future lags spot VIX.
strategies.margin_note: Long premium only. VIX options are cash-settled, European, multiplier $100, AM-settled and Section 1256 60/40.
strategies.crypto_notes: No US-listed vol-index options for BTC; the analogue is a far-OTM BTC put on Deribit or IBIT, or a far-dated long BTC straddle.
strategies.metals_notes: No GVZ options; gold tail hedges use GC/GLD puts (or GLD calls for flight-to-safety convexity).
variants: Call spread hedge (long K1, short K2) to cut carry
1x2 call ratio (near zero cost, short the extreme tail)
VIX call calendar (long far, short near)

trial.statistic: 1 - MDD(hedged)/MDD(unhedged); secondary: Sharpe difference and hedge P&L per cycle.
trial.procedure: Monthly cycles from 2009-09 (VIX3M start). The call is priced with Black-76 on F_adj = sqrt((93*VIX3M^2 - 30*VIX^2)/63)*exp(-(VVIX/100)^2*T/2) with sigma = VVIX/100 (model-priced); payoff on spot VIX at expiry as the SOQ proxy. Block bootstrap of the drawdown ratio by resampling 12-month blocks; budget fixed ex ante.
trial.data: CBOE VIX, VIX3M and VVIX (archive), SPY closes. Model-priced: no VIX option or futures history.
trial.pass: Lower 95% bound of the drawdown reduction > 25%, with the Sharpe difference reported (not required to be positive).
trial.controls: SPX 10-delta put hedge with the same budget (model-priced at VIX x skew scale); cash-drag control at the same budget.

strategies.name: VIX call spread and call ratio (defined-cost vol hedge / vol-of-vol sale)

legs.strike_rule: K1 = F_fut + 3 to F_fut + 5 (delta ~0.35 vs the VIX future)
K2 = K1 + 10 to K1 + 15 (qty 2 for the 1x2 ratio variant)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: 1x1: min(max(SOQ - K1, 0), K2 - K1) - D0. 1x2: max(SOQ - K1, 0) - 2*max(SOQ - K2, 0) - D0 (D0 often near 0 or a credit): peaks at K2 with (K2 - K1) - D0, falls with slope -1 above K2, and turns negative above 2K2 - K1 - D0.
strategies.max_profit: 1x1: (K2 - K1) - D0 for SOQ >= K2. 1x2: (K2 - K1) - D0 at SOQ = K2.
strategies.max_loss: 1x1: D0. 1x2: unbounded above 2K2 - K1 - D0 (short the extreme tail); below K1 it is D0 (or nothing if D0 <= 0).
strategies.breakevens: 1x1: K1 + D0. 1x2: lower K1 + D0 (none if D0 <= 0) and upper 2K2 - K1 - D0.

greeks_at_inception.delta: 1x1 positive to the VIX future; 1x2 small, may be slightly negative
greeks_at_inception.gamma: positive near K1, negative near K2
greeks_at_inception.theta: 1x1 mildly negative; 1x2 near zero or positive
greeks_at_inception.vega: 1x1 small positive to VVIX; 1x2 short VVIX (sells the upper strike's convexity)

strategies.when_to_use: Hedge a moderate vol spike (VIX 25-40) at lower carry than outright calls. The 1x2 sells the far tail where VIX-option implied vol is richest, financing the hedge; use it when VVIX is high relative to the realised vol of VIX.
strategies.risks: 1x1: protection capped at K2 in a 2008/2020-type event. 1x2: the position turns short in exactly the catastrophic scenario; SOQ settlement risk; roll timing.
strategies.margin_note: 1x1 debit spread: no further margin. 1x2: the extra short call is naked under Cboe strategy-based rules (see the specification page's margin sections), and brokers often add house requirements. Cash-settled, Section 1256.
strategies.crypto_notes: Not directly available; the BTC analogue is a far-OTM put spread or put ratio on Deribit or IBIT.
strategies.metals_notes: Not directly available; use GLD/GC put or call spreads depending on the shock direction (gold rallied in early 2020, then fell in the liquidity squeeze).

Call-spread collar financed by a short VIX put
Diagonal call spread (long far K1, short near K2)

trial.statistic: Win rate of 1{VVIX_t > 100*sqrt(252)*sd(dlnVIX_{t..t+21})}; secondary: model-priced 1x2 P&L with Black-76 on F_adj and VVIX as IV.
trial.procedure: Daily VVIX from 2006-03-06 (not 2007) and VIX; non-overlapping 21d windows (~245); exact binomial CI plus block bootstrap; walk-forward halves. Spot VIX realises more vol than the futures VVIX refers to, so the test is biased against the claim (conservative).
trial.data: CBOE VVIX and VIX (archive); VIX3M for the forward proxy in the secondary.
trial.pass: Lower 95% bound of the win rate > 0.70; positive premium in both halves.
trial.controls: SPX VRP win rate (VIX^2 vs RV^2) for scale; shuffled-VVIX placebo.

strategies.name: VIX futures roll-down harvest via short VIX call spread

legs.strike_rule: K1 = ATM vs the VIX future of the same expiry (F_fut)
legs.expiry_rule: 30-45 DTE VIX monthly (Wednesday AM SOQ settlement)

legs.strike_rule: K2 = K1 + 5 to K1 + 10 vol points

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Credit C0 = C(K1) - C(K2). V = C0 - min(max(SOQ - K1, 0), K2 - K1): keep the full credit if the VIX SOQ settles below K1 (in contango the future rolls down toward spot), max loss if SOQ >= K2.
strategies.max_profit: C0 (SOQ <= K1).
strategies.breakevens: SOQ* = K1 + C0.
strategies.when_to_use: When the VIX term structure is in contango (VIX3M > VIX, front future > spot): absent a shock the future converges down to spot over the month. Sell the roll-down with a defined-risk call spread rather than naked.
strategies.risks: Vol spikes are fast and large (VIX can double in days); the credit is small relative to the width; VIX options settle on the Special Opening Quotation, which can diverge from the prior close; Wednesday AM expiry.
strategies.margin_note: Defined risk: margin = width - credit. VIX options are cash-settled, European, multiplier $100 and Section 1256. They price off the VIX future of the same expiry, not spot VIX, so ATM means the futures level.

strategies.name: VIX spike mean-reversion via long VIX put / put spread

legs.strike_rule: K2 = ATM vs the VIX future of that expiry (F_fut)
K1 = K2 - 5 to K2 - 8 (optional; makes the put spread)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Put spread: min(max(K2 - SOQ, 0), K2 - K1) - D0. Outright put: max(K2 - SOQ, 0) - D0. Profits when VIX falls back toward its long-run level after a spike in backwardation.

greeks_at_inception.delta: negative to the VIX future (positive to SPX)
greeks_at_inception.theta: negative, plus adverse roll: in backwardation the future sits below spot and rises toward spot if VIX stays elevated

strategies.when_to_use: After a VIX spike (VIX > 30 and VIX > VIX3M, i.e. backwardation), when the futures curve already prices part of the decline. Strike the put on the future (which sits below spot in backwardation), not on spot.
strategies.risks: Spikes cluster (Aug 2015, Feb 2018, Mar 2020, Aug 2024), and a second leg can send VIX higher; part of the expected decline is already priced; SOQ risk.
strategies.margin_note: Debit only. VIX options are cash-settled, European and Section 1256.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC analogue: after a DVOL spike, sell a BTC straddle or buy a BTC call spread. Deribit inverse, 24/7, settlement 08:00 UTC.
strategies.metals_notes: After a GVZ spike, short a GLD straddle or GC strangle; GC is American on futures with SPAN.

strategies.name: Vol-of-vol trade: short VIX strangle vs VVIX

legs.strike_rule: K2 = F_fut + 5 (OTM vs the VIX future)
K1 = F_fut - 3 (OTM; the VIX floor near 9-10 limits the downside)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Short VIX strangle: C0 - max(SOQ - K2, 0) - max(K1 - SOQ, 0). Sells vol-of-vol: it profits when VVIX-implied movement of the VIX future exceeds its realised movement to settlement. The reverse (long VIX straddle) is used when VVIX is low ahead of a catalyst.
strategies.max_profit: C0 for SOQ in [K1, K2].
strategies.max_loss: Upside unbounded (SOQ - K2 - C0); downside K1 - C0 in theory, about K1 - 9 - C0 in practice given the VIX floor.
strategies.breakevens: K1 - C0 and K2 + C0.

greeks_at_inception.delta: about 0 to the VIX future (asymmetric: the short put side has a floor)

strategies.when_to_use: Short when VVIX is in its top quartile relative to the realised vol of VIX and the curve is in contango; long a VIX straddle when VVIX < 85 and a dated macro catalyst is ahead.
strategies.risks: VIX has a log-normal-like upside and bounded downside, so the short call carries nearly all the risk (2018 and 2020 losses); VVIX itself spikes to 150-200 in crises; SOQ settlement.
strategies.margin_note: Naked VIX calls carry heavy margin; PM stresses use large VIX moves. Cash-settled, European, Section 1256.
strategies.crypto_notes: No DVOL options; BTC vol-of-vol is traded via straddle calendars or the DVOL-realised spread over short windows on Deribit.
strategies.metals_notes: Not available (no GVZ derivatives).
variants: Long VIX straddle when VVIX is low
Short VIX call + long VIX put (synthetic short future with skew)
VIX straddle calendar (long far, short near)
strategies.claim: Over non-overlapping months since 2006, VVIX exceeds the subsequently realised 21-trading-day volatility of daily log changes in spot VIX by more than 10 vol points on average.

trial.statistic: Mean of VVIX_t - 100*sqrt(252)*sd(dlnVIX_{t..t+21}); by VVIX quartile as a secondary; model-priced short-strangle P&L (Black-76 on F_adj with VVIX as IV) with crisis months tabulated.
trial.procedure: Daily VVIX from 2006-03-06 and VIX; non-overlapping 21d windows; studentized block bootstrap; quartile monotonicity test (harness_horizon_monotone pattern); deflated Sharpe on the model-priced secondary.
trial.data: CBOE VVIX, VIX and VIX3M (archive).
trial.pass: Lower 99% bound of the mean gap > 10; quartile means increasing (reported); model-priced Sharpe reported separately.
trial.controls: Shuffled-VVIX placebo; realised vol of the forward proxy F instead of spot VIX (lower variance, closer to what VVIX prices).

strategies.harness_suggestion: harness_vvix (T-243) implements the data part; add the strangle pricer so a pass is no longer reported as inconclusive.

strategies.name: VRP harvest: delta-hedged short ATM straddle

legs.strike_rule: daily delta hedge to zero (qty starts at ~0 and tracks -delta)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Unhedged: C0 - |S_T - K|, with C0 the straddle credit. Hedged: P&L ~ sum of 0.5*Gamma*S^2*(sigma_imp^2 - r_t^2/dt)*dt, which under constant dollar gamma is Vega/(2*sigma_imp)*(IV^2 - RV^2) (no extra T factor): short variance at strike IV^2 in the amount of dollar gamma, path-dependent because gamma concentrates near K.
strategies.max_profit: Unhedged: C0 at S_T = K. Hedged: approx. Vega*(IV - RV) for RV near IV, bounded by about C0 as RV goes to 0.
strategies.max_loss: Unhedged: unbounded above, K - C0 below. Hedged: unbounded in realised variance (a jump realises variance that cannot be hedged).
strategies.breakevens: Unhedged: K - C0 and K + C0 (OIC). Hedged: RV over the life approximately equal to IV at entry, with path dependence.
strategies.when_to_use: The default short-vol harvest: implied variance of equity indices exceeds subsequently realised variance on average (the variance risk premium). Size by IV minus a realised-vol forecast and avoid known events.
strategies.risks: Crash and jump risk; vol-of-vol; losses correlate with equity drawdowns; hedging costs; margin calls when VIX spikes. The premium is compensation for exactly these risks.
strategies.margin_note: Reg-T naked straddle: the greater of the two legs' naked requirements plus the other leg's premium. Portfolio margin (FINRA 4210(g)) stresses SPX/SPY at +6%/-8% and single stocks at +/-15%. SPX/XSP are cash-settled, European and Section 1256 60/40; SPY is American with assignment risk.
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit the straddle is priced and settled in BTC (inverse); hedge with the BTC perpetual using a premium-adjusted delta, and account for funding (often positive carry for a short-perp hedge in bull markets). DVOL is the 30-day implied index and realised vol uses 365 days. The BTC VRP is positive on average with fatter negative tails, and weekend realised vol counts because the market trades 24/7.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold VRP via GLD straddles (GVZ is the implied index) or GC options (American, SPAN, Section 1256, exercise into futures, so an assigned leg becomes a futures position to flatten). Silver via SLV/SI, whose implied vol runs well above gold's.
strategies.claim: Model-priced: a daily delta-hedged short 30-DTE SPY ATM straddle priced at ATM IV = 0.81 x VIX (the ATM-to-VIX ratio used by harness_short_straddle, to be recalibrated on the captured SPY surface) earns a positive mean P&L per monthly cycle after a 0.5 vol-point round-trip cost.

trial.statistic: Mean cycle P&L / straddle premium for the BS-priced, daily-rehedged short straddle.
trial.procedure: Monthly non-overlapping cycles from 1993-02 (SPY) with VIX-scaled IV and FRED DTB3 rates; hedge at daily closes; studentized block bootstrap; walk-forward thirds; deflated Sharpe over the IV scales {1.0, 0.9, 0.81} and hedge frequencies tried.
trial.data: CBOE VIX, SPY closes and FRED DTB3. Model-priced: the captured ATM IV/VIX ratio replaces the 0.81 scale as chain history accrues.
trial.pass: Mean > 0 with the 95% CI excluding zero at IV scale 0.81 and at the scale measured on the capture; deflated Sharpe p < 0.05; positive in all three thirds.
trial.controls: Unhedged short straddle; buy-and-hold SPY (harness_controls); shuffled-VIX placebo.

strategies.harness_suggestion: harness_short_straddle (T-57) already prices at VIX and at 0.81 x VIX; add the daily re-hedge path, costs, and the ATM/VIX ratio measured from surface_summary atm_iv vs VIX on capture days.

strategies.name: VXX / UVXY decay harvest with options (put spreads, call spreads, diagonals)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Put spread: min(max(K2 - S_T, 0), K2 - K1) - D0, with S_T the VXX price at expiry. VXX holds a constant-30-day VIX futures position rolled daily from month 1 into month 2; in contango the roll loses roughly (F2 - F1)/F1 per month, which drives the expected decline.
strategies.max_profit: (K2 - K1) - D0 for S_T <= K1.
strategies.max_loss: D0 (defined). Short-call variants are unbounded (VXX can triple in weeks).

greeks_at_inception.gamma: positive near K2 (net, long the ATM put)
greeks_at_inception.theta: negative on the debit, offset by the expected roll decay of the underlying

strategies.when_to_use: When the VIX curve is in steep contango (VIX3M/VIX > 1.1): the ETN bleeds roll yield, so long VXX put spreads or short VXX/UVXY call spreads harvest the decay with defined risk; SVXY (-0.5x) call spreads express the same view.
strategies.risks: Spikes: VXX rose +100-300% in weeks in Feb 2018 and Mar 2020, wiping out short calls; put spreads can lose the whole debit; UVXY is 1.5x leveraged and path-dependent; ETN issuer credit risk (Barclays); reverse splits; acceleration or delisting (XIV in 2018).
strategies.margin_note: Put spread: debit only. Short calls on VXX/UVXY: brokers often require very high margin (high-vol class). Options are American and physically settled in ETN/ETF shares, taxed as equity options (not Section 1256). SVXY and UVXY are ProShares Trust II commodity pools that issue Schedule K-1; VXX is an ETN (1099).
strategies.crypto_notes: No listed BTC vol ETN in the US; leveraged BTC ETFs with options (e.g. BITX) carry similar path-dependent volatility drag.
strategies.metals_notes: No gold-vol ETN; leveraged metals ETFs (UGL, AGQ, NUGT) have options and volatility drag, so the same long-put-spread logic applies with much smaller carry.
variants: VXX put diagonal (long far ATM put, short near OTM put)
Short VXX shares hedged with long VXX calls (synthetic put)
strategies.claim: Conditional on VIX3M/VIX > 1.10 at entry, the mean 21-trading-day log return of VXX is below -3%.

trial.statistic: Mean 21d VXX log return conditional on VIX3M/VIX > 1.10; secondary: model-priced put-spread P&L (BS on VXX with a VVIX-scaled IV proxy) until VXX chain captures exist.
trial.procedure: Daily VXX closes (current VXX from 2018-01; splice the matured 2009-2019 series only with a documented roll), VIX and VIX3M; non-overlapping 21d cycles; studentized block bootstrap; walk-forward threshold; deflated Sharpe. Replace the IV proxy with surface_summary VXX IVs after 60 captures.
trial.data: VXX/UVXY daily closes (NOT in the archive); SVXY closes ARE archived (from 2011-10: -1x until 2018-02-27, -0.5x after); VIX and VIX3M (archive); daily VXX chain capture (not in CHAIN_SYMBOLS).
trial.pass: Upper 95% bound of the conditional mean < -0.03; model-priced P&L reported separately.
trial.controls: Unconditional VXX drift (also expected negative); random-entry placebo; worst-month table; SVXY-based proxy run (sign-flipped, leverage-adjusted) as a cross-check.

strategies.blocked_on: VXX/UVXY daily close history (add to the closes fetch) and adding VXX/UVXY/SVXY to CHAIN_SYMBOLS, ~60 days of capture for real IVs. An SVXY-based proxy of the same contango claim is testable now from the archived SVXY closes.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Add VXX/UVXY/SVXY to CHAIN_SYMBOLS and VXX/UVXY to the daily closes fetch; then harness_vxx_decay in the harness_term_structure style, with an immediate SVXY-proxy run.

strategies.name: Albatross (long / short)

legs.strike_rule: K1, lowest strike (deep ITM call, e.g. -12%)
K4, far OTM (e.g. +12%), K4 - K3 = K2 - K1

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Long albatross: max(S_T-K1,0) - max(S_T-K2,0) - max(S_T-K3,0) + max(S_T-K4,0) - D (a condor with a very wide body). Short albatross: the credit mirror
strategies.max_profit: Long: (K2 - K1) - D for K2 <= S_T <= K3. Short: C_r for S_T <= K1 or S_T >= K4
strategies.max_loss: Long: D for S_T <= K1 or S_T >= K4. Short: (K2 - K1) - C_r inside the body
strategies.breakevens: Long: K1 + D and K4 - D. Short: K1 + C_r and K4 - C_r

greeks_at_inception.gamma: long albatross: short (-) but small; short albatross: long (+) small

strategies.when_to_use: A wide condor at the far tails. The long albatross, and its common iron form (short low-delta strangle plus farther wings), collects small credits at a high win rate; the short albatross buys the far tails as a credit-financed tail bet. It is a pure tail-frequency vs tail-price claim. Flat VIX cannot price the far wings: on 2026-10-14 the 47-DTE 5-delta SPY put traded at 24.1% IV, 1.93x the ATM IV (12.5%) and 1.6x VIX.
strategies.risks: Iron form: tiny credit relative to max loss; far-wing liquidity; tail events cluster. Long albatross bleeds when the range breaks.
strategies.margin_note: Defined risk: width minus credit; portfolio margin small for far-OTM shorts but spikes in stress.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit lists wide BTC strike ranges, so far-tail trading is common. DVOL discards options below 5% delta (Deribit methodology), so DVOL does not see far-tail richness.
strategies.metals_notes: GC far wings are thin, silver tails fat; SPAN; GLD/SLV: Reg T.
variants: Iron albatross (far-OTM put spread + call spread)
Long albatross as a cheap range bet
strategies.claim: A 45-DTE SPY short iron albatross (short 5-delta strangle, long wings at the next strikes 2% further out), entered at mid on captured chains and held to expiry, has positive mean P&L per unit max loss.

trial.statistic: mean P&L/max loss with studentized block-bootstrap CI; secondary: realised breach frequency vs mid-implied and the IV(5d put)/IV(ATM) ratio series
trial.procedure: Daily strike selection by delta; mid and bid/ask fills; settle on the expiry close
trial.data: options-chain-SPY-<date>, daily-history-SPY
trial.pass: lower CI > 0 at bid/ask fills with a >10% drawdown month in the sample
trial.controls: Verdict capped at 'inconclusive' until a stress month is captured.

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture: 250 entry days including a stress episode
strategies.harness_suggestion: Harness 'tail_wing_richness' using bs.implied_vol on captured mids.

strategies.name: Big Lizard

legs.strike_rule: ATM, K (with the put: a short straddle)
K_c2 > K with K_c2 - K <= C_r (credit covers the width)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: C_r - |S_T - K| + max(S_T - K_c2, 0)
strategies.max_profit: C_r, at S_T = K
strategies.max_loss: Downside: K - C_r at S_T = 0. Upside: max(0, (K_c2 - K) - C_r)
strategies.breakevens: K - C_r; no upside breakeven when C_r >= K_c2 - K

greeks_at_inception.delta: positive (the long call outweighs the short straddle's slight negative delta)
greeks_at_inception.theta: long (+), larger than the jade lizard

strategies.when_to_use: A short straddle with the upside capped by a long call: maximal theta with one-sided (downside) risk. Needs the realised down-move to stay below C_r. CORRECTION on the proxy: flat VIX overprices the ATM straddle (+21%), which favours the seller, and overprices the +2% call (which hurts the seller). Net, on 2026-10-14, the flat-VIX credit was 19.08 vs 18.02 at mid (+6%), so a flat-VIX test is mildly optimistic, not conservative. Use the smile-scaled model.
strategies.risks: Full downside risk of a short ATM put; the condition fails at low IV; early assignment on the ATM American short legs.
strategies.margin_note: Naked-put margin plus the covered call side; portfolio margin lower.
strategies.crypto_notes: ATM BTC straddle credits are large, so the condition is often met. The inverse short put's coin loss is unbounded as S_T -> 0. European.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: SPAN; GLD/SLV: Reg T.
variants: Reverse big lizard (short straddle + long put: no downside risk)
Wider long call (more credit, some upside risk)
strategies.claim: A 30-DTE SPY big lizard (short ATM straddle, long +2% call), sold at the smile-scaled VIX model price and held to expiry, has positive mean P&L per unit downside max loss over 1993-2026 (MODEL-PRICED proxy).

trial.statistic: mean P&L/max loss with block-bootstrap CI; condition frequency (C_r >= 0.02 S) by VIX bucket; paired difference vs the short straddle
trial.procedure: Price the straddle at s*VIX (s grid) and the +2% call at VIX x r(1.02); settle at S_{t+21}.
trial.data: daily-history-SPY, cboe-VIX-history, fred-DTB3, options-surface-2026-10-14
trial.pass: lower CI > 0 under the smile-scaled model and at s = 0.90
trial.controls: Width fixed at 2%; proxy cap; costs haircut.

strategies.blocked_on: Nothing blocks the model-priced proxy. Market-priced confirmation needs 250+ captured SPY chain days.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Harness 'big_lizard' sharing the short-straddle engine in overlay_backtest plus one smile-priced call leg.

strategies.name: Broken-Wing (Skip-Strike) Butterfly

legs.strike_rule: K1 < K2, far wing with K2 - K1 > K3 - K2 (e.g. K2 - K1 = 2(K3 - K2); 'skip one strike' is meaningless on SPY's $1 grid)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(K3-S_T,0) - 2 max(K2-S_T,0) + max(K1-S_T,0) + C_r (C_r < 0 if debit)
strategies.max_profit: (K3 - K2) + C_r, at S_T = K2
strategies.max_loss: Downside: (K2 - K1) - (K3 - K2) - C_r, for S_T <= K1. Upside: 0 if C_r >= 0, else |C_r| for S_T >= K3
strategies.breakevens: Lower: K2 - (K3 - K2) - C_r. Upper: K3 + C_r only when entered for a debit (C_r < 0); none when C_r >= 0

greeks_at_inception.delta: small positive for the put BWB (+0.003 on the 2026-10-14 SPY 30/20-delta example), negative for a call BWB

strategies.when_to_use: Harvest the put skew. The doubled body sits on a steeper part of the smile than the near wing, so the 1x2 is sold rich and part of the credit buys the far wing, leaving little or no risk on one side. Profit zone: anything but a fall through the lower breakeven. Not testable on the VIX proxy: the edge is the slope of the smile, which flat VIX lacks. On 2026-10-14 (47 DTE, SPY 762/2x746/714) the structure cost a 0.08 debit at mid, i.e. about zero, not a reliable credit.
strategies.risks: Crash risk on the skipped side, concentrated where the skew premium is paid; early assignment on the two American short puts; wing liquidity; adjustment costs when the body is tested.
strategies.margin_note: Defined risk: margin = max loss = (K2 - K1) - (K3 - K2) - C_r.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC skew changes sign with regime (IBIT showed put skew, 25-delta RR -1.9, on 2026-10-14), so the BWB side must follow the live smile. Coarse strikes make the broken wing a large width step. European and inverse.
strategies.metals_notes: Where the call wing is rich (SLV 25-delta RR +2.0 on 2026-10-14) the call BWB is the natural form; GLD was flat. GC/SI: SPAN; GLD/SLV: Reg T.
variants: Call BWB (broken upper wing) for upside skew
Credit BWB (no risk on one side) vs debit BWB
Rolled out when the body is breached
strategies.claim: A 30-45 DTE SPY put BWB (K3 30-delta, K2 20-delta, K2 - K1 = 2(K3 - K2)) entered at mid on captured chains and held to expiry has positive mean P&L per unit max loss.

trial.statistic: mean P&L/max loss over daily entries, studentized block-bootstrap CI (overlapping trades, block >= holding period)
trial.procedure: Select strikes by delta from options-chain-SPY-<date>; fill at mid and, separately, at bid/ask; settle at intrinsic on the expiry close from daily-history-SPY.
trial.data: options-chain-SPY-<date> (daily capture from 2026-10-14), daily-history-SPY
trial.pass: lower CI > 0 at bid/ask fills, with at least one >10% SPY drawdown month in the sample
trial.controls: Delta rule fixed. Report credit frequency as descriptive only. Verdict capped at 'inconclusive' without a stress episode.

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture: 250 entry days (each resolving 30-45 days later) including a stress month
strategies.harness_suggestion: Harness 'bwb_skew' reading options-chain-SPY-* bundles, with strike selection via the chain's delta field (fallback bs.strike_for_delta); per-day strikes stored for audit.

strategies.name: Call Ratio Backspread
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: -max(S_T-K1,0) + 2 max(S_T-K2,0) + C_r (C_r = net credit; negative if debit)
strategies.max_profit: Unlimited on the upside (slope +1 above K2); C_r for S_T <= K1 if a credit
strategies.max_loss: (K2 - K1) - C_r, at S_T = K2 (OIC: max loss at the upper strike)
strategies.breakevens: Upper: K2 + (K2 - K1) - C_r. Lower: K1 + C_r, only when entered for a CREDIT (C_r > 0); with a debit there is no lower breakeven and S_T <= K1 loses the debit

greeks_at_inception.delta: strike-dependent. On 2026-10-14 (65 DTE, short ATM, long 2x +5%) it was -0.17, turning positive as S rises; it is positive only when the long strikes are close to K1
greeks_at_inception.gamma: long (+) (small when K2 is far OTM)
greeks_at_inception.vega: long (+) (OIC: an IV increase is positive)

strategies.when_to_use: Long-vol, upside-convex structure financed by the near call: profits on a large rally and, if a credit, a little on a collapse; loses on a moderate rise to K2. In equities it buys the cheap call wing (SPY 105% call at 10.1% vs ATM 12.3%). CORRECTION: with these strike rules SPY backspreads open for a large CREDIT (2026-10-14: 12.43 credit for short ATM / long 2x +5%, 9.09 for long 2x 25-delta), not a debit. Needs chain data, since flat VIX misprices the two strikes in opposite directions.
strategies.risks: Loss zone exactly at a moderate rally; theta while waiting; OTM call spreads; early assignment on the short American call before ex-dividend.
strategies.margin_note: Spread margin on the 1:1 part (max loss of the vertical); the extra long call is paid for.
strategies.crypto_notes: Popular ahead of expected BTC rallies; in call-skew regimes the OTM calls are expensive and the structure becomes a debit; inverse calls cap coin payoff at 1 coin per contract.
strategies.metals_notes: Where the call wing is rich (SLV) the backspread is costlier; GC: SPAN credit for the vertical; GLD/SLV: Reg T.
variants: Short leg ITM for more credit
strategies.claim: A 60-DTE SPY 1:2 call backspread (short ATM, long 2x 25-delta calls), entered at mid on captured chains and held to expiry, has negative mean P&L per unit max loss: realised upside rarely reaches the upper breakeven.

trial.statistic: mean P&L/max loss with studentized block-bootstrap CI
trial.procedure: Delta-selected strikes from daily chains; mid and bid/ask fills; settle at expiry
trial.data: options-chain-SPY-<date>, daily-history-SPY
trial.pass: upper CI < 0 at mid fills
trial.controls: Rule fixed; credit/debit frequency reported descriptively; IBIT and GLD runs reported as cross-asset contrasts.

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture: 250 entry days resolving ~60 days later
strategies.harness_suggestion: Harness 'backspread' reading options-chain-* with the shared delta selector.

strategies.name: Delta-Hedged Risk Reversal (skew trade)

legs.strike_rule: dynamic: shares = -(delta_call - delta_put_short) to zero the net delta, rebalanced daily (side follows the residual)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Unhedged legs: max(S_T - K_c,0) - max(K_p - S_T,0) + C_r (C_r = put premium - call premium). Hedged P&L ~ sum 0.5 S^2 [Gamma_c (r^2 - sigma_c^2 dt) - Gamma_p (r^2 - sigma_p^2 dt)] plus vanna/volga terms from smile moves
strategies.max_profit: Hedged: bounded by the skew premium collected plus favourable smile moves; unhedged: unlimited on the upside
strategies.max_loss: Large in a crash with a skew blow-out: the short put gains gamma loss and vega loss together; unhedged K_p - C_r at S_T = 0
strategies.breakevens: Hedged: realised downside variance (weighted by put gamma) ~ the put's implied variance minus the call side's net; no closed form

greeks_at_inception.gamma: ~0 to slightly short (equal-delta wings have similar gamma)
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive when put IV > call IV (the skew is collected)
greeks_at_inception.vega: ~0 net in level; short skew (short vanna: loses when spot falls and put vols rise)

strategies.when_to_use: Isolates the skew premium: sells the rich equity put wing and buys the cheap call wing with the delta hedged away. Wikipedia defines the 25-delta risk reversal R25 = sigma_call,25 - sigma_put,25. On 2026-10-14 R25 was SPY -4.1, IBIT -1.9, GLD +0.2 and SLV +2.0 vol points, so the sign of the trade depends on the asset. The CBOE SKEW index measures the same tail richness for SPX. Flat VIX has no skew, so this is untestable on VIX proxies.
strategies.risks: Crash plus skew blow-out (the trade is short crash convexity); hedge costs; early assignment on the short American put.
strategies.margin_note: Naked short put margin (15% broad index / 20% stock rate) plus the long call debit plus the hedge.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC R25 changes sign with regime; trade the rich side shown by the live smile. Deribit inverse: hedge with the Net Transaction Delta (BS delta - mark) in futures or perps; 24/7.
strategies.metals_notes: For GLD/SLV/GC the rich wing is often the call (SLV R25 +2.0), so the mirror (short call, long put) is the skew sale; SPAN for GC/SI.
variants: Mirror: short call / long put where the call wing is rich
strategies.claim: A 30-45 DTE SPY 25-delta risk reversal (short put, long call), entered at captured mids and delta-hedged daily to expiry, has positive mean P&L per unit put vega.

trial.statistic: mean hedged P&L/vega with studentized block-bootstrap CI
trial.procedure: Strikes from the captured chain's delta field; daily delta hedge at SPY closes using bs.greeks at the entry IVs; settle at expiry
trial.data: options-chain-SPY-<date>, daily-history-SPY, cboe-SKEW-history (descriptive)
trial.pass: lower CI > 0 with a >10% drawdown month in the sample
trial.controls: Without a crash in-sample the result is biased positive, so the verdict is capped at inconclusive; report against the skew_tail harness (SKEW vs realised tails).

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture: 250 entry days including a stress episode
strategies.harness_suggestion: Harness 'rr_skew_premium' combining the delta selector with the 'gamma_scalp_vrp' hedging loop.

strategies.name: Dispersion Trade (short index vol, long constituent vol)

legs.strike_rule: ATM calls on each constituent i, qty w_i scaled so total constituent vega = index vega (vega-neutral) or theta-neutral
ATM puts on each constituent i, same w_i
delta hedges on the index and each constituent, rebalanced daily (side follows the residual delta)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Delta-hedged approximately: sum_i w_i Vega_i (sigma_i,R - sigma_i,I) - Vega_idx (sigma_idx,R - sigma_idx,I), i.e. short implied correlation: gains when realised correlation < implied
strategies.max_profit: Bounded by the index premium collected plus constituent gains; largest when stocks move a lot independently (low realised correlation)
strategies.max_loss: Large: when correlation spikes toward 1 in a crash, index vol rises as much as single-stock vol and the short index straddle loses without bound on the upside
strategies.breakevens: Realised average correlation ~ implied correlation (the COR1M-style level) over the holding period

greeks_at_inception.gamma: long single-stock gamma, short index gamma (net sign depends on weights)
greeks_at_inception.theta: near 0 for theta-neutral weighting; slightly positive for vega-neutral (index vol richer)

strategies.when_to_use: Harvest the correlation risk premium: index options embed implied correlation above typical realised correlation, because index puts are bid as portfolio hedges. Variance form: sell an index variance swap and buy constituent variance swaps (Wikipedia, Correlation trading). Cboe publishes implied correlation indices (COR1M etc., methodology fetched); the archive holds cboe-COR1M-history from 2006-01-03.
strategies.risks: Correlation spikes in crashes (the trade is short crash); many legs, high costs and wide single-stock spreads; earnings events in constituents; early exercise on American single-stock legs.
strategies.margin_note: Short index straddle margined as naked (15% broad index); long single-stock options are debits; portfolio margin essential in practice.
strategies.crypto_notes: A crypto analogue is short BTC/ETH-basket vol vs long alt vol, but Deribit lists options only on a few coins, so there is no index-option leg; not practical.
strategies.metals_notes: Not applicable as a dispersion trade; the closest analogue is a gold vs silver vol spread (GVZ vs SLV IV).
variants: Variance dispersion (index var swap vs single-name var swaps)
Reverse dispersion as a crash hedge
strategies.claim: Over 2006-2026, 1-month implied correlation (COR1M) exceeds the subsequently realised average pairwise correlation of the index constituents on average, so a vega-neutral short-index/long-constituent straddle book has positive mean P&L.

trial.statistic: mean of (COR1M_t - realised average correlation over t+1..t+21) with studentized block-bootstrap CI; realised correlation from constituent daily returns via sigma_idx^2 = sum w_i^2 s_i^2 + sum_{i!=j} w_i w_j s_i s_j rho
trial.procedure: Monthly non-overlapping; COR1M from the archive; realised correlation from constituent or sector-ETF closes
trial.data: cboe-COR1M-history (archive, 2006 on), daily closes of the top-50 constituents or the 11 sector SPDRs (NOT yet captured)
trial.pass: lower CI > 0
trial.controls: Sector ETFs give an upward-biased realised correlation (diversified within sector), which is conservative; COR1M uses the top-50 constituents.

strategies.blocked_on: constituent or sector-ETF daily closes are not in the free data set yet (the daily-history fetcher already handles ETFs, so adding XLK..XLU bundles unblocks the proxy); a market-priced test also needs single-stock chain captures
strategies.harness_suggestion: Harness 'implied_vs_realised_correlation' in mandel/experiments/volatility.py with bundles ['cboe-COR1M-history','daily-history-XL*'].

strategies.name: Front Ratio Spread (short ratio call / put spread)

legs.strike_rule: K1, ATM or slightly OTM (put version: K2' near the money)
K2 > K1, OTM, 1:2 (put version: 2 short puts at K1' < K2')

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Call version: max(S_T-K1,0) - 2 max(S_T-K2,0) + C_r. Put version: max(K2'-S_T,0) - 2 max(K1'-S_T,0) + C_r
strategies.max_profit: (K2 - K1) + C_r at S_T = K2 (OIC). Put version: (K2' - K1') + C_r at S_T = K1'
strategies.max_loss: Call version: unlimited above the upper breakeven. Put version: K1' - (K2' - K1') - C_r at S_T = 0
strategies.breakevens: Call: upper K2 + (K2 - K1) + C_r; lower K1 - C_r only if a debit (C_r < 0). Put: lower K1' - (K2' - K1') - C_r; upper K2' + C_r only if a debit

greeks_at_inception.delta: strike-dependent (2026-10-14: call 1:2 long ATM / short 2x +5% = +0.31; put long 40d / short 2x 20d = ~0)
greeks_at_inception.theta: usually long (+); NEGATIVE when the long leg is ATM and the shorts are far OTM (2026-10-14 call example), turning positive with time
greeks_at_inception.vega: short (-) (OIC: an IV increase is negative)

strategies.when_to_use: Sells vol and skew in the direction of the extra short. The put front-ratio (long ~40-delta put, short 2x ~20-delta puts) is the classic index skew sale: it profits on a drift down to K1' or a flat market, with naked tail risk below. Tastylive frames it as turning a debit spread into a credit. CORRECTION: on 2026-10-14 the SPY 47-DTE put 1:2 (773 / 2x746) cost a 0.38 DEBIT, so 'credit on >= 70% of days' is not a safe assumption.
strategies.risks: Naked tail on the ratio side; margin on one uncovered short; early assignment on American shorts.
strategies.margin_note: Spread margin on the 1:1 plus naked margin (15% / 20% rate) on the extra short; portfolio margin lower.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC call front-ratios sell call skew when it is rich. CORRECTION: an inverse short call's coin loss saturates at 1 coin per contract, while the put version's coin loss is unbounded as S_T -> 0; size by coin on the put side. Deribit portfolio margin.
strategies.metals_notes: Where the call wing is rich (SLV) the call front-ratio is the skew sale; SPAN; GLD/SLV: Reg T.
variants: Front ratio with a far wing bought (becomes a broken-wing butterfly)
strategies.claim: A 45-DTE SPY put front-ratio (long 40-delta put, short two 20-delta puts), entered at mid on captured chains and held to expiry, has positive mean P&L per unit of naked-leg margin.

trial.statistic: mean P&L/margin with studentized block-bootstrap CI
trial.procedure: Delta-selected strikes; mid and bid/ask fills; settle at expiry
trial.data: options-chain-SPY-<date>, daily-history-SPY
trial.pass: lower CI > 0 at bid/ask with a stress month in the sample
trial.controls: Rule fixed; tail absent from short samples, so the verdict is capped at inconclusive.

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture: 250 entry days including a stress episode
strategies.harness_suggestion: Harness 'front_ratio_skew' sharing the delta selector.

strategies.name: Gamma Scalping a Long Straddle (delta-neutral)

legs.strike_rule: dynamic: shares = -(delta_call + delta_put) x multiplier, rebalanced daily or at a delta band so net delta = 0 (the side flips to long when the straddle delta is negative)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Path-dependent: P&L ~ sum over rebalances of 0.5 Gamma_i S_i^2 (r_i^2 - sigma_I^2 dt) minus hedge costs. Only for constant dollar gamma (the 1/K^2 log-contract strip) is it exactly a variance swap: payoff = sigma_R^2 - sigma_I^2 (Demeterfi et al. 1999, EQ 7)
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded in principle (large realised variance); in practice limited as gamma decays when spot leaves K
strategies.max_loss: About D (premium) plus hedge costs and discrete-hedging error, reached when spot stays pinned at K
strategies.breakevens: Realised vol over the holding period ~ the straddle's implied (ATM) vol at entry; exact only for constant dollar gamma, otherwise path-weighted by Gamma S^2

greeks_at_inception.delta: 0 by construction, re-zeroed at each rebalance
greeks_at_inception.theta: short (-): the daily rent equals the implied-variance expectation of the gamma P&L

strategies.when_to_use: The cleanest expression of 'realised will exceed implied': direction is hedged away, leaving the gamma-weighted integral of realised minus implied variance. CORRECTION: the straddle's break-even vol is ATM IV, not VIX. VIX is the variance-swap (strip) rate and exceeded SPY ATM IV by about 1.24x on 2026-10-14. Comparing realised vol to VIX tests the strip, which vrp_spx already supports (T-48: VIX 21.0 vs realised 18.6); comparing it to s*VIX tests the straddle, and 0.81 x 21.0 = 17.0 < 18.6, so the sign at the calibrated scale is genuinely open. The proxy cannot capture intraday rebalancing, American exercise and dividends, or costs beyond an assumed per-share fee.
strategies.risks: Hedge slippage and costs eat the gamma; gamma collapses if spot trends away from K (re-strike); theta dominates in quiet regimes; jumps favour the long side but discrete hedges miss part of them.
strategies.margin_note: Debit for the straddle; stock hedge under Reg T (50%) or portfolio-margin netting; ES/MES futures hedge under SPAN is capital-light for SPX/XSP.
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit the hedge is the perpetual (with funding) or a dated future, 24/7. CORRECTION: public/ticker 'greeks.delta' is the Black-Scholes delta. For a coin-denominated (inverse) book, Deribit's docs use the Net Transaction Delta = BS delta - mark price (in coin) as the hedge quantity. Realised variance includes weekends. DVOL vs realised (vrp_btc, 2,031 daily rows since 2021-03-24) gives the crypto variance premium.
strategies.metals_notes: Hedge GC/SI options with the underlying future (SPAN offsets); GLD/SLV with the ETF under Reg T; GC has a daily maintenance break, so overnight gaps exist.
variants: Short gamma scalping (short straddle hedged daily)
Hedging at implied vs realised/forecast vol (changes the P&L distribution; the expectation differs only at second order)
Variance-swap replication with a 1/K^2 strip (see entry)
strategies.claim: A 30-DTE ATM SPY straddle bought at BS(0.90*VIX) and delta-hedged daily at that entry vol has negative mean P&L per unit vega over 1993-2026 (MODEL-PRICED proxy).

trial.statistic: mean hedged P&L/vega over non-overlapping cycles, studentized block-bootstrap CI; run at s in {0.81, 0.90, 1.00}; secondary: correlation of P&L with (RV_21 - (s*VIX)^2)
trial.procedure: Each cycle: price the straddle at s*VIX_t; each day compute BS delta (bs.greeks) at the entry vol, hedge at the SPY close, charge 1 bp per share traded; sum to expiry
trial.data: daily-history-SPY, cboe-VIX-history, fred-DTB3
trial.pass: upper CI < 0 at s = 0.90; report the s at which the sign flips
trial.controls: Daily (not intraday) hedging; cost declared; VIX is SPX; q = 0 with unadjusted closes; report the variance-term share of P&L vs hedging error; BTZ 1990-2007 as an external anchor (monthly %^2 units).

strategies.blocked_on: Nothing blocks the model-priced proxy. Market-priced confirmation needs 250+ captured SPY chain days.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Add a 'hedged_straddle' branch to mandel/experiments/volatility.py that walks daily closes with bs.greeks; register harness 'gamma_scalp_vrp'. The BTC sibling reuses the vrp_btc bundles (deribit-dvol-BTC-history, daily-history-BTC-USD) with DVOL as the entry vol.

strategies.name: Guts (long / short)

legs.strike_rule: ITM put, K_p > F (so K_p > K_c)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(S_T-K_c,0) + max(K_p-S_T,0) - D = (K_p - K_c) + max(S_T-K_p,0) + max(K_c-S_T,0) - D: an OTM strangle at the swapped strikes plus a bond paying K_p - K_c
strategies.max_profit: Long: unlimited on the upside; K_p - D at S_T = 0. Short guts: C_r - (K_p - K_c), for K_c <= S_T <= K_p
strategies.max_loss: Long: D - (K_p - K_c), for K_c <= S_T <= K_p. Short guts: unlimited on the upside
strategies.breakevens: K_c - [D - (K_p - K_c)] and K_p + [D - (K_p - K_c)] (short guts: replace D with C_r)
strategies.when_to_use: Payoff-identical to the strangle at the swapped strikes plus a bond (Wikipedia: buy or sell a pair of ITM put and call). Used when ITM quotes are tighter or for venue-specific margin reasons. The expectancy claim is the strangle's; the guts-specific claim is execution cost.
strategies.risks: Large debit tied up in intrinsic; ITM American legs can be exercised early (puts when rates are high, calls before ex-dividend); ITM spreads are usually wider.
strategies.margin_note: Long: debit. Short guts: margined as a naked strangle including intrinsic.
strategies.crypto_notes: European Deribit options remove early-exercise risk from ITM legs; ITM premiums in coin are large, so guts tie up more coin than a strangle.
strategies.metals_notes: American ITM futures options (calls and puts) carry early-exercise value when rates are positive; SPAN; GLD/SLV: Reg T.
variants: Guts vs strangle parity arbitrage when mids diverge beyond the spread
strategies.claim: On captured SPX chains, buying the guts at the ask costs more (after subtracting PV(K_p - K_c)) than buying the swapped-strike strangle at the ask on at least 80% of capture days: the strangle beats the guts on execution.

trial.statistic: fraction of days with guts_ask - PV(K_p - K_c) > strangle_ask; secondary: mid-parity residual
trial.procedure: Matched strikes (K_c = 25-delta put strike, K_p = 25-delta call strike) from options-chain-SPX-<date>; PV at fred-DTB3
trial.data: options-chain-SPX-<date>, options-chain-SPY-<date>, fred-DTB3
trial.pass: fraction >= 0.8 with binomial lower bound > 0.5 on SPX
trial.controls: SPX European (clean); SPY reported separately since the American early-exercise premium can legitimately break parity; same timestamp for all legs.

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture, 30 days
strategies.harness_suggestion: Include in 'condor_parity_check' as a second execution test.

strategies.name: Iron Butterfly (short, credit)

legs.strike_rule: K3 (upper wing), K3 - K2 = K2 - K1

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: C_r - |S_T - K2| + max(K1 - S_T, 0) + max(S_T - K3, 0)
strategies.max_profit: C_r (net credit), at S_T = K2
strategies.max_loss: (K3 - K2) - C_r, for S_T <= K1 or S_T >= K3 (OIC: difference between the body and either wing, less premium received)
strategies.breakevens: K2 - C_r and K2 + C_r
strategies.when_to_use: A short straddle with bought wings: the same VRP harvest with defined risk. It is the OIC 'short iron butterfly' and is payoff-equivalent to a long call (or put) butterfly plus cash. It profits iff |S_T - K2| < C_r. CORRECTION on the proxy (the original text contradicted itself): flat VIX overprices the short ATM body (+21%) and underprices the bought put wing, and both errors favour the seller. On 2026-10-14 the +/-5% iron fly credit was 23.16 at flat VIX, 20.26 at 0.81*VIX and 19.38 at mid, so a flat-VIX test is OPTIMISTIC for the seller. Use the smile-scaled model.
strategies.risks: Narrow max-profit point; wings cut the credit substantially when near; four legs of spreads; early assignment on the short American body.
strategies.margin_note: Defined risk: margin = max loss = wing width - credit.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit portfolio margin recognises the wings. CORRECTION: the coin P&L equals the USD P&L divided by S_T, so a put-side max loss (S_T low) costs MORE coin than the same USD loss on the call side. All legs are European with 08:00 UTC expiry.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI iron flies get SPAN spread credit; GLD/SLV are defined-risk under Reg T.
strategies.claim: A 30-DTE SPY iron butterfly with +/-5% wings, sold at the smile-scaled VIX model price and held to expiry, has positive mean P&L per unit max loss over 1993-2026 (MODEL-PRICED proxy).

trial.statistic: mean P&L/max loss with studentized block-bootstrap CI; secondary: max drawdown and Sharpe vs the naked short straddle (paired, compare_strategies)
trial.procedure: Price four legs with the smile-scaled model; terminal payoff; paired with the short-straddle series on the same dates.
trial.data: daily-history-SPY, cboe-VIX-history, fred-DTB3, options-surface-2026-10-14
trial.pass: lower CI > 0 under the smile-scaled model and at ATM scale s = 0.90
trial.controls: Wing width fixed. Flat VIX is reported as the optimistic bound. The same cost haircut applies. Proxy cap until the smile is refit.

strategies.blocked_on: Nothing blocks the model-priced proxy. Market-priced confirmation needs 250+ captured SPY chain days.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Harness 'iron_fly_vs_straddle' using build_position (mandel/options/strategies.py) for legs and compare_strategies for the paired test.

strategies.name: Iron Condor (short, credit)

legs.strike_rule: K3, OTM call (16-20 delta), K3 > K2
K4 (upper wing), K4 - K3 = K2 - K1

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: C_r - max(K2 - S_T,0) + max(K1 - S_T,0) - max(S_T - K3,0) + max(S_T - K4,0)
strategies.max_profit: C_r (net credit), for K2 <= S_T <= K3
strategies.max_loss: (K2 - K1) - C_r = (K4 - K3) - C_r for equal widths (OIC: difference between the call or put strikes, less premium received)
strategies.breakevens: K2 - C_r and K3 + C_r
strategies.when_to_use: A short strangle with bought wings: defined-risk VRP harvest (OIC 'Short Condor (Iron Condor)'). Profits when the terminal price stays inside the short strikes; the credit/width ratio is roughly the market's implied breach probability. CORRECTION: flat VIX is NOT conservative here. On 2026-10-14 (47 DTE, SPY 717/740/818/840) the condor credit was 5.51 at flat VIX against 3.10 at mid (+78%), because flat VIX hugely overprices the OTM call spread and the put-wing errors partly cancel. A flat-VIX condor test is strongly biased toward the seller; use the smile-scaled model.
strategies.risks: Loss/credit ratio typically 3-10x, so a few breaches erase many winners; whipsaw can test both sides; vega losses during spikes even inside the strikes; early assignment on American short legs near ex-dividend.
strategies.margin_note: Defined risk: margin = max loss of one side (equal widths); portfolio margin similar or lower.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit iron condors: coarse strikes mean large widths; portfolio margin recognises the wings. CORRECTION: coin P&L = USD P&L / S_T, so the put-side max loss costs more coin than the call-side one. Realised BTC vol has exceeded DVOL in trend regimes, though DVOL exceeded realised on average (T-49).
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI condors: SPAN. Silver breaches more often than gold at the same delta (fatter tails; realised vol 1.83x). GLD/SLV: Reg T defined risk.
variants: 16-delta condor managed at 50% credit or 21 DTE
strategies.claim: A 45-DTE SPY iron condor with short strikes at +/-5% and wings at +/-8%, sold at the smile-scaled VIX model price and held to expiry, has positive mean P&L per unit max loss over 1993-2026 (MODEL-PRICED proxy).

trial.statistic: mean P&L/max loss over non-overlapping 31-trading-day cycles, studentized block-bootstrap CI; secondary: realised breach frequency vs the model-implied breach probability
trial.procedure: Price four legs with the smile-scaled model at T = 45/365; settle at S_{t+31}. Sensitivity: term-adjust VIX toward VIX3M (VIX3M history starts 2009-09-18 in the archive, so this covers 2009-2026 only).
trial.data: daily-history-SPY, cboe-VIX-history, cboe-VIX3M-history, fred-DTB3, options-surface-2026-10-14
trial.pass: lower CI > 0 under the smile-scaled model; flat-VIX result reported as the optimistic bound
trial.controls: Widths fixed. The 30-day VIX vs 45-day tenor mismatch is flagged. Proxy cap until 60 capture days refit the smile (the 2026-10-14 calibration is a low-vol, high-SKEW day).

strategies.blocked_on: Nothing blocks the model-priced proxy. Market-priced confirmation needs 250+ captured SPY chain days.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Harness 'iron_condor_breach' using build_position plus smile_ratio; implied breach probability via norm_cdf in mandel/validation/backtest_eval.py.

strategies.name: Ladder / Christmas Tree (long or short, call or put)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Long call ladder: max(S_T-K1,0) - max(S_T-K2,0) - max(S_T-K3,0) - D (D < 0 if credit). Short ladder: the negative
strategies.max_profit: Long: (K2 - K1) - D for K2 <= S_T <= K3. Short: unlimited above the upper breakeven
strategies.max_loss: Long: unlimited above the upper breakeven; D below K1 if a debit. Short: (K2 - K1) - C_r for K2 <= S_T <= K3
strategies.breakevens: Long: lower K1 + D (only if a debit); upper K2 + K3 - K1 - D

greeks_at_inception.delta: long call ladder: small, positive if K1 is ATM, turning negative above K2
greeks_at_inception.gamma: long ladder: short (-); short ladder: long (+)
greeks_at_inception.vega: long ladder: short (-); short ladder: long (+)

strategies.when_to_use: Wikipedia: a long ladder suits traders expecting low volatility, a short ladder those expecting high volatility. It is a bull call spread plus a further short call: it sells the upper wing, so it is a skew trade in metals and crypto where the call wing is rich, and cheap financing in equities where it is not (SPY 105% call at 0.66x VIX on 2026-10-14). The put ladder (long K3 put, short K2 and K1 puts) sells the rich equity put wing.
strategies.risks: Naked tail on the extra short; early assignment on American shorts; loss zone above K3 (call) or below K1 (put).
strategies.margin_note: Spread margin on the vertical plus naked margin on the extra short.
strategies.crypto_notes: Call ladders sell BTC call skew in rally regimes; an inverse short call's coin loss is capped at 1 coin per contract, but a put ladder's coin loss is unbounded as S_T -> 0.
strategies.metals_notes: SLV call ladders sell the rich call wing (25-delta RR +2.0 on 2026-10-14); SPAN for GC/SI; Reg T for GLD/SLV.
variants: Long put ladder (sells the equity put wing)
Short call or put ladder (long vol, credit)
Ladder with an added far wing (becomes a condor)
strategies.claim: A 45-DTE SPY long put ladder (long 40-delta put, short 25-delta and 15-delta puts), entered at mid on captured chains and held to expiry, has positive mean P&L per unit naked-leg margin.

trial.statistic: mean P&L/margin with studentized block-bootstrap CI
trial.procedure: Delta-selected strikes; mid and bid/ask; settle at expiry
trial.data: options-chain-SPY-<date>, daily-history-SPY
trial.pass: lower CI > 0 at bid/ask with a stress month in the sample
trial.controls: Rule fixed; verdict capped at inconclusive without a stress episode.

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture: 250 entry days including a stress episode
strategies.harness_suggestion: Harness 'ladder_skew' sharing the delta selector with 'front_ratio_skew'.

strategies.name: Long Butterfly (call or put)

legs.strike_rule: K2 = body, usually ATM; K2 - K1 = K3 - K2

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(S_T-K1,0) - 2 max(S_T-K2,0) + max(S_T-K3,0) - D (the same with puts at the same strikes, by put-call parity)
strategies.max_profit: (K2 - K1) - D, at S_T = K2 (OIC: the difference between the lower and middle strike, less the premium paid)
strategies.max_loss: D (net debit), for S_T <= K1 or S_T >= K3
strategies.breakevens: K1 + D and K3 - D

greeks_at_inception.gamma: short (-) near the body; turns long (+) when spot sits near a wing
greeks_at_inception.theta: long (+) with the body ATM, negative when the body is away from the money (OIC)
greeks_at_inception.vega: short (-) with the body ATM (OIC: a rise in IV is slightly negative)

strategies.when_to_use: Bet that the underlying finishes near K2, with risk bounded by a small debit: a short-vol, short-gamma view. Its value approximates the risk-neutral density at K2 (Breeden-Litzenberger), so it is a smile object. CORRECTION on the proxy: BS(VIX) UNDERprices the ATM fly, because VIX overstates ATM vol and spreads the density too wide. On 2026-10-14 the +/-5% call fly was 15.71 at flat VIX, 18.62 at 0.81*VIX and 19.66 at market mid, so a flat-VIX test is optimistic for the buyer. Excess kurtosis means MORE mass near the centre and in the tails, not less, so the original 'pins less often' reasoning was inverted.
strategies.risks: Narrow profit tent; four contracts across three strikes; max profit needs a pin at K2; early assignment on the American short body; wing liquidity.
strategies.margin_note: Debit paid; the embedded verticals are spread-margined, so the requirement is the debit.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit's coarse strike grid constrains symmetric flies; all legs are European, so there is no early assignment on the body; combo orders exist. Coin payoff = USD payoff / S_T, so a USD-symmetric fly is asymmetric in coin.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI flies: the American short body can be assigned into futures before expiry; SPAN recognises the spread. GLD/SLV: Reg T spread margin.
variants: Put butterfly (same payoff; sometimes cheaper at mid due to quote asymmetry)
Directional butterfly (body at a target price)
Butterfly ladder across several bodies (a density bet)
strategies.claim: A 30-DTE SPY ATM call butterfly with +/-5% wings, bought at the smile-scaled VIX model price and held to expiry, has positive mean P&L per unit debit over 1993-2026: realised 30-day returns land near the money more often than the model's risk-neutral density implies (MODEL-PRICED proxy).

trial.statistic: mean P&L/debit with studentized block-bootstrap CI; secondary: realised frequency of |S_{t+21}/S_t - 1| < 2.5% vs the model-implied probability
trial.procedure: Price three legs with the smile-scaled model (and the ATM-scale grid s in {0.81, 0.90, 1.00} with flat wings as a sensitivity); terminal payoff from daily-history-SPY.
trial.data: daily-history-SPY, cboe-VIX-history, fred-DTB3, options-surface-2026-10-14 (smile ratios)
trial.pass: lower CI > 0 under the smile-scaled model and at s = 0.90
trial.controls: Wing width fixed at 5%. Flat VIX is reported only as the optimistic-for-buyer bound. Proxy cap until 60 capture days refit the smile.

strategies.blocked_on: Nothing blocks the model-priced proxy. Market-priced confirmation needs 250+ captured SPY chain days.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Harness 'butterfly_density': build legs with mandel/options/strategies.build_position from the strategies.json template and value at intrinsic with payoff.Position; emits long and short verdicts.

strategies.name: Long Condor (all-call or all-put, debit)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(S_T-K1,0) - max(S_T-K2,0) - max(S_T-K3,0) + max(S_T-K4,0) - D
strategies.max_profit: (K2 - K1) - D, for K2 <= S_T <= K3
strategies.max_loss: D (net debit), for S_T <= K1 or S_T >= K4
strategies.breakevens: K1 + D and K4 - D

greeks_at_inception.delta: ~0 when the body straddles the forward

strategies.when_to_use: A range bet with defined risk. By put-call parity it equals the iron condor at the same strikes plus a bond paying the width: D_condor = PV(K2 - K1) - C_iron. The practical differences are debit vs credit, a single option type, and ITM legs. Its expectancy claim is the iron condor's; what is specific to it is execution cost. Useful when one side of the chain is more liquid.
strategies.risks: Four contracts; debit at risk if the range breaks; ITM American short legs can be assigned early (the iron form uses OTM shorts and avoids this); wider ITM quotes.
strategies.margin_note: Debit; spread margin nets to the debit.

greeks_at_inception.delta: ~0 but slightly positive: with K = S, delta = e^{-qT}(2N(d1) - 1) > 0 when r - q + sigma^2/2 > 0; still slightly positive at K = F (d1 = sigma*sqrt(T)/2 > 0); exactly zero only at K = F*exp(sigma^2 T/2)
greeks_at_inception.vega: long (+): the largest vega per contract of any two-leg structure (OTM strangles carry more vega per dollar of premium)

strategies.when_to_use: Expect realised volatility over the holding period to exceed the straddle's implied vol, or expect an event (earnings, FOMC, CPI, protocol upgrade) to move the underlying more than the market prices. Held to expiry it pays iff |S_T - K| > D, and D ~ 0.8*sigma_ATM*S*sqrt(T), so the hurdle move is set by ATM implied vol. MODEL-PRICED PROXY: VIX is a strike-integrated 30-day variance-swap rate and sits ABOVE SPY ATM IV in normal skew. On the 2026-10-14 SPY capture (VIX 15.27, SKEW 154.7) the 30-DTE ATM IV was 12.3% (ratio 0.81); BS(VIX) priced the straddle at 27.27 against a 22.60 mid (+21%), while BS(0.81*VIX) gave 22.13. A flat-VIX test therefore overprices the straddle and biases it toward finding a loss. Daily SPY closes and VIX history can test 30-DTE ATM straddles held to expiry across an ATM-scale grid. They cannot test fills, intraday exits, other tenors or any off-ATM strike.
strategies.risks: Theta bleed if nothing happens; post-event IV crush often exceeds the realised move; two bid-ask spreads; early assignment is the counterparty's risk (the long holder decides exercise), but SPY calls are worth exercising early before ex-dividend dates, so the long holder must manage that; mismatch between the 30-day VIX horizon and weekly structures.
strategies.margin_note: Full debit paid, no margin. SPX/XSP: cash-settled European, Section 1256 60/40. SPY: American, physical delivery, equity-option tax treatment.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit BTC/ETH options are European and inverse: premium and P&L are in coin, and 1 contract = 1 BTC or 1 ETH. They expire at 08:00 UTC and trade 24/7, so weekend realised vol counts and there are no dividends. Use the matching-expiry future (not spot) as the forward, so basis enters the ATM strike. A straddle's coin payoff is |S_T - K|/S_T, so it pays more coin on a crash than on an equal-size rally. DVOL is the crypto analogue of VIX: a 30-day variance-swap-style index interpolated between the two bracketing expiries, discarding ITM options and options below 5% delta (Deribit DVOL methodology). The archive holds 2,031 daily DVOL rows since 2021-03-24 (deribit-dvol-BTC-history), not ~1000. Linear USDC-settled options also exist.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI options are American options on futures that exercise into the futures contract. They are SPAN-margined and taxed under Section 1256: 60/40 treatment and year-end mark-to-market (26 USC 1256, fetched). GLD/SLV options are American equity options on grantor trusts, with equity-style margin and no 1256 treatment; the trust shares themselves are taxed as collectibles. CME pages returned 403 in this run, so the GC/SI contract specifics are prior knowledge, not a fetched page.

strategies.when_to_use: Same realised-vs-implied logic as the straddle, but with a wider dead zone and cheaper premium: it needs a bigger move and loses less when wrong. The OTM legs carry smile vols. On 2026-10-14 (30 DTE) the 95% put traded at 17.2% IV and the 105% call at 10.1%, against VIX 15.27. BS(VIX) underpriced the put (1.65 vs 2.73 mid) and overpriced the call fivefold (2.47 vs 0.49), so the flat-VIX strangle was overpriced overall (4.11 vs 3.22). A flat-VIX test is biased TOWARD finding that buyers lose. Use the smile-scaled VIX model: leg IV = VIX x r(m), with r fitted on captured SPY surfaces (2026-10-14: 90% put 1.51, 95% put 1.12, 97% put 0.98, ATM 0.81, 103% call 0.69, 105% call 0.66). It is single-day calibrated and refit as captures accumulate.

strategies.when_to_use: Harvest the variance risk premium. Bollerslev-Tauchen-Zhou (2009, Table 1, 1990-2007) report mean implied variance (VIX^2, in monthly percent-squared) of 33.23 against realised variance of 14.93: a premium of 18.30 percent-squared per month. These are variances, not vols. Best when implied is high relative to recent realised and no scheduled event sits inside the tenor. MODEL-PRICED PROXY: BS at VIX overstates the ATM straddle credit (by 21% on the 2026-10-14 capture), so a flat-VIX test is optimistic for the seller; use the ATM-scale grid. The proxy cannot reproduce the tail of the P&L distribution (few crash cycles), margin calls and forced liquidations, or skew.
strategies.risks: Unbounded loss; gap risk; margin expansion in a vol spike forces liquidation at the worst time; negatively skewed returns make the plain Sharpe misleading (use PSR/DSR with skew and kurtosis); early assignment on American legs (SPY calls before ex-dividend dates; deep ITM puts).
strategies.margin_note: Reg T straddle (CBOE Margin Manual): the greater of the two naked requirements plus the premium of the other side. The naked requirement is premium + 15% of underlying (broad-based index and broad-index ETFs such as SPX, SPY, QQQ, IWM) or 20% (single stocks and other ETFs, including GLD, SLV, IBIT), less the OTM amount. The floor is premium + 10% of underlying for calls or 10% of strike for puts. Portfolio margin is lower. Futures options: SPAN. Deribit: coin margin.
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit the coin P&L of a short straddle is C_r - |S_T - K|/S_T. On a crash the short put loses coin without bound as S_T -> 0, since (K - S_T)/S_T -> inf; its USD loss is capped at K, as on any put. On a rally the short call's coin loss (S_T - K)/S_T is capped at 1 coin per contract, but its USD loss is unbounded. For a coin-margined book the put side is therefore the dangerous side. The margin formula (IM about max(0.15 - OTM/S, 0.10) + mark, MM 0.075 + mark) is from prior knowledge: the Deribit KB is JS-rendered and was not fetched. 24/7 trading means no closed-market gaps, but adjustments must use the 24/7 futures or perpetual. DVOL against realised BTC vol gives the crypto VRP directly (vrp_btc, T-49: DVOL 62.9 vs realised 54.9).
strategies.metals_notes: Short GC/SI straddles are SPAN-margined against the futures and taxed under Section 1256. On 2026-10-14 the 25-delta risk reversals were GLD +0.2 and SLV +2.0 vol points (call wing at or above the put wing), so the call side carries relatively more tail than in equities (SPY -4.1). SLV realised vol is 1.83x GLD's (2006-2026 daily closes). GLD/SLV route: Reg T at the 20% rate, no 1256.
