strategies.name: Short Strangle

legs.strike_rule: OTM, K_p < F (16-30 delta), K_p < K_c

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: C_r - max(S_T - K_c, 0) - max(K_p - S_T, 0)
strategies.max_profit: C_r (net credit), for K_p <= S_T <= K_c
strategies.max_loss: Unlimited on the upside; K_p - C_r on the downside (S_T = 0)
strategies.breakevens: K_p - C_r and K_c + C_r
strategies.when_to_use: The workhorse premium-selling structure: it collects the VRP plus the put-wing skew premium, with a wide profit zone. It profits iff the terminal price stays inside the strikes widened by the credit. CORRECTION: flat VIX is NOT conservative for the seller. It underprices the short put (+5% OTM: 1.65 vs 2.73 mid on 2026-10-14) but overprices the short call about fivefold (2.47 vs 0.49), so the flat-VIX credit (4.11) exceeded the market credit (3.22) by 28%, and a positive flat-VIX result is not robust to skew. Use the smile-scaled VIX model. The proxy cannot quantify the tail-loss distribution (few crash cycles) or margin-driven forced exits.
strategies.risks: Unbounded tail on the call side and a large one on the put side; a vol spike raises margin; losses are correlated across underlyings in a crash; pin and assignment risk on American legs.
strategies.margin_note: Reg T (CBOE Margin Manual): the greater of the two naked requirements plus the other side's premium, at 15% for broad-index products (SPX, SPY) and 20% for stocks and other ETFs, less OTM, with a 10% floor. Portfolio margin is typically much lower. SPAN for futures options; coin margin on Deribit.
strategies.crypto_notes: CORRECTION: in coin terms the PUT side is the dangerous side of a short inverse strangle. The coin loss (K_p - S_T)/S_T is unbounded as S_T -> 0, while the short call's coin loss (S_T - K_c)/S_T saturates at 1 coin per contract; in USD the call side is unbounded as for any short call. DVOL minus realised vol is the crypto VRP: positive on average (T-49) with violent inversions (e.g. March 2020 pre-dates DVOL; Nov 2022 is in-sample). 24/7 trading means no closed-market gap protection.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: SPAN and Section 1256. SLV realised vol is 1.83x GLD's (2006-2026), and both gap on CPI/FOMC. GLD/SLV: Reg T at the 20% rate, no 1256.
variants: 16-delta strangle managed at 50% of credit or 21 DTE
strategies.claim: A 30-DTE SPY short strangle at +/-5% strikes, priced with the smile-scaled VIX model, has a higher Sharpe ratio than the ATM short straddle priced on the same model and the same entry dates, 1993-2026 (MODEL-PRICED proxy).

strategies.name: Short Vol with Wings (tail-protected short straddle/strangle)

legs.strike_rule: ATM or 20-30 delta call, K3 >= K2
far OTM put K1 (~5 delta or -10%); qty 1 per short, or 2 for a long-tail profile
legs.expiry_rule: same, or a longer expiry (diagonal protection)

legs.strike_rule: far OTM call K4 (~5 delta or +10%)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: C_r - max(K2-S_T,0) - max(S_T-K3,0) + n_w[max(K1-S_T,0) + max(S_T-K4,0)], n_w = wings per short (1 or 2)
strategies.max_profit: C_r (net of wing cost), for K2 <= S_T <= K3 (with 2:1 wings, unbounded beyond the outer breakevens)
strategies.max_loss: 1:1 wings: max(K2 - K1, K4 - K3) - C_r beyond a wing. 2:1 wings: the same amount, reached exactly at K1 (or K4), after which P&L recovers
strategies.breakevens: Inner: K2 - C_r and K3 + C_r. With 2:1 wings also outer breakevens at K1 - (K2 - K1) + C_r and K4 + (K4 - K3) - C_r

greeks_at_inception.gamma: short (-) near the money, long (+) in the far tails
greeks_at_inception.vega: short ATM vega, long wing vega (exposed to skew changes)

strategies.when_to_use: The institutional form of premium selling: harvest the VRP at the centre and own the tails so a crash does not end the program. The question is whether the wing cost (where skew premium is richest) consumes the VRP. Proxy: flat VIX overstates the net credit. On 2026-10-14 the 30-DTE ATM straddle with +/-10% wings was 26.94 at flat VIX vs 21.49 at mid (+25%), driven mostly by ATM overpricing; the -10% put traded at 23% IV (1.5x VIX). A flat-VIX result is an upper bound; the smile-scaled model is the central proxy.
strategies.risks: Wing-cost drag; the wings help only beyond K1/K4, so the drawdown between K2 and K1 is real; wing vega can blow out the marks before expiry; margin still spikes on the short centre.
strategies.margin_note: Defined risk: width minus credit; portfolio margin recognises the wings; SPAN for futures options.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit far-OTM wings are relatively liquid. DVOL excludes options below 5% delta, so wing richness is invisible in DVOL. For coin-margined books the PUT wing matters most, since the short put's coin loss is unbounded as S_T -> 0.
strategies.metals_notes: Buy the wing the smile makes cheap; the call wing is rich in SLV, GLD is flat. SPAN; GLD/SLV: Reg T.
variants: Wings in a longer expiry (diagonal tail hedge)
Centre managed at 50% with wings held to expiry

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: 2 max(S_T-K,0) + max(K-S_T,0) - D

strategies.max_loss: D, at S_T = K
strategies.breakevens: K - D and K + D/2
strategies.when_to_use: A straddle with a bullish tilt (Wikipedia: two calls and one put at the same strike). Same proxy caveat as the strip: flat VIX overprices the ATM legs, so use the ATM-scale grid.
strategies.risks: Three premiums of theta; directional.
strategies.margin_note: Debit only.
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit each inverse call pays (S_T - K)/S_T coin, capped at 1 coin, so the strap's coin upside is concave and bounded; USDC linear options give the linear 2x slope.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: SPAN; GLD/SLV: Reg T.
variants: Strap into earnings or a halving

strategies.name: Strip
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(S_T-K,0) + 2 max(K-S_T,0) - D
strategies.max_profit: Unlimited on the upside; 2K - D on the downside
strategies.max_loss: D (net debit), at S_T = K
strategies.breakevens: K - D/2 and K + D
strategies.when_to_use: A straddle with a bearish tilt: pays double on a down move; needs a move of D/2 down or D up. CORRECTION: flat VIX is NOT unbiased at the money. On 2026-10-14 the strip was 39.44 at flat VIX, 31.73 at 0.81*VIX and 32.94 at mid. Use the ATM-scale grid. The ATM put/call IV difference is small (12.3% vs 12.3%).
strategies.risks: Three premiums of theta; directional exposure, so not a pure vol bet.
strategies.margin_note: Debit only.
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit the two inverse puts pay (K - S_T)/S_T coin each, which grows without bound as S_T falls; this is a natural crash hedge for coin-denominated books. European.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: SPAN; GLD/SLV: Reg T.

strategies.name: Unbalanced (Skewed) Iron Condor

legs.strike_rule: K1 (lower wing); put-spread width W_p = K2 - K1; qty n_p (e.g. 2)
K3 > K2, OTM call; qty n_c
K4, call-spread width W_c = K4 - K3 (W_c != W_p or n_c != n_p)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: C_r - n_p[max(K2-S_T,0) - max(K1-S_T,0)] - n_c[max(S_T-K3,0) - max(S_T-K4,0)]
strategies.max_profit: C_r, for K2 <= S_T <= K3
strategies.max_loss: max(n_p W_p, n_c W_c) - C_r on the heavier side; the lighter side's loss is max(0, n W - C_r)
strategies.breakevens: K2 - C_r/n_p and K3 + C_r/n_c (each valid when C_r < n W on that side)

greeks_at_inception.delta: non-zero by design: positive when the put side is heavier (more put spreads or wider)

strategies.when_to_use: An iron condor with a skew or directional lean: weight the put side to collect skew premium while keeping the call side light (or the reverse where call skew is rich), or narrow one side until the credit covers it. On 2026-10-14 (47 DTE, SPY) the 16-delta put mid was 4.13 vs 2.45 for the 16-delta call: put share 63%. The asymmetry is a smile decision, so VIX proxies cannot test it.
strategies.risks: Concentrated loss on the heavy side; delta exposure; the usual condor tail and margin issues.
strategies.margin_note: Margin = the heavier side's max loss.
strategies.crypto_notes: Weight the side the live smile makes rich (IBIT showed put skew on 2026-10-14). Coin losses are largest on the put side (coin P&L = USD P&L / S_T).
strategies.metals_notes: A heavier call side suits SLV-type call skew; GLD was flat; SPAN; GLD/SLV: Reg T.
variants: One side narrowed to zero risk (lizard-like)

strategies.name: Variance Swap Replication (long / short variance via 1/K^2 strip)

legs.strike_rule: strip of every OTM put K < F, each weighted (2/T) dK/K^2 (per unit variance notional)
legs.expiry_rule: same expiry; 30 days for the VIX analogue

legs.strike_rule: strip of every OTM call K >= F, each weighted (2/T) dK/K^2
dynamic: hold (2/T)(1/S_t - 1/S*) units, rebalanced daily (net short above S*, long below); S* = F at inception

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: N_var (sigma_R^2 - K_var), with K_var = fair variance strike; for 30-day SPX, K_var ~ (VIX/100)^2 (Demeterfi et al. EQ 7 / Wikipedia: rebalanced 1/S_t hedge plus a short log contract)
strategies.max_profit: Long variance: unbounded (sigma_R^2 large). Short variance: N_var K_var at sigma_R = 0
strategies.max_loss: Long variance: N_var K_var at sigma_R = 0. Short variance: unbounded (listed variance swaps usually carry a 2.5x vol cap)
strategies.breakevens: sigma_R = sqrt(K_var) (~VIX/100 for 30-day SPX)

greeks_at_inception.gamma: long (+): constant cash gamma (Gamma S^2 independent of S inside the strike range)
greeks_at_inception.vega: long (+): constant variance vega, unlike a single straddle

strategies.when_to_use: The pure realised-vs-implied variance trade: unlike the straddle, its exposure does not drift as spot moves. Short variance is the canonical VRP harvest, and its pricing input is the VIX itself (VIX is the 30-day SPX strip), so the proxy is not a BS assumption. The remaining basis is SPX strip vs SPY close-to-close variance, truncated and discrete strikes, and no caps. Retail cannot trade OTC variance swaps; SPX strips or VIX futures are the listed routes.
strategies.risks: Short variance has extreme left-tail losses (variance is quadratic in the move: 2008, 2020); strip truncation in crashes; hedge costs; OTC counterparty risk.
strategies.margin_note: OTC ISDA for swaps; a listed strip is margined leg by leg (debit for the long strip); the stock hedge uses Reg T or portfolio margin.
strategies.crypto_notes: DVOL^2 is the BTC 30-day strip rate, but it discards options below 5% delta, so it understates true variance-swap fair value. The vrp_btc harness (T-49) compares DVOL with realised vol. Deribit lists no variance swaps; replicate with the option strip plus the perpetual or future (24/7, funding).
strategies.metals_notes: The CBOE gold vol index (cboe-GVZ-history in the archive) is the GLD strip rate; the vrp_gold harness exists. GC options strips are possible but wing liquidity is thin.
variants: Long variance as a crash hedge
Vol swap (pays sigma_R - K_vol; needs a convexity adjustment)
Corridor variance (only accrues inside a range)

strategies.when_to_use: Convex hedge for a short-vol book or an equity portfolio: pays when VIX spikes. VIX options price off the VIX future for their expiry, which sits above spot VIX in contango, so spot VIX is the wrong underlying. The claim is about whether the hedge's cost (vol-of-vol premium plus contango) is repaid by spikes.
strategies.risks: Persistent bleed (contango and vol-of-vol premium); the spike may revert before expiry; cash-settled European, with the SOQ settlement gap.
strategies.margin_note: Debit only; cash-settled European; broad-based volatility index options are 1256 contracts.

strategies.metals_notes: No liquid listed options on GVZ were verified; for metals use GLD/SLV or GC option structures instead.
